documents.title: What really moves your Red Sea freight rate?
documents.description: A Red Sea freight rate moves when capacity, demand, empty boxes or the routing changes. Compare two quotes only when the scope matches.
documents.lead: A Red Sea freight rate moves when capacity, demand, empty boxes or the routing changes. Compare two quotes only when the scope matches.

body.text: What the number on a quote actually is

richText.text: The number on a quote is ocean freight for one container, from one Chinese port to one Red Sea port, on one sailing. It is not the cost of getting the goods into a warehouse in Riyadh, Cairo or Amman. Local charges at origin, destination charges, duty, tax, insurance and the truck after the port sit outside it.

Two numbers can be compared only when those boundaries match, and when the container type and the sailing window match too. A port-to-port 40HQ rate and an all-in rate for a 20GP are answers to different questions, even when both say Jeddah.

body.text: Capacity, and why this lane is tight

richText.text: Space on a ship is the first force. Carriers decide how many vessels to put on the China to Red Sea run, which Chinese ports those vessels call, and how much of each voyage they will still sell on the spot market. A blank sailing, a skipped port call, or a block of space held for contract customers all shrink what is left to quote this week. Shanghai having space does not mean Ningbo has space.

The Red Sea itself has narrowed the options. Since late 2023 many services have sailed around the Cape of Good Hope instead of through the Suez Canal. The voyage takes longer, so the same ship makes fewer trips in a year. In 2026 the Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed, and cargo that used to enter Saudi Arabia through the Gulf now comes in through Jeddah. More volume through one gateway means fuller ships and a congested berth. Underwriters treat the Red Sea up to Jeddah as a war-risk area, and that risk is priced on top of the freight.
None of this tells you next week's rate. It tells you why a quote can move even when your cargo has not changed.

Demand is the second force, and it follows a calendar you can plan around. Chinese factories push cargo out in the weeks before Chinese New Year, then go quiet, then refill the ships after the holiday. Ramadan and the Eid holidays slow customs desks and trucking in Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Jordan, so a container can arrive on the day the schedule promised and still wait. The run-up to year-end in the Gulf does the same at the other end of the year.

A busy week is a reason to book earlier and to ask whether the sailing you want still has space. It is not a formula that adds a fixed percentage to last month's price. A quiet week is a better moment to ask again. It is not a promise that the market will be cheaper.

The third force is the empty container. A 40HQ rate assumes a 40-foot high cube is sitting at the loading port. When a port runs short, the carrier has less to sell, or prices the scarce box higher. Nansha can have equipment when Shekou does not, in the same week, for the same destination. That is one reason the country pages show a separate median for each Chinese origin instead of one national price.

If the factory is inland, the nearest port that has both a box and a sailing often beats a slightly cheaper ocean rate from a port that needs a long truck haul. Tell us the factory city when you enquire, not only the port you guessed.

The fourth force is the routing. A direct sailing is the short version of the trip. From Shanghai or Shenzhen to Jeddah, direct services take about 17 to 18 days, and a sailing that connects through another hub can stretch the same move toward 31 days. Sokhna is about 20 to 23 days direct from South China, and can run to 32 to 35 days from North China when there is a connection. Aqaba direct is about 20 to 28 days, and a connection adds 3 to 7. Djibouti direct is about 19 to 24 days, or 25 to 30 with a call via Singapore or Colombo. These are port-to-port ranges, not a promise for a named vessel.

Port Sudan is the exception. Direct sailings from China are limited, and a lot of cargo connects through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti. Miss that connection and the box can wait a week or more. The connection decides the transit time, so we do not publish one for Port Sudan. Ask for the routing on every Sudan quote.

A cheaper rate with a connection is a different product, not a discount on the same one. You trade money for days, and for one more port where the connection can fail. Free time at destination is part of that product. One quote may include 14 days, another 21, and the longer free time is often already in the price. Read that line before you decide the freight number is low.

body.text: Charges that move on their own

richText.text: Carriers adjust other lines on the invoice on their own timetable. A fuel or bunker adjustment follows oil. A war-risk or contingency charge follows the security picture on the Red Sea. A peak-season surcharge appears when ships are full. A general rate increase is a carrier's announced step-up for a given month, and it does not always stick at the announced level. At the far end, a drop-off or congestion charge can be billed at the destination port.

Two quotes a hundred dollars apart on ocean freight can swap places once those lines are written out. Ask for the quote split into ocean freight, origin charges, anything billed at destination, and what is excluded. The medians on the rates page and the country pages are ocean freight only. They show where the market is. They are not the amount you will pay, and they are not a booking.

Most of what we publish is the spot market: a price for a near sailing, valid for days rather than for a year. A contract rate can sit far from that median and still be real for the shipper who signed it. Comparing a contract offer with the median on this site is comparing two different deals. The median describes the spot market. The contract describes what you already locked.

Validity is easy to mix up in the other direction too. The rates table shows a reading dated today, displayed as valid for seven days, because that is how we present the quotes we have collected. A carrier's own quote can expire sooner, on that vessel's cut-off. The date on our page is the date of the reading. The date on the quote is the date you can still book. Do not treat them as the same date.

body.text: How a pile of quotes becomes one median

richText.text: The index is the median of 40HQ market quotes collected from every China origin over the last 28 days, one figure per destination port. A price more than 50 percent away from the median is dropped, so one wild quote does not drag the line. The sample count is printed next to the figure. A median built on two quotes will jump when the next quote arrives. A median built on twenty will not. Week on week compares today's 28-day reading with the same reading a week earlier.

Gaps stay empty. We do not fill a missing week with an estimate, and we do not publish a median when there is no quote. The chart and the table are a reading of the market we see. Space and the final price are confirmed on WeChat or WhatsApp.

body.text: Five checks before you pick a quote

richText.text: Same origin port, or a clear reason the two ports differ.
Same destination, same container.
Same scope: ocean freight against ocean freight, not against an all-in number.
The dates the price is valid, and the sailing it sits on.
The routing and the free days.

If a quote sits far under the recent median, ask what is missing before you call it a bargain. A short free time, a connection, or a charge that appears only at destination explains a lot of those gaps.

documents.title: 哪些因素真正影响红海运价？
documents.description: 红海运价随运力、货量、空箱和航线变化。两份报价只有口径一致时才能放在一起比。
documents.lead: 红海运价随运力、货量、空箱和航线变化。两份报价只有口径一致时才能放在一起比。

body.text: 报价上的数字到底是什么

richText.text: 报价上的数字，是一个柜子从中国某一个港口到红海某一个港口、某一班船的海运费。它不是货进利雅得、开罗或安曼仓库的总费用。起运港的本地费用、目的港费用、关税、税费、保险，还有港口之后的拖车，都不在里面。
这些边界一致、柜型一致、出运窗口也一致，两个数字才比得了。一份港到港的 40HQ，和一份全包的 20GP，哪怕都写着吉达，回答的也不是同一个问题。

body.text: 运力，以及这条航线为什么紧

richText.text: 舱位是第一项。船公司决定这条中国到红海的航线派几艘船、挂哪些中国港口、现货市场还能卖出多少。抽掉一班船、跳过一个挂港，或者把一块舱位留给协议客户，这一周能报出来的就少了。上海有舱，不代表宁波有舱。
红海本身把选择收窄了。2023 年底以来，不少航线绕开苏伊士运河，改走好望角。航程变长，同一艘船一年能跑的航次就少了。2026 年霍尔木兹海峡实际关闭后，原来从海湾一侧进沙特的货，改走红海从吉达进。货挤到一个门户港，船更容易满，泊位也堵。保险把红海直到吉达列为战争风险区，这笔风险加在运费之外。
这些说明不了下周的具体价格。它说明的是：货没有变，报价也可以变。
货量是第二项，而且有日历可循。春节前几周工厂集中出货，假期里产量掉下去，节后再把船填满。斋月和开斋节期间，沙特、埃及、约旦的清关和拖车都会变慢。船按期到了，柜子仍可能等。海湾年底假期之前，另一头也是这个节奏。
旺的那一周，该早点订，并问清楚想要的那班船还有没有舱。这不是在上个月的价格上加一个固定百分比。淡的那一周适合再问一次，也不保证市场一定更便宜。
第三项是空箱。40HQ 的运价默认装货港有一只 40 英尺高箱。港口缺这种箱子时，船公司能卖的就少，或者把紧俏的箱子报得更贵。同一周、同一个目的港，南沙有箱，蛇口未必有。所以国家页按中国起运港分开写中位数，不给一个全国统一价。
工厂在内陆的话，最近的、又有箱子又有船期的港口，常常比运费略低但拖车很长的港口更划算。询价时告诉工厂所在的城市，不要只报一个猜的港口。
第四项是航线。直航是短的那种走法。上海或深圳到吉达，直航大约 17 到 18 天，经其他枢纽中转可以拉到 31 天左右。苏赫纳从华南直航大约 20 到 23 天，华北若要中转，可以到 32 到 35 天。亚喀巴直航大约 20 到 28 天，中转再加 3 到 7 天。吉布提直航大约 19 到 24 天，经新加坡或科伦坡大约 25 到 30 天。这些是港到港的区间，不是某一班船的承诺。
苏丹港是例外。中国直航有限，很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提中转。错过衔接，柜子可能再等一周以上。衔接决定时效，所以我们不公布苏丹港的航程。每一份苏丹报价都要问清航线。
中转更便宜，不是同一产品打了折，而是另一种产品。你用时间换运费，还多一个可能错过衔接的港口。目的港免柜期也是这个产品的一部分。一份报价含 14 天，另一份含 21 天，较长的免柜期往往已经算进价格。先看这一行，再决定运费数字低不低。
船公司还会按自己的时间表改发票上的其他项目。燃油附加跟着油价走。红海的战争风险或应急附加跟着安全局势走。船满的时候会出现旺季附加费。一般费率上调是船公司宣布的某个月涨价，宣布的幅度不一定全部落地。目的港还可能另收还箱费或拥堵费。
海运费相差一百美元的两份报价，把这些项目列出来之后，高低可能对调。请对方把报价分开写：海运费、起运港费用、在目的港收取的费用，以及不包含什么。运价页和国家页上的中位数只有海运费。用来看市场，不是你要付的总额，也不能拿来订舱。
本站公布的大多是现货市场：近一班船的价格，有效期是几天，不是一年。协议价可以离这个中位数很远，对签了协议的货主仍然有效。拿一份协议价去比本站的中位数，比的是两笔不同的交易。中位数描述现货市场。协议描述你已经锁住的条件。
有效期也容易弄反。运价表上的日期是今天的读数，页面上按七天展示，因为我们就是这样呈现已收集的报价。船公司自己的报价可以更短，到那班船的截关为止。本站页面上的日期是读数的日期。报价单上的日期才是你还能订的日期。不要当成同一天。

body.text: 一堆报价怎么变成一个中位数

richText.text: 指数是近 28 天、中国各起运港 40HQ 市场报价的中位数，每个目的港一个数。偏离中位数超过 50% 的价格会被剔除，避免一条离谱报价把线拽走。数字旁边写着样本量。两条报价做出来的中位数，下一条进来就会跳。二十条做出来的，就稳得多。周环比是拿今天这个 28 天读数，和一周前的同口径读数比。
没有报价的地方就空着。我们不用估算去填缺口，也没有报价就不发中位数。图和表是我们看到的市场读数。舱位和最终价格以微信或 WhatsApp 确认为准。

body.text: 选定之前先对齐这五项

richText.text: 起运港相同，或者不同的理由说得清。
目的港相同，柜型相同。
口径相同：海运费对海运费，不要拿纯海运费去比全包价。
价格有效期，以及对应的船期。
航线和免柜期。
报价比近期中位数低很多时，先问少了什么，再把它当成便宜。免柜期短、需要中转，或者有一笔费用要到目的港才出现，往往就是原因。

documents.title: Jeddah, Sokhna or Aqaba: choose your gateway.
documents.description: Pick the Red Sea port that serves your consignee. The cheapest port-to-port rate is not always the cheapest once trucking and customs are included.
documents.lead: Pick the Red Sea port that serves your consignee. The cheapest port-to-port rate is not always the cheapest once trucking and customs are included.

body.text: Start from the address, not the rate

richText.text: The gateway is the port that can clear your cargo and hand it to the consignee. Jeddah, Sokhna and Aqaba cover most shipments from China to the Red Sea. Djibouti and Port Sudan cover two more. They are not substitutes. A low rate into the wrong port means a second move, a second set of documents, and often a higher total than the rate that looked expensive.

Decide in this order. Where does the consignee want the goods? Which port clears cargo for that place as an ordinary import? What does the haul from that port cost? Only then compare ocean freight, on the same container and the same scope.

body.text: A consignee in Cairo is not a consignee in Jeddah

richText.text: Three short cases show why the port comes first. The consignee is in Cairo. Sokhna is the normal gateway. A cheaper rate into Jeddah still leaves the box outside Egypt, with a land border and a second customs entry between the cargo and the buyer. The consignee is in Addis Ababa. Djibouti is the sea gate, and the cost to compare is China to Djibouti plus the rail or the truck and clearance at Modjo, not a rate to Jeddah. The consignee is in Amman. Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport, so the question is the sailing and whether the goods sit inside the Aqaba zone, not which port to pick.

Jeddah serves western Saudi Arabia, and in 2026 it is the practical gateway for most Saudi container imports. With the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, cargo that once arrived through the Gulf is coming down the Red Sea instead. Ships are fuller, the berth is congested, and war-risk cover applies up to Jeddah.

Port to port from Shanghai or Shenzhen is about 17 to 31 days: roughly 17 to 18 days direct, longer when the sailing connects somewhere else. Every shipment needs a SABER shipment certificate, whether or not the product is regulated, and the customs declaration is filed on FASAH at least 48 hours before arrival. Duty is often 5 percent and sometimes as high as 20, plus 15 percent VAT. If the consignee is in Jeddah, Yanbu or another western city, this is the port. If the consignee is in Riyadh or Dammam, ask which gateway their broker actually clears through before you book a cheap rate into a port they do not use.

items.text: Saudi Arabia: documents, transit and live rates

richText.text: Ain Sokhna sits at the southern end of the Suez Canal and serves Cairo and the Suez industrial zone. Direct services from South China take about 20 to 23 days. Sailings from North China that connect elsewhere can take 32 to 35. War-risk and congestion charges on Red Sea services apply here as well.

Egypt requires Advance Cargo Information. The importer registers the shipment and receives an ACID number, and that number has to appear on the documents. The exporter files the bill of lading, packing list, invoice and certificate of origin on CargoX, and the exporting company has to be verified there before the first shipment. Filing early is what lets the importer use the faster release lane. A filing made hours before arrival does not.

items.text: Egypt: ACID, transit and live rates

richText.text: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport. Direct services take about 20 to 28 days, and a connection adds 3 to 7. The consignee needs an active Jordanian tax number that matches the documents, and the HS code belongs on the bill of lading. Regulated goods need JSMO approval. Medicines and medical items need JFDA approval. A clean file usually clears in 2 to 5 working days on ASYCUDA World.

Outside the Aqaba Special Economic Zone, duty is commonly 5 percent plus 16 percent general sales tax. Inside the zone a flat 5 percent applies, which changes the landed cost on its own, so ask the consignee which side of that line they are on. Free time at Aqaba is often short. Read the days on the quote instead of assuming you have two weeks.

items.text: Jordan: customs, transit and live rates

body.text: Djibouti, and the road on to Ethiopia

richText.text: Djibouti is a destination of its own and the sea gate for landlocked Ethiopia. Port to port is about 19 to 30 days. For Ethiopia, add the railway to Addis Ababa, about 12 to 15 hours, or 2 to 5 days by road, and clearance at Modjo dry port.

Containers for Ethiopia move under customs bond, so the Djibouti transit papers have to match the Ethiopian import declaration exactly. An ECTN is required for containers unloaded in Djibouti, and it should be in hand before departure. Cargo in direct transit to Ethiopia can be exempt when the bill of lading says "In transit to Ethiopia" and the consignee is in Ethiopia. The importer there also needs an import licence and foreign-exchange approval through an Ethiopian bank before you ship.

items.text: Djibouti and Ethiopia: ECTN, transit and live rates

body.text: Port Sudan, only after extra checks

richText.text: Sudan has been in armed conflict since April 2023, and Port Sudan is the gateway that is working. Direct sailings from China are limited. Much of the cargo connects via Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti, and a missed connection can add a week or more. We do not state a transit time, because the connection is the transit time.

For vessels sailing from 1 January 2026, Sudan-bound cargo needs an Advance Cargo Declaration number before it is loaded in China, and that number has to be printed on the bill of lading. Most commercial goods also need an SSMO inspection certificate before they leave China, plus an import licence. Confirm the port, the bank and the inland leg with the consignee before you book.

items.text: Sudan: ACD rules and live rates

richText.text: Once the consignee has named a gateway, compare quotes on one container type, one scope and one sailing window. A 40HQ median into Sokhna and a 40HQ median into Jeddah answer different questions. Use each one to see that port's market, then add the truck, the duty and the free time for the port you are actually using.

If the city is still unclear, run the shipment through the estimator and send us the consignee's city on WeChat or WhatsApp. The port is a question about the delivery. The rate comes after it. The checklist for a first shipment is the other half of this decision.

documents.title: 吉达、苏赫纳或亚喀巴：如何选择门户港？
documents.description: 先按收货人的地址选港口。港到港最低的运价，加上拖车和清关后不一定最低。
documents.lead: 先按收货人的地址选港口。港到港最低的运价，加上拖车和清关后不一定最低。

body.text: 从地址选起，不要从运价选起

richText.text: 门户港是能把这票货清关、再交到收货人手里的那个港口。中国到红海的货，大多走吉达、苏赫纳或亚喀巴。吉布提和苏丹港覆盖另外两种货。它们不能互相替代。运价低但港口选错，就要再运一次、再办一套单证，总数常常高于那份看起来贵的运价。
按这个顺序定。收货人要把货送到哪里？哪个港口按普通进口为那个地方清关？从那个港口拉过去要多少钱？然后才比较海运费，而且柜型和口径要一样。

body.text: 开罗的收货人不是吉达的收货人

richText.text: 三个短例子可以看出为什么港口要先定。收货人在开罗，苏赫纳是通常的门户。一份更便宜的吉达运价，柜子仍在埃及境外，中间还隔着陆路口岸和第二次清关。收货人在亚的斯亚贝巴，海运门户是吉布提，要比较的是中国到吉布提的运费，加上铁路或公路，以及莫焦的清关，不是一份到吉达的运价。收货人在安曼，亚喀巴是约旦唯一的海港，要问的是船期，以及货在不在亚喀巴特区里，不是选哪个港。
吉达服务沙特西部。2026 年它也是沙特大部分集装箱进口的实际门户。霍尔木兹海峡实际关闭后，原来从海湾进的货改走红海。船更满，泊位拥堵，战争风险覆盖到吉达。
上海或深圳到港大约 17 到 31 天：直航大约 17 到 18 天，中转更长。每票货都要办 SABER 货物符合性证书，不论产品是否受管制。报关单至少在到港前 48 小时通过 FASAH 提交。关税常见是 5%，有的高到 20%，另加 15% 的增值税。收货人在吉达、延布或其他西部城市，就走这个港。收货人在利雅得或达曼，先问他们的报关行实际从哪个港清关，再去订一个他们不用的港口的低价。

items.text: 沙特：单证、航程和当前运价

richText.text: 苏赫纳在苏伊士运河南端，服务开罗和苏伊士工业区。华南直航大约 20 到 23 天。华北经其他港中转，可以到 32 到 35 天。红海航线上的战争风险和拥堵附加，这里同样有。
埃及要求提前货物信息申报。进口商登记这票货并取得 ACID 编号，单证上必须写上这个号。出口商在 CargoX 提交提单、装箱单、发票和原产地证，出口公司第一次出运前要先在那里完成认证。早点申报，进口商才能走更快的放行通道。到港前几小时才提交，就享受不到。
亚喀巴是约旦唯一的海港。直航大约 20 到 28 天，中转再加 3 到 7 天。收货人要有与单证一致的有效约旦税号，提单上要写 HS 编码。受管制的产品需要 JSMO 批准。药品和医疗用品需要 JFDA 批准。单证齐全的话，在 ASYCUDA World 上通常 2 到 5 个工作日清关。
亚喀巴经济特区以外，关税常见是 5%，另加 16% 的一般销售税。特区内统一 5%，到岸成本会因此差一截，所以要问收货人在线的哪一边。亚喀巴的免柜期常常偏短。看报价上的天数，不要默认有两周。

items.text: 约旦：清关、航程和当前运价

body.text: 吉布提，以及继续去埃塞俄比亚

richText.text: 吉布提本身是一个目的地，也是内陆国埃塞俄比亚的海运门户。港到港大约 19 到 30 天。去埃塞俄比亚，还要加上到亚的斯亚贝巴的铁路，大约 12 到 15 小时，或者公路 2 到 5 天，清关在莫焦陆港。
去埃塞俄比亚的柜子在海关监管下转运，吉布提的转运单证必须和埃塞的进口申报完全一致。在吉布提卸货的集装箱需要 ECTN，最好开船前就办好。直接转运埃塞俄比亚的货，提单写明 “In transit to Ethiopia”、且收货人在埃塞俄比亚时，可以免办。那边的进口商还要在出运前办妥进口许可证，并通过埃塞的银行拿到外汇额度。

items.text: 吉布提和埃塞俄比亚：ECTN、航程和当前运价

richText.text: 苏丹自 2023 年 4 月起处于武装冲突中，苏丹港是目前能用的门户。中国直航有限。很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提中转，错过衔接可能再多一周以上。我们不写航程，因为衔接本身就是航程。
2026 年 1 月 1 日起开航的船，去苏丹的货要在中国装船前取得预先货物申报编号，并印在提单上。多数商品离开中国前还要有 SSMO 检验证书，另加进口许可证。订舱前先和收货人确认港口、银行和内陆这段还能不能走。

items.text: 苏丹：ACD 规则和当前运价

richText.text: 收货人指定门户港之后，再按同一种柜型、同一种口径、同一个出运窗口比报价。苏赫纳的 40HQ 中位数和吉达的 40HQ 中位数，回答的是不同的问题。各自用来看那个港的市场，然后加上你真正要走的那个港的拖车、关税和免柜期。
城市还不确定的话，先用估价器跑一遍，再在微信或 WhatsApp 上把收货人的城市发给我们。港口是配送问题。运价排在它后面。第一次出运还要配一份清单。

items.text: 哪些因素影响红海运价

documents.title: Your first shipment? Start with this checklist.
documents.description: A first shipment from China to the Red Sea needs a full enquiry, a price built the right way, and destination documents filed before the cargo is ready.
documents.lead: A first shipment from China to the Red Sea needs a full enquiry, a price built the right way, and destination documents filed before the cargo is ready.

body.text: What to send before anyone prices it

richText.text: A quote is only as good as the facts behind it. Send the cargo description and the HS code, the number of packages, the dimensions and the gross weight, the date the cargo will be ready, and the Incoterms you sold on. Name an origin you can actually load from, the destination port, and the consignee's city. For a full container, add the type and how many: 20GP, 40GP or 40HQ. For groupage, add the volume in cubic metres and the weight in tonnes.
Dangerous goods, and anything with batteries, belong in that first message. A quote built for general cargo cannot be reused for them. Finding out after the booking wastes the sailing.

Full containers are priced per box, so settle the type first. A 40HQ carries more cubic cargo than a 40GP, and it is the box most of the market quotes on this site are for. A 20GP is the better fit when the cargo is heavy and would hit the weight limit of a 40-foot box long before it filled the space. Mixing those up makes every comparison meaningless.

Groupage, LCL, is priced per W/M. The carrier bills the larger of the cubic metres and the metric tonnes, with a minimum of 1 W/M. Dense cargo pays on weight. Light cargo pays on volume. The minimum means a small shipment is billed as one unit even when it is smaller than that.

Either way, a port-to-port figure is ocean freight. Origin charges in China, destination charges, customs, duty, insurance and inland delivery are separate budgets. An all-in quote can be the right way to buy, but only if you can see the lines. Ask for it written out.

Check the commercial invoice, the packing list and the consignee's details while the cargo is still at the factory. The invoice needs a real description, the HS code, the value and the currency, and the seller and buyer named as they appear on the contract. The packing list needs marks, package counts, weights and measures that match the invoice. The consignee's name has to match their tax or commercial registration, not a shortened trading name.

The bill of lading is drawn from those papers. If the consignee, the HS code or a destination reference such as an ACID is wrong on the draft, the filing at the far end fails, and the correction costs time at both ends. Read the draft. Do not leave it until the day of departure.
Each Red Sea destination adds a filing of its own, and most of them have to be done before the ship sails, not after it arrives. A generic export file will not catch a missing one.

Saudi Arabia: a SABER shipment certificate for every shipment, plus a product certificate when the goods are regulated. The customs declaration is filed on FASAH at least 48 hours before the vessel arrives.
Egypt: an ACID number from the importer, printed on the documents, and an Advance Cargo Information filing by the exporter on CargoX. The exporting company has to be verified on CargoX first.
Jordan: a consignee tax number that matches the documents, the HS code on the bill of lading, and JSMO or JFDA approval when the goods are regulated.

Djibouti: an ECTN before departure, unless the cargo is in direct transit to Ethiopia and the bill of lading says so. Cargo for Ethiopia also needs the importer's licence and bank approval before you ship.

Sudan: an Advance Cargo Declaration number obtained before loading and printed on the bill of lading, for vessels sailing from 1 January 2026, plus an SSMO inspection certificate for most commercial goods.
The country pages spell out the fees, the validity and the papers each filing takes. Read the page for the port you are using.

body.text: Three clocks before the ship sails

richText.text: Three clocks run before departure, and missing any of them rolls the cargo to a later sailing. Shipping instructions have to reach the forwarder in time for the carrier's document cut-off. The verified gross mass has to be filed before the container is loaded on the vessel. The cargo itself has to be inside the terminal before the cargo cut-off.

Those cut-offs are often a couple of days before departure, and a holiday in between makes the window shorter than it looks. Ask for all three times in writing when the booking is confirmed. "The ship leaves on the 20th" is not a cargo cut-off.

A workable order is: confirm the cargo and the consignee, choose the port, start the destination filing while the booking is being made, send shipping instructions before the document cut-off, and deliver the container before the cargo cut-off. Do not send the truck to the factory until the sailing and the price are confirmed. Doing the documents after the ship has sailed is how a first shipment loses a week.
Which port to choose, and why a rate moves, are covered in the other two notes. This list assumes you have read them, or that you already know the consignee's gateway.

Sending an enquiry through this site does not hold space. A rate here is a market reading or an estimate, valid for the window we state, and space moves. A container is reserved only after we confirm the sailing and the price with you on WeChat or WhatsApp.

Keep that confirmation. It should name the carrier or the service, the ports, the container, the sailing, the price, what the price includes, the free days, and the three cut-offs above. If a line is missing, ask before the cargo leaves the factory. Changing a bill of lading after departure is slower and more expensive than writing it correctly the first time.

body.text: Send this list back with the enquiry

richText.text: Cargo name, HS code, packages, dimensions, gross weight.
Ready date, Incoterms, origin port, destination port, consignee city.
Container type and quantity, or volume and weight for LCL.
Dangerous goods or batteries named at the start, if there are any.
Invoice, packing list and consignee details checked against each other.
The destination filing started: SABER, ACID, ECTN or ACD, as that port requires.
A written quote, itemised, with the routing and the free days.
Sailing, price and cut-offs confirmed on WeChat or WhatsApp before the cargo moves.
You can start with the estimator and send whatever you already have. A partial enquiry gets a partial answer. A complete one gets a quote you can book against.

documents.title: 首次出运？从这份清单开始。
documents.description: 第一次走红海，先把询价信息、计费方式和目的港申报备齐，再安排出货。
documents.lead: 第一次走红海，先把询价信息、计费方式和目的港申报备齐，再安排出货。

richText.text: 报价好不好，取决于后面的事实。发品名和 HS 编码、件数、尺寸、毛重、货好的日期，以及你成交用的贸易条款。起运港要是你真正能装货的那个，再加上目的港和收货人的城市。整箱写明柜型和数量：20GP、40GP 或 40HQ。拼箱写立方米体积和吨数。
危险品和任何带电池的货，第一条消息里就要说。按普货做的报价不能挪来用。订完才发现，这班船就浪费了。
整箱按柜计价，所以先定柜型。40HQ 比 40GP 装更多泡货，本站大多数市场报价也是这种柜。货很重、40 英尺柜还没装满就超重时，20GP 更合适。柜型弄混，后面的比较都没有意义。
拼箱按 W/M 计价。船公司取立方米和公吨中较大的那个，最低 1 W/M。重货按重量付，泡货按体积付。最低收费的意思是，货再小，也按一个单位计。
不管哪种，港到港的数字都只是海运费。中国的起运港费用、目的港费用、清关、关税、保险和内陆运输，要分开做预算。全包价可以是合适的买法，但前提是你看得到分项。请对方逐行写出来。
货还在工厂时，就把商业发票、装箱单和收货人资料核对完。发票要有真实品名、HS 编码、金额和币种，买卖双方的名称要和合同上一致。装箱单上的唛头、件数、重量和尺寸要和发票对得上。收货人名称要和税号或商业登记一致，不要用简称。
提单是从这些文件里抽出来的。草稿上的收货人、HS 编码，或 ACID 这类目的港编号写错了，那边的申报就会失败，两头都要花时间改。草稿要读。不要留到开船当天。

body.text: 每个目的港另外要的申报

richText.text: 红海每个目的港都有自己的申报，而且多数要在开船前办，不是到港之后。一套通用的出口文件查不出漏了哪一项。
沙特：每票货都要 SABER 货物符合性证书，受管制的产品还要产品证书。报关单至少在船舶到港前 48 小时通过 FASAH 提交。
埃及：进口商提供 ACID 编号并印在单证上，出口商在 CargoX 做提前货物信息申报。出口公司要先在 CargoX 完成认证。
约旦：与单证一致的收货人税号，提单上的 HS 编码，受管制产品还要 JSMO 或 JFDA 的批准。
吉布提：开船前办 ECTN。直接转运埃塞俄比亚、且提单写明的，可以免。去埃塞的货，出运前还要有进口商的许可证和银行额度。
苏丹：2026 年 1 月 1 日起开航的船，装船前取得预先货物申报编号并印在提单上。多数商品还要 SSMO 检验证书。
费用、有效期和每项申报要哪些材料，写在对应的国家页上。走哪个港，就读哪一页。
开船前有三个时间，错过任何一个，货就得改下一班。提单补料要赶在船公司的截单时间之前交给货代。核实总重必须在集装箱装上船之前申报。货本身要在截关前进入码头。
这些截点常常比开船早几天，中间再夹一个假期，窗口比看上去更短。订舱确认时把三个时间都要成书面的。“船 20 号开”不是截关时间。
比较顺的顺序是：先确认货和收货人，选定港口，订舱的同时办目的港申报，截单前交补料，截关前把柜子送进码头。船期和价格确认之前，不要派车去工厂。单证留到开船之后再补，第一次出运往往就这样多等一周。
港口怎么选、运价为什么会变，写在另外两篇里。这份清单默认你已经看过，或者已经知道收货人走哪个港。
在本站提交询价，并不占舱。这里的价格是市场读数或估价，只在我们写明的窗口内有意义，舱位本身在变。只有我们在微信或 WhatsApp 上和你确认了船期和价格，柜子才算留住。
把这封确认留着。上面应写明船公司或航线、港口、柜型、船期、价格、价格包含什么、免柜期，以及上面那三个截点。少一行，就在货离开工厂之前问。提单开船后再改，比第一次写对更慢，也更贵。

body.text: 询价时把这份清单对一遍

richText.text: 品名、HS 编码、件数、尺寸、毛重。
货好日期、贸易条款、起运港、目的港、收货人城市。
柜型和数量；拼箱则是体积和重量。
有危险品或电池，一开始就写明。
发票、装箱单和收货人资料互相核对过。
目的港申报已经开始：按港口办理 SABER、ACID、ECTN 或 ACD。
书面分项报价，含航线和免柜期。
货动之前，船期、价格和截点已在微信或 WhatsApp 上确认。
也可以先用估价器，把你已经有的资料发过来。询价不完整，回答就不完整。资料齐的那一份，才能拿去订舱。

documents.title: Shipping to Jeddah: SABER in 5 steps
documents.description: Five SABER steps for Jeddah: check the HS code, open the importer account, then the product certificate and the shipment certificate.
documents.lead: Five SABER steps for Jeddah: check the HS code, open the importer account, then the product certificate and the shipment certificate.

body.text: A process note, not clearance advice

richText.text: This is a general process note for the SABER steps on a shipment to Jeddah. It is not legal advice, and it is not customs advice. The certificate a product needs depends on its HS code and on the rules in force when the file is made. Check the HS code, and treat the clearance partner's confirmation as the result that counts. Nothing on this page promises an outcome for a named product.

SABER is SASO's platform. The five steps below are the same sequence as the short note already written for this subject: find out whether the HS code is regulated, have the Saudi importer open the record, obtain the product certificate where one is required, obtain the shipment certificate for this cargo, and leave a certificate that Jeddah customs can read electronically. Read them in that order. A later step does not repair a code or a product record that was wrong at the start.

Start with the HS code. On SABER, that code is how you tell whether the product is regulated. A regulated product needs a certificate. A product that is not regulated is not asked for that certificate: only the basic information is recorded.

The Saudi Arabia page describes the non-regulated path in its own words: non-regulated products use an importer self-declaration. This note does not merge that sentence with the line above into a new rule. Both are already written. The code decides which description you are in. A code copied from a similar product, or guessed from a trade name, sends the file through the wrong door. The person who knows the goods should confirm the code before anyone opens a SABER record.

Do this before the booking is treated as ready. The product certificate, where the product is regulated, is issued against the product and the model that the code describes. A code that changes later is not a clerical fix. It changes the product the certificates were built for, and the shipment certificate that hangs on those certificates stalls. Confirm the code once, write it the same way on the invoice, and leave it.

The Saudi-registered importer opens the SABER account, or a representative that importer has authorized does it. The record they enter is the product and the importer. A shipper in China does not take the importer's place on the platform. If the buyer has not opened the account, and has not named the representative who will, the certificates in the next steps have nowhere to sit.

Ask whether that account exists while the cargo is still at the factory. The product information and the importer information in the account have to be the information the commercial invoice and the bill of lading will carry. The shipment certificate has to match those two papers. An account opened under a shortened trading name, or under a product description the invoice will not use, has to be corrected before the shipment certificate is requested, not after Jeddah has already tried to read it.

The importer is also the party named when a marking rule applies. Since 1 October 2026, the Saudi Arabia page says products under ten technical regulations must show the importer's name and commercial registration number. This note does not list those ten regulations. They are not listed on that page either. Whether this product is one of them is a question for the HS code and for the clearance partner, not a conclusion this page can make.

The product certificate of conformity, the PCoC, comes next for a regulated product. It is one certificate per product and per model. A conformity body that SASO recognizes issues it, against the Saudi standard that applies. Where that standard requires testing, the file includes the test evidence.

A PCoC is valid for up to 1 year. Testing can add 2–4 weeks, so the work has to start several weeks before the shipment certificate is needed. A product certificate that expires before you apply for the shipment certificate is not a valid product certificate. Renew it before the expiry. Waiting until a file has already been refused is the late version of the same task.

One model is one certificate. A second model is a second certificate, even when the commercial name looks the same. Keep the model, the applicable standard and the test evidence on the version of the product that will actually be loaded. If the declared specification changes while the certificate is in progress, the shipment certificate that has to hang on this PCoC stalls. Finish the specification before the application, and do not revise it in the middle.

The shipment certificate of conformity, the SCoC, is one certificate for this shipment. It hangs on a PCoC that is still valid. The application uses the invoice and the bill of lading data. No valid PCoC means there is no SCoC. No SCoC means Jeddah cannot clear the cargo.

The Saudi Arabia page states the same certificate for every shipment, regulated or not. It states the fee as SAR 350 before VAT, the validity as 90 days, and the match: the certificate must agree with the bill of lading and the commercial invoice. Those 90 days are the life of the shipment certificate. They are not the period of up to 1 year on the PCoC. A shipment certificate built on an old consignee, an old model or an old value will not match the papers, and a certificate that does not match is not the certificate customs will accept.

Read the draft invoice and the draft bill of lading against the SABER application before you treat the shipment certificate as finished. The data on the application are the data customs will compare. A correction after the certificate is issued is a new pass through the same match, not a note in the margin. For a product that is not regulated, SABER still only records the basic information at the product step, and the Saudi Arabia page still calls that path an importer self-declaration. The shipment step does not disappear. Every shipment still needs the shipment certificate.

At Jeddah, customs checks the SCoC electronically. SABER and the customs platform are linked. The certificate is the record on that link, for this shipment. There is nothing useful to add at the counter if the shipment certificate was never issued, or if the product certificate under it has already expired.

Renew the PCoC before it expires. A product certificate that runs out while the shipment certificate still depends on it leaves the shipment without a valid PCoC, and without a valid PCoC there is no SCoC. Changing the declared specification at this stage stalls the SCoC as well. The specification customs reads has to be the specification the certificates were issued for.

The Saudi Arabia page adds a separate clock for the customs declaration. It is filed on FASAH at least 48 hours before the vessel arrives. That 48 hours is the declaration before arrival. It is not the 2–4 weeks that testing can add to a PCoC, and it does not stand in for the shipment certificate. Both have to be done. The declaration does not create the SCoC, and the SCoC does not replace the declaration.

body.text: Before the cargo is called ready

richText.text: A workable order is the five steps, started while the cargo is still at the factory. Confirm the HS code and whether SABER treats the product as regulated. Have the Saudi-registered importer, or the authorized representative, open the account and enter the product and the importer. If the product is regulated, start the PCoC several weeks ahead, allow 2–4 weeks where testing is required, and keep a certificate whose validity is at most 1 year. Apply for the SCoC against a PCoC that is still valid, using the invoice and the bill of lading, and check the match. The Saudi Arabia page is where the shipment-certificate fee of SAR 350 before VAT and the 90-day validity are stated. Leave the declared specification unchanged once that chain is built. Renew the PCoC before it expires, so the electronic check at Jeddah has a shipment certificate to read.

If the product is not regulated, the product step is the basic information only, which the Saudi Arabia page describes as an importer self-declaration, and the shipment still needs its SCoC. Check the HS code again with the clearance partner before the file is treated as ready. This page does not confirm a certificate for any named product. The country page is the place for the rest of the Saudi file, including the FASAH declaration at least 48 hours before arrival.

items.text: Saudi Arabia: the SABER shipment certificate on the country page

richText.text: Q: Does every shipment to Jeddah need a SABER shipment certificate?
A: Yes. Every shipment needs a SABER shipment certificate, whether or not the product is regulated. Without that certificate, Jeddah cannot clear the cargo.
Q: How long do the SABER certificates last?

A: A product certificate (PCoC) is valid for up to 1 year. The shipment certificate (SCoC) stated on the Saudi Arabia page is valid for 90 days, costs SAR 350 before VAT, and must match the bill of lading and the commercial invoice.
Q: What if the product is not regulated?

A: On SABER, a product that is not regulated only needs its basic information recorded. The Saudi Arabia page describes non-regulated products as an importer self-declaration. The shipment still needs a shipment certificate.
Q: What stops the shipment certificate?

A: There is no shipment certificate without a valid product certificate. Jeddah customs checks the shipment certificate electronically, because SABER is linked to the customs platform. Changing the declared specification stalls the shipment certificate, and the product certificate has to be renewed before it expires.

documents.title: 运往吉达：SABER 分五步
documents.description: 吉达 SABER 分五步：核对 HS 编码，进口商开户，再办产品证书和货物证书。
documents.lead: 吉达 SABER 分五步：核对 HS 编码，进口商开户，再办产品证书和货物证书。

body.text: 这是流程说明，不是清关意见

richText.text: 这篇只写运往吉达时 SABER 的通用流程。它不是法律意见，也不是清关意见。具体要哪一种证书，取决于产品的 HS 编码，以及办理当时的现行法规。先核对 HS 编码，再以清关伙伴的确认为准。本页不对任何具体产品承诺结果。
SABER 是 SASO 的平台。下面五步和这个题目已有的短稿是同一条顺序：先按 HS 编码确认是否受管制，再由沙特进口商建档，需要产品证书的就去办，然后为这一票办理货物证书，最后留下吉达海关能够电子读取的证书。按这个顺序读。后面的步骤补不回一开始就写错的编码或产品记录。

body.text: 第 1 步：核对 HS 编码

richText.text: 从 HS 编码开始。在 SABER 上，用这个编码确认产品是否受管制。受管制的产品要证书。不受管制的产品不要那张证书，只录入基本信息。
沙特页用自己的说法写非管制这一路：非管制产品使用进口商自我声明。这里不把这句话和上面那句合成一条新规则。两句都是已经写过的。编码决定你落在哪一种说法里。从相近产品抄来的编码，或用品名猜出来的编码，会把档案送进另一扇门。了解这票货的人，应该在任何人开设 SABER 记录之前确认编码。
在把订舱当成已经就绪之前做这一步。产品受管制时，产品证书是按这个编码所描述的产品和型号签发的。事后改编码不是改一个笔误。它改的是证书所对应的产品，挂在那些证书下面的货物证书会卡住。编码确认一次，发票上按同一个写法，然后不要再改。

body.text: 第 2 步：进口商开设 SABER

richText.text: 由在沙特注册的进口商开设 SABER 账户，或由其授权代表开设。录入的是产品和进口商信息。中国的发货人不能在平台上代替这个进口商。买方还没有开户，也没有指定由谁作为授权代表来办，后面的证书就没有地方挂。
货还在工厂时就问这个账户在不在。账户里的产品信息和进口商信息，必须是商业发票和提单将要写的那些信息。货物证书必须和这两份文件一致。用简称开的户，或用发票上不会出现的品名开的户，要在申请货物证书之前改好，而不是等吉达已经读过一次之后。
涉及标识要求时，写上的也是这个进口商。沙特页写明：自 2026 年 10 月 1 日起，10 项技术法规下的产品须标注进口商名称和商业登记号。本篇不列出那 10 项。沙特页也没有逐项列出。这票货是不是其中之一，问 HS 编码和清关伙伴，不是本页能下的结论。

body.text: 第 3 步：产品符合性证书

richText.text: 受管制的产品下一步是产品符合性证书，PCoC。每个产品、每个型号一份。由 SASO 认可的符合性机构签发，按适用的沙特标准。适用标准要求检测时，档案里附上检测证据。
PCoC 的有效期最长 1 年。检测可能再加 2–4 周，所以要在需要货物证书之前数周就启动。申请货物证书时产品证书已经过期，它就不是一份有效的产品证书。在到期前续办。等档案已经被退了再去续，只是同一件事的晚版本。
一个型号一份证书。第二个型号就是另一份证书，哪怕商品名称看起来一样。型号、适用标准和检测证据，都要对上真正要装的那一版产品。证书还在办、申报规格中途改了，必须挂在这份 PCoC 下面的货物证书会卡住。规格在申请之前定下来，办到一半不要改。

body.text: 第 4 步：货物符合性证书

richText.text: 货物符合性证书，SCoC，是这一票一份。它挂在仍然有效的 PCoC 下面。申请时用发票和提单上的数据。没有有效的 PCoC，就没有 SCoC。没有 SCoC，吉达清不了关。
沙特页写的是同一张证书：每一票都要，不论是否受管制。费用写的是 350 里亚尔（不含增值税），有效期 90 天，并且必须与提单和商业发票一致。这 90 天是货物证书的有效期，不是 PCoC 最长 1 年的那个期限。货物证书如果按旧的收货人、旧的型号或旧的货值来做，就和单证对不上。对不上的证书，不是海关会接受的那一张。
把货物证书当成办完之前，拿发票草稿和提单草稿对一遍 SABER 里的申请。申请上的数据就是海关要核对的数据。证书签发后再改，是按同样的一致性再走一遍，不是在页边补一句。产品不受管制时，SABER 在产品这一步仍然只录入基本信息，沙特页仍把这一路称为进口商自我声明。货物这一步不会因此取消。每一票仍然要货物证书。

body.text: 第 5 步：吉达海关读取证书

richText.text: 在吉达，海关电子核验 SCoC。SABER 与海关平台联动。证书就是这条联动上、属于这一票的那条记录。货物证书根本没有签发，或者它下面的产品证书已经过期，到柜台再补也没有用。
PCoC 在到期前续好。货物证书还依赖它的时候产品证书先到期，这一票就没有有效的 PCoC；没有有效的 PCoC，就没有 SCoC。这个阶段再改申报规格，同样会卡住 SCoC。海关读到的规格，必须是签发证书时的那个规格。
沙特页另外写了一个报关时间：报关单至少在船舶到港前 48 小时通过 FASAH 提交。这 48 小时是到港前的申报，不是 PCoC 检测可能加上的那 2–4 周，也不能代替货物证书。两件事都要做。申报不会生成 SCoC，SCoC 也不代替申报。

比较顺的做法，是货还在工厂时就把五步启动。确认 HS 编码，以及 SABER 是否把这个产品当作受管制。由沙特注册进口商或其授权代表开户，录入产品和进口商。产品受管制的，PCoC 提前数周开始；需要检测时留出 2–4 周；证书有效期最长 1 年。在 PCoC 仍然有效时，用发票和提单申请 SCoC，并核对是否一致。货物证书 350 里亚尔（不含增值税）的费用和 90 天有效期，写在沙特页上。这条链一旦建好，申报规格就不要再改。PCoC 在到期前续办，吉达的电子核验才读得到货物证书。
产品不受管制时，产品这一步只录入基本信息，沙特页称之为进口商自我声明，这一票仍然要 SCoC。把档案当成就绪之前，再和清关伙伴核对一次 HS 编码。本页不确认任何具体产品的证书。沙特文件的其余部分在国家页上，包括至少在到港前 48 小时通过 FASAH 提交的报关单。

items.text: 沙特：国家页上的 SABER 货物证书

richText.text: 问：运到吉达的每一票都要 SABER 货物证书吗？
答：要。每一票都要 SABER 货物符合性证书，不论产品是否受管制。没有这张证书，吉达清不了关。
问：SABER 的证书有效期是多久？
答：产品符合性证书（PCoC）有效期最长 1 年。沙特页上写的货物符合性证书（SCoC）有效期 90 天，费用 350 里亚尔（不含增值税），并且必须与提单和商业发票一致。
问：产品不受管制怎么办？
答：在 SABER 上，不受管制的产品只录入基本信息。沙特页把非管制产品写成进口商自我声明。这一票仍然要货物符合性证书。
问：什么情况会让货物证书办不下来？
答：没有有效的产品符合性证书，就没有货物符合性证书。吉达海关电子核验货物证书，因为 SABER 与海关平台联动。中途改申报规格会卡住货物证书。产品证书要在到期前续好。

documents.title: Shipping to Sokhna: the ACID number in 3 steps
documents.description: Sokhna needs the 19-digit ACID on the documents. The importer files it on NAFEZA, and the exporter uploads on CargoX.
documents.lead: Sokhna needs the 19-digit ACID on the documents. The importer files it on NAFEZA, and the exporter uploads on CargoX.

body.text: A process note, not clearance advice

richText.text: This is a general process note for the ACID on a sea shipment into Egypt, including a shipment that will clear at Sokhna. It is not legal advice, and it is not customs advice. What has to be declared follows the HS code and the rules in force when the file is made. Check the HS code, and treat the clearance partner's confirmation as the result that counts. Nothing on this page promises an outcome for a named product.

ACID means Advance Cargo Information Declaration. Egyptian customs issues one 19-digit number for each shipment. The number is not a general import licence. A new shipment needs a new number, and the validity of a number is limited. This note does not add a length to that validity, because no length is stated in the sources used here. Sea cargo into Egypt has required an ACID since October 2021. Air cargo has required one since January 2026. Sokhna is a sea port, so the sea rule is the one this shipment is under. The air date is part of the same declaration, and it does not limit the sea rule to Sokhna.

If the documents do not carry the ACID, Sokhna cannot clear the cargo. The same number applies to all sea cargo into Egypt, not only to cargo that discharges at Sokhna. Choosing another Egyptian port does not retire the declaration. The three steps below are the ones already written for this subject: the importer files on NAFEZA, the exporter is verified on CargoX and linked to that shipment, and the 19-digit number is printed on the papers before the vessel sails.

body.text: Step 1: the importer files on NAFEZA

richText.text: The Egyptian importer files the shipment on NAFEZA, the national single window. The filing is made from the proforma invoice. It enters the parties, the HS code, the value and the origin. Those four are the content of the declaration. A proforma that still uses a working description, a provisional value or an origin that the final invoice will not use, is the wrong base for the number.

File at least 48 hours before the vessel sails. The same filing may be made up to 3 months before sailing. That window is about departure, not about the day the ship reaches Sokhna. Earlier than 3 months is outside the window stated here. Later than 48 hours before sailing misses the minimum stated here. Count the 48 hours from sailing, and do not borrow a different 48-hour rule from another country's arrival declaration.

The importer is the party who files this step and who receives the number. A shipper in China can prepare the proforma invoice so the parties, the HS code, the value and the origin are stable. The shipper does not replace the Egyptian importer on NAFEZA. If the importer has not filed, there is no ACID for the exporter to print, however complete the export documents look.

The exporter, the supplier in China, opens a company account on CargoX. CargoX is the partner platform on the exporter's side of NAFEZA. The account has to be verified, and it has to be linked with the importer on this same shipment. Registration of the account is free. Verification is charged once, as a small fee. This note does not name that fee. No amount is stated in the sources used here.

The Egypt page says the same gate in its own words. The exporter's company must be verified on CargoX before the Advance Cargo Information is filed. The filing the exporter makes there is the bill of lading, the packing list, the commercial invoice as a PDF and as a structured Excel file, and the certificate of origin. A company that has not passed verification cannot use that filing, even when the documents themselves are already drafted.

Open the verified account before the first shipment, not on the day the number arrives. The link is to the importer and to this shipment, not to a standing approval for every future cargo. The next shipment is a new ACID and a new link. Verification of the company is the one-time step. The shipment link is not.

When customs approves the filing, NAFEZA sends the 19-digit ACID to the importer and to the exporter. Print it. The printing is typed, not handwritten. It goes on the commercial invoice, the packing list, the bill of lading and the certificate of origin. A number that lives only in an email, or that is written by hand in a margin, is not the number on the documents.

The exporter uploads the final documents through CargoX before the vessel sails. Final means the documents that carry the typed ACID, not an earlier draft that still has a blank where the number will go. Uploading a set that does not match the parties, the HS code, the value and the origin entered on NAFEZA leaves the declaration and the documents as two different shipments.

The Egypt page adds what the timing is worth at the far end. Filing the Advance Cargo Information well before arrival lets the importer use the faster release lane. A filing made hours before arrival does not. That sentence is about arrival, and it sits next to the rule already stated: the importer's declaration itself is at least 48 hours before sailing, and at most 3 months before sailing. This page does not collapse those into one threshold. Do the NAFEZA filing inside its own window, and do not leave the CargoX upload until a few hours before the ship reaches Sokhna.

An ACID is issued per shipment. It is not a licence the importer holds and reuses. The next booking, even for the same product and the same buyer, needs its own 19-digit number. The validity of each number is limited. When a number is no longer the valid number for that shipment, printing it on a new set of documents does not revive it. Request the new number, then print that one.

Keep the typed number identical on the commercial invoice, the packing list, the bill of lading and the certificate of origin. One transposed digit is a different number. The Egypt page says the ACID must appear on all shipping documents, which is the same requirement from the other side: the number NAFEZA sent is the number the documents show, on each of them, not on a covering message alone.

A workable order is the three steps, closed before sailing. The Egyptian importer files on NAFEZA from a proforma invoice that already has the parties, the HS code, the value and the origin, at least 48 hours before sailing and no earlier than 3 months. The Chinese exporter has a verified CargoX account, linked to that importer for this shipment, with registration free and verification charged once as a small fee. After approval, both sides hold the same 19-digit ACID. It is typed on the commercial invoice, the packing list, the bill of lading and the certificate of origin. The exporter uploads those final documents on CargoX before the vessel sails. The Egypt page is where the PDF-and-Excel invoice and the faster release lane are stated.

Check the HS code with the clearance partner before the file is treated as ready. The number does not decide whether the product may be imported. It identifies this shipment's advance declaration. This page does not confirm an ACID for any named product. Without the number on the documents, Sokhna cannot clear the cargo, and the same gap blocks any other sea arrival in Egypt.

items.text: Egypt: ACID on the country page

richText.text: Q: What is an ACID number?

A: ACID means Advance Cargo Information Declaration. Egyptian customs issues one 19-digit number for each shipment. It is not a general import licence. A new shipment needs a new number, and the validity is limited.
Q: When does the importer have to file the ACID?

A: The importer files on NAFEZA at least 48 hours before the vessel sails, and may file up to 3 months ahead, from the proforma invoice. Sea cargo into Egypt has required an ACID since October 2021. Air cargo has required it since January 2026.
Q: Where is the 19-digit number printed?

A: After customs approves the filing, NAFEZA sends the 19-digit ACID to the importer and the exporter. It is printed, not handwritten, on the commercial invoice, the packing list, the bill of lading and the certificate of origin. The exporter uploads the final documents on CargoX before the vessel sails.
Q: Is the ACID only for Sokhna?
A: No. An ACID applies to all sea cargo into Egypt, not only to Sokhna. If the documents for a Sokhna shipment do not carry the ACID, Sokhna cannot clear it.

documents.title: 运往苏赫纳：ACID 编号分三步
documents.description: 苏赫纳的单证要有 19 位 ACID。进口商在 NAFEZA 申报，出口商在 CargoX 上传。
documents.lead: 苏赫纳的单证要有 19 位 ACID。进口商在 NAFEZA 申报，出口商在 CargoX 上传。

body.text: 这是流程说明，不是清关意见

richText.text: 这篇只写海运进入埃及、包括在苏赫纳清关的这一票，ACID 的通用流程。它不是法律意见，也不是清关意见。要申报什么，取决于 HS 编码和办理当时的现行法规。先核对 HS 编码，再以清关伙伴的确认为准。本页不对任何具体产品承诺结果。

ACID 即 Advance Cargo Information Declaration，预先货物信息申报。埃及海关为每一票货发一个 19 位编号。这个编号不是通用进口许可。新的一票要新的编号，编号的有效期有限。这里的材料没有写有效期是多少天，本篇就不补一个天数。海运进入埃及的货物自 2021 年 10 月起必须有 ACID。空运自 2026 年 1 月起必须有。苏赫纳是海港，这一票适用的是海运这条。空运的日期属于同一项申报，并不把海运规则收成只有苏赫纳。
单证上没有 ACID，苏赫纳就清不了关。同一个编号规则适用于所有海运进入埃及的货物，不只是在苏赫纳卸的货。改挂埃及的另一个港，不会取消这项申报。下面三步就是这个题目已经写过的三步：进口商在 NAFEZA 申报，出口商在 CargoX 完成核验并关联到这一票，19 位编号在开船前印上单证。

body.text: 第 1 步：进口商在 NAFEZA 申报

richText.text: 埃及进口商在 NAFEZA，也就是国家单一窗口，申报这一票。申报依据形式发票。录入的是各方、HS 编码、货值和原产地。这四项就是申报的内容。形式发票如果还是工作用的品名、临时货值，或最终发票不会采用的原产地，就不该拿来生成编号。
至少在开船前 48 小时申报。同一次申报最长可以提前到开船前 3 个月。这个窗口说的是开船，不是船到苏赫纳的那一天。早于 3 个月，超出这里写明的窗口。晚于开船前 48 小时，就错过这里写明的下限。48 小时从开船算，不要借另一个国家到港申报的 48 小时。
这一步由进口商申报，编号也是发给进口商的。中国的发货人可以把形式发票准备好，让各方、HS 编码、货值和原产地稳定下来。发货人不能在 NAFEZA 上代替埃及进口商。进口商还没有申报，出口商就没有 ACID 可印，哪怕出口单证看起来已经齐了。

body.text: 第 2 步：出口商在 CargoX

richText.text: 出口商，也就是中国的供应商，在 CargoX 开设公司账户。CargoX 是 NAFEZA 在出口商一侧的合作平台。账户必须经过核验，并且要就这一票与进口商关联。注册账户是免费的。核验收一次小额费用。本篇不写这个费用的金额。这里用的材料没有写金额。
埃及页用自己的说法写了同一道门：出口公司必须先在 CargoX 完成认证，再提交预先货物信息。出口商在那里提交的是提单、装箱单、商业发票（PDF 和规定格式的 Excel）以及原产地证。公司还没有通过核验，就不能做这项提交，哪怕单证草稿已经写好了。
第一次出运之前就办好经过核验的账户，不要等到编号下来的那一天。关联的是这个进口商和这一票，不是对以后每一票的长期许可。下一票是一个新的 ACID，也是一次新的关联。公司核验是收一次的那一步。货与货之间的关联不是。

body.text: 第 3 步：印上 19 位 ACID

richText.text: 海关批准申报后，NAFEZA 把 19 位 ACID 发给进口商，也发给出口商。把它印上去。用机打，不用手写。印在商业发票、装箱单、提单和原产地证上。编号如果只留在一封邮件里，或是手写在页边，就不算印在单证上。
出口商在开船前通过 CargoX 上传最终单据。最终，指的是已经机打上 ACID 的那套单证，不是编号还空着的早期草稿。上传的一套如果和 NAFEZA 里录入的各方、HS 编码、货值、原产地对不上，申报和单证就成了两票不同的货。
埃及页写了时间在目的港这边有什么用。预先货物信息申报得足够早，进口商才能走更快的放行通道。到港前几小时才提交，就享受不到。这句话说的是到港，它旁边还有已经写明的规则：进口商自己的申报至少在开船前 48 小时，最长提前 3 个月。本页不把这两句收成同一个门槛。NAFEZA 的申报落在它自己的窗口里，CargoX 的上传也不要留到船抵苏赫纳前的几小时。
ACID 按票发放。它不是进口商持有、可以反复使用的许可。下一票订舱，哪怕产品和买方都相同，也要自己的 19 位编号。每个编号的有效期有限。一个编号不再是这一票的有效编号时，把它印到一套新单证上也不会让它恢复。重新取得编号，再印那一个。
商业发票、装箱单、提单和原产地证上的机打编号必须相同。错一位就是另一个编号。埃及页写 ACID 必须出现在所有货运单证上。这是同一项要求的另一面：NAFEZA 发出来的编号，就是每一份单证上显示的编号，而不是只写在一封说明邮件里。

比较顺的做法，是开船前把三步做完。埃及进口商凭已经写明各方、HS 编码、货值和原产地的形式发票，在 NAFEZA 申报，至少提前到开船前 48 小时，最早不早于 3 个月。中国出口商有经过核验的 CargoX 账户，就这一票与该进口商关联；注册免费，核验收一次小额费用。批准之后，双方拿到同一个 19 位 ACID。把它机打在商业发票、装箱单、提单和原产地证上。出口商在开船前通过 CargoX 上传这些最终单据。发票要 PDF 和规定格式的 Excel，以及更快的放行通道，写在埃及页上。
把档案当成就绪之前，和清关伙伴核对 HS 编码。这个编号不决定产品能不能进口。它标识的是这一票的预先申报。本页不确认任何具体产品的 ACID。单证上没有这个编号，苏赫纳清不了关；埃及其他海运到港同样过不了这个缺口。
问：ACID 编号是什么？
答：ACID 是 Advance Cargo Information Declaration，预先货物信息申报。埃及海关按票签发一个 19 位编号。它不是通用进口许可。新的一票要新的编号，有效期有限。
问：进口商要在什么时候申报 ACID？
答：进口商在 NAFEZA 上至少于开船前 48 小时申报，最长可以提前 3 个月，依据是形式发票。海运进入埃及的货物自 2021 年 10 月起就要 ACID。空运自 2026 年 1 月起要。
问：这 19 位编号印在哪里？
答：海关批准后，NAFEZA 把 19 位 ACID 发给进口商和出口商。它要机打在商业发票、装箱单、提单和原产地证上，不能手写。出口商在开船前通过 CargoX 上传最终单据。
问：ACID 只用于苏赫纳吗？
答：不是。ACID 适用于所有海运进入埃及的货物，不只是苏赫纳。运往苏赫纳的单证上没有 ACID，苏赫纳就清不了关。

documents.title: Cape vs Suez: what it does to Red Sea rates
documents.description: The Cape and Suez are two different networks, not two prices for the same sailing. Here is how the routing choice reaches a Red Sea quote.
documents.lead: The Cape and Suez are two different networks, not two prices for the same sailing. Here is how the routing choice reaches a Red Sea quote.

body.text: Two networks, not two prices for one ship

richText.text: A container from China to Jeddah does not choose between the Cape and Suez the way a container to Rotterdam does. Jeddah is inside the Red Sea. The ship enters through Bab el-Mandeb either way. The Cape versus Suez decision belongs to the service network: carriers routing Asia–Europe vessels, repositioning capacity, and deciding which Red Sea ports get a direct call. That decision still reaches your quote, but through capacity and connections, not through a simple detour on your own box.

The Suez routing is the shorter path from Asia to Europe and to the Red Sea. The Cape routing sends the vessel around Africa. For a service that continues to Europe, the Cape adds distance, time and vessels. For a Red Sea destination, the visible effect is usually fewer direct calls, more transhipment and a schedule that is harder to keep. Both routings can appear in the same week, from different carriers, and neither is automatically the better product for your cargo.

body.text: Why a longer voyage absorbs capacity

richText.text: A ship is a fixed asset. If a round voyage takes two more weeks, the same vessel completes fewer voyages in a year. To keep a weekly service weekly, the carrier needs more ships or has to cut capacity somewhere. That is the first channel from routing to price: the longer voyage absorbs tonnage that would otherwise be available to carry cargo, including cargo to the Red Sea. The effect is not linear. One service changing its routing can tighten a specific port pair while another port pair stays loose.

Fuel, crew, insurance and port time rise with the extra distance. Carriers also lose the ability to rotate boxes as quickly, so empty containers can be in the wrong place. None of these costs is a fixed surcharge on every quote. They show up as a higher base rate, a space shortage, or a sailing that is full earlier than usual. That is why a rate can move even when your cargo, your supplier and your destination have not changed.

body.text: What Red Sea ports feel first

richText.text: Red Sea ports feel the routing change through their connections. A direct call is simple: one vessel, one port, one bill of lading. A transhipment adds a hub, a second vessel and a connection window. If the first vessel is late, the box waits at the hub. Jeddah, Jebel Ali, Djibouti, Colombo and Singapore can all appear as hubs, and each has a different cut-off, free time and cost.

That is why two quotes to the same port can look far apart. One is direct and includes a certain free time. The other tranships, uses a cheaper ocean rate, and pushes more cost to the destination. The ocean number alone does not tell you which product is cheaper for your cargo. Ask what the box actually does after it leaves the first vessel.
Direct: fewer handovers, usually faster, often less free time at destination.
Transhipment: lower ocean rate possible, one more connection risk, more local charges.
Ask which hub, which vessel and how long the connection is.

War-risk insurance is priced separately from ocean freight. Underwriters can treat the Red Sea up to a port as a risk area, and the carrier may pass a war-risk surcharge through. The surcharge can change faster than the base rate. It is not a sign that the base market has moved, and it may not apply to every carrier or every sailing. Read it as a separate line, not as part of the median.

Fuel and peak-season surcharges work the same way. Ask for a line-item quote: base ocean freight, origin charges, destination charges, war-risk, fuel, documentation, free time and validity. A single all-in number without those lines is hard to compare and easy to change after booking. The line that moves most is not always the line that matters most.

body.text: How to read a quote in a diverted market

richText.text: In a diverted market, read the routing before the number. Is the sailing direct or transhipped? Which hub? How many days is the connection? What is the free time at destination? Does the quote include war-risk? Is the space confirmed or subject to carrier approval? These questions matter more than a small difference in the ocean rate.

Then compare the total. Add origin charges, destination charges, inland trucking, customs and the cost of one extra week of transit. A cheaper ocean rate with a missed connection can cost more than a direct sailing that looked expensive on the first line. If the cargo is time-sensitive, the schedule is part of the price.

body.text: The schedule buffer is a cost you cannot see

richText.text: Published transit times already contain a buffer. A carrier that says 32 days may plan for 28 days of sailing and connection plus four days of recovery. In a diverted market the buffer gets longer, because the connection is less predictable, the hub is busier and the vessel can miss its window. The number on the quote is not a promise that the box will arrive on that day; it is the carrier's current planning allowance.

That buffer is a real cost for the shipper. If the cargo is for a promotion, a project or a production line, an extra week ties up working capital and may force air freight or a local purchase. If the consignee has a warehouse slot or a truck booked, a late arrival adds storage and rescheduling. A cheaper ocean rate with ten more days of transit can be the more expensive choice once those costs are counted.
Ask what the transit is measured from: loaded on board, departed, or arrived at the hub.
Ask for the connection window and the next sailing if it is missed.
Compare the arrival window, not only the fastest published day.
Put the cost of one extra week into the comparison.

body.text: What to do before you book

richText.text: If your cargo is ready now, ask for the next two sailings, not just the cheapest one. A sailing that leaves later but connects cleanly can arrive earlier. If your cargo is flexible, ask what changes in the following week; do not assume the direction will continue. A single week is a reading, not a trend.

The index on this site is a market reading, not a bookable offer. Use it to see the level and the sample size, then ask for a quote on your actual cargo, route and date. The routing question is part of that quote, not a separate research project.

items.text: What moves a Red Sea rate

richText.text: Q: Does every China–Red Sea container go around the Cape now?

A: No. A container whose destination is inside the Red Sea still enters through Bab el-Mandeb. The Cape is a choice for services that continue to Europe, or for carriers repositioning capacity. What changes for Red Sea cargo is often the number of direct calls and the amount of transhipment, not a single detour on your own box.
Q: Is the Cape route always more expensive?

A: Not as a simple rule. The longer voyage absorbs capacity and can raise the market, but a transhipment quote can be cheaper than a direct one on the same day. Compare the routing, the connection, the free time and the total cost, not the routing label alone.
Q: How much longer does the Cape take?

A: On Asia–Europe services, often one to two weeks, depending on the port pair. For a Red Sea destination, the effect is usually felt through connections and schedules rather than one published transit time. Ask for the routing on your quote.

documents.title: 好望角 vs 苏伊士：对红海运价的影响
documents.description: 好望角和苏伊士是两张不同的航线网络，不是同一班船的两种价格。这篇讲绕行如何传导到红海报价。
documents.lead: 好望角和苏伊士是两张不同的航线网络，不是同一班船的两种价格。这篇讲绕行如何传导到红海报价。

body.text: 两张网络，不是一条船的两种价格

richText.text: 从中国到吉达的柜子，不会像到鹿特丹的柜子那样直接在好望角和苏伊士之间二选一。吉达在红海里面，船最终都要从曼德海峡进入。好望角还是苏伊士，是船公司做亚洲—欧洲航线、调配运力和决定红海直挂港时的选择。这个选择会传导到你的报价，但靠的是运力和衔接，不是你的柜子单独绕一圈。
苏伊士是亚洲到欧洲、也是到红海的短路径。好望角让船绕非洲走。对继续去欧洲的航线，绕行增加距离、时间和船舶数量。对红海目的港，看得见的影响通常不是船直接绕行，而是直挂减少、中转增多、船期更难保证。同一周里，不同船公司可能同时给出两种走法；哪一种更适合你的货，不能只看名字。

body.text: 为什么更长的航程会吸走运力

richText.text: 船是固定资产。一个往返航次多出两周，同一艘船一年就跑不了那么多趟。要把周班维持成周班，船公司要么加船，要么在别处砍运力。这是航线影响价格的第一条通道：更长的航程吸走了原本可以运货的运力，包括运往红海的运力。影响不是线性的。一条航线改道，可能让某个港口组合变紧，另一个组合仍然宽松。
多出的距离带来燃油、船员、保险和港口时间。空箱周转也会变慢，箱子可能停在错误的地方。这些成本不会以一笔固定附加费出现在每份报价上，而是表现为更高的基础运价、更紧的舱位，或者比往常更早满舱的船。所以货没变、工厂没变、目的港没变，报价仍然会动。

body.text: 红海港口最先感受到什么

richText.text: 红海港口通过衔接感受到航线变化。直挂很简单：一条船、一个港、一份提单。中转多一个枢纽、第二条船和一个衔接窗口。第一程晚了，柜子就在枢纽等。吉达、杰贝阿里、吉布提、科伦坡和新加坡都可能成为枢纽，各自的截点、免柜期和费用不同。
所以同一个目的港的两份报价可能差很多。一份直航，含一定免柜期；另一份中转，海运费更低，但把更多成本推到目的港。只看海运费，判断不了哪个产品对你的货更便宜。要问清楚柜子离开第一条船之后到底怎么走。
直航：交接少，通常更快，目的港免柜期往往更短。
中转：海运费可能更低，多一个衔接风险，当地费用更多。
问清哪个枢纽、哪条船、衔接要等多久。

body.text: 战争风险、燃油和附加费

richText.text: 战争风险保险和海运费是分开计的。保险方可以把红海到某个港口划为风险区，船公司也可能把战争风险附加费转嫁出来。附加费比基础运价变得更快。它不代表基础市场动了，也不是每家船公司、每个航次都收。把它当一条独立费用看，不要混进中位数里。
燃油和旺季附加费也是这个逻辑。要分项报价：基础海运费、起运港费用、目的港费用、战争风险、燃油、单证、免柜期和有效期。只给一个总价，既难比较，也容易在订舱后变。变动最大的那一行，不一定是影响你决策最大的那一行。

body.text: 绕行市场里怎么看报价

richText.text: 在绕行市场里，先看航线，再看数字。直航还是中转？哪个枢纽？衔接几天？目的港免柜期多久？含不含战争风险？舱位是确认的还是待船公司批复？这些问题比海运费差几十美元更重要。
然后再比总成本。把起运港费用、目的港费用、内陆拖车、清关和多出来的一周时效都加进去。海运费便宜、但错过衔接的方案，可能比第一行看起来贵的直航更贵。货期紧的话，船期本身就是价格的一部分。

body.text: 船期缓冲：看不见的成本

richText.text: 公开的航程数字里已经带了缓冲。船公司写 32 天，可能实际按 28 天航行和衔接、再加 4 天恢复来排。绕行市场里缓冲会变长，因为衔接更难预测、枢纽更忙、船更容易错过窗口。报价上的数字不是“这天一定到”的承诺，而是船公司当前的计划余量。
这个缓冲对货主是实打实的成本。货是促销、项目或生产线用料，多一周就占资金，还可能被迫空运或当地采购。收货人订了仓、约了车，晚到就多仓储和改期费。海运费便宜、时效多十天，把这些算进去，往往是更贵的选择。
问清航程从哪天算：装船、开航，还是到枢纽。
问衔接窗口，以及错过后的下一班船。
比到货窗口，不要只比最快的那一天。
把多一周的成本放进比较里。
货已经好了，就问最近两班船，不要只问最便宜的那班。晚开但衔接顺的船，可能更早到。货期灵活，就问下周会有什么变化；不要假设涨跌会延续。一周只是一个读数，不是趋势。
本站指数是市场读数，不是可订舱报价。用它看水平和样本量，再按你的实际货物、航线和日期询价。航线问题应该包含在这份报价里，而不是另做一个研究项目。

items.text: 哪些因素影响红海运价

richText.text: 问：现在中国到红海的柜子都绕好望角吗？
答：不是。目的港在红海里面的柜子，最终仍从曼德海峡进入。好望角是继续去欧洲的航线、或者船公司调配运力时的选择。对红海货来说，变的通常是直挂数量和转船比例，不是你的柜子单独绕一圈。
问：绕好望角一定更贵吗？
答：不能这么简单判断。更长的航程会吸走运力、抬高市场，但同一天里中转报价也可能比直航便宜。要比航线、衔接、免柜期和总成本，不能只看“绕行”两个字。
问：走好望角要多多久？
答：亚洲到欧洲的航线，通常多一到两周，具体看港口组合。对红海目的港，影响更多体现在衔接和船期上，而不是一个统一的航程数字。询价时直接问走哪条航线。

documents.title: FCL vs LCL to the Red Sea: which fits?
documents.description: FCL and LCL are different products with different cost lines. Compare them on total cost, handling and transit, not on the ocean freight alone.
documents.lead: FCL and LCL are different products with different cost lines. Compare them on total cost, handling and transit, not on the ocean freight alone.

richText.text: FCL means one shipper uses a whole container. LCL means several shippers share a container, and the forwarder consolidates the cargo at a warehouse. FCL is usually the better fit when the cargo fills a container, is heavy, fragile, high-value or time-sensitive. LCL is usually the better fit when the cargo is small and the destination charges are understood.

The mistake is comparing only the ocean freight. LCL often wins on the first line and loses on the total, because the destination charges are spread over a small volume. FCL often looks expensive on the first line and becomes competitive once you count the cargo volume and the handling.

LCL is billed per W/M: the larger of cubic metres and metric tonnes. If 3 CBM weighs 2 tonnes, the charge is 3 W/M. If 3 CBM weighs 4 tonnes, the charge is 4 W/M. There is usually a minimum of 1 W/M. The ocean freight is only one line; the forwarder also charges for origin CFS, documentation, destination CFS, customs and delivery.

Because the box is shared, the forwarder has to wait for every shipper's cargo before it can close the container. One late supplier can delay the whole group. The destination warehouse also has to separate the cargo and release it, which adds time and handling compared with a single container.
Billed on W/M, minimum 1 W/M.
Origin CFS, documentation and destination CFS add lines.
Consolidation waits for the last cargo in the group.

FCL is priced per container, not per CBM. A 20GP, 40GP or 40HQ has its own ocean freight, origin charges, destination charges and free time. Once you pay for the container, the marginal cost of filling it with more cargo is low, as long as you stay within the payload and the destination rules.

FCL also gives you control of the box. You can load at your factory or warehouse, seal it, and track one unit. The consignee gets one container, one delivery order and one set of destination charges. That simplicity is part of what you pay for.

Start with the cargo: volume, weight, package count and whether it can be stacked. Then add the destination. A 5 CBM LCL shipment to Jeddah may look cheap on the ocean line, but the destination CFS, documentation and delivery can make a small FCL or a different routing more attractive. The same 5 CBM to a port with fewer LCL services may have no good LCL option at all.

Also count the time cost. LCL adds consolidation and destination separation. If the cargo is for a project, a promotion or a production line, a week of extra handling can cost more than the freight difference. If the cargo is slow-moving and the warehouse can wait, LCL's lower first line may be worth it.
Volume above roughly 15 CBM: price FCL first.
Heavy cargo: check payload before comparing per-CBM prices.
High value, fragile or time-sensitive: FCL usually reduces handling risk.
Small cargo: compare LCL total including destination CFS.

A direct FCL sailing is usually the shortest and simplest. LCL may route through a consolidation hub, and the connection can add days. The cargo also moves through more hands: origin warehouse, container freight station, vessel, destination CFS, then delivery. Each handover is a chance for a delay or a document mismatch.

That does not make LCL unreliable. It makes the schedule less direct. If you need a specific arrival date, ask for the actual routing and the cut-off at the CFS, not only the vessel's ETD. If you need one supplier's cargo isolated, FCL is the cleaner choice.

body.text: The 15 CBM rule, and when it fails

richText.text: A common rule of thumb is to price FCL once the cargo passes roughly 15 CBM. Below 10 CBM, LCL is usually the place to start. Between 10 and 15 CBM, the answer depends on density, destination charges and how much handling the cargo can take. The rule is a starting point, not a tariff boundary.

Density breaks the rule first. Twelve CBM of machinery at nine tonnes is not the same shipment as twelve CBM of cartons at two tonnes. The heavy cargo may hit a 20GP payload limit, while the light cargo leaves most of the container empty by weight. Palletised cargo breaks it again: pallets waste height and floor space, so the usable CBM is lower than the carton count suggests. A 20GP may hold fewer pallets than the arithmetic says.

Destination breaks it second. LCL needs a consolidation service and a destination CFS. Jeddah, Sokhna, Aqaba and Djibouti have regular LCL options; Port Sudan has fewer, and the routing may be longer. The destination CFS charge is also spread over your small volume, so a 3 CBM shipment can carry a disproportionate share of the handling cost. Always ask for the destination CFS, documentation and delivery as separate lines.
Under 10 CBM and not urgent: price LCL first.
10–15 CBM: compare both totals, including destination CFS.
Over 15 CBM or over 15 tonnes: price FCL first.
Palletised or high-value cargo: count the handling risk, not only the freight.

Write down the volume, gross weight, package dimensions, cargo value, ready date and consignee address. Then ask for two quotes: one FCL with the right container, one LCL with the destination charges itemised. Compare the total delivered cost and the transit, not the ocean line alone.

If the two totals are close, choose the option with fewer handovers and clearer free time. If LCL is much cheaper and the cargo is not time-sensitive, LCL can be the right answer. The goal is not to pick a label; it is to pick the cost structure that fits the cargo.
Q: Is LCL cheaper for 5 CBM?

A: Often the ocean freight is lower, but the total may not be. LCL adds destination CFS handling, documentation and consolidation time, and those charges can be large relative to 5 CBM. Compare the door-to-door total, not just the freight line.
Q: Can I ship less than 1 CBM?

A: Yes, but LCL is billed on the larger of cubic metres or metric tonnes, with a minimum of 1 W/M. A small shipment still pays for at least 1 W/M plus destination charges. Ask for the minimum charge before you decide.
Q: Is FCL always faster?

A: Usually it has fewer handovers, but the sailing and routing still decide. A direct FCL sailing can beat a transhipped LCL; a delayed FCL can lose to a clean LCL connection. Compare the actual schedule, not the label.

documents.title: 整柜还是拼箱：红海出货怎么选？
documents.description: 整柜和拼箱是两种产品，费用结构也不同。比较时要看总成本、操作和时效，不能只看海运费。
documents.lead: 整柜和拼箱是两种产品，费用结构也不同。比较时要看总成本、操作和时效，不能只看海运费。

richText.text: 整柜是一个货主用一个柜子；拼箱是几个货主共用一个柜子，由货代在仓库集拼。货量接近整柜、货重、易碎、高价值或时效紧，通常选整柜。货量小、并且已经算清目的港费用，拼箱才更合适。
最常见的错误是只比海运费。拼箱常常在第一行赢，在总成本输，因为目的港费用摊在小体积上。整柜常常第一行看起来贵，把货量和操作算进去后才有可比性。
拼箱按 W/M 计费：立方米和公吨取较大值。3 立方米、2 吨，按 3 W/M；3 立方米、4 吨，按 4 W/M。通常最低 1 W/M。海运费只是一行，货代还会收起运港拼箱费、单证费、目的港拆箱费、清关和派送。
柜子是共用的，货代要等所有货主的货到齐才能封柜。一个供应商晚了，整组都晚。目的港仓库还要分货、放货，比整柜多一道操作和时间。
按 W/M 计费，最低 1 W/M。
起运港拼箱、单证和目的港拆箱都会另计。
集拼要等整组最后一票货到齐。
整柜按柜计费，不按立方米。20GP、40GP、40HQ 各有自己的海运费、起运港费用、目的港费用和免柜期。付了一个柜子的钱，只要不超载、不违反目的港规定，多装一点货的边际成本很低。
整柜还把柜子交给你控制。可以在工厂或仓库装柜、加封，按一个单位跟踪。收货人拿到一个柜子、一份提货单和一套目的港费用。这种简单性本身就是你付的钱的一部分。
先看货：体积、重量、件数、能不能叠。再看目的港。5 立方米到吉达，海运费那一行可能很便宜，但目的港拆箱、单证和派送加起来，可能让一个小柜或另一种走法更划算。同样是 5 立方米，去拼箱服务少的目的港，可能根本没有好的拼箱选择。
还要算时间成本。拼箱多出集拼和目的港分货。货是项目货、促销货或生产线用料，多一周操作可能比运费差更贵。货不急、仓库也能等，拼箱第一行更低才有意义。
体积大约超过 15 立方米：先问整柜。
货重：先看载重，再比每立方米价格。
高价值、易碎、时效紧：整柜通常减少操作风险。
小货：拼箱要把目的港拆箱费算进总成本。
直航整柜通常最短、最简单。拼箱可能经集拼枢纽，衔接会多几天。货经过的手也更多：起运仓、拼箱站、船、目的港拆箱站、再派送。每次交接都可能带来延误或单证不一致。
这不是说拼箱不可靠，而是船期没那么直接。要有明确到货日，就问实际航线和拼箱站的截货时间，不要只问船的 ETD。要把一个供应商的货单独隔开，整柜更干净。

body.text: 15 立方米经验法则，以及它什么时候不成立

richText.text: 一个常见的经验法则是：货量超过大约 15 立方米，就开始问整柜。低于 10 立方米，通常先从拼箱问起。10 到 15 立方米之间，答案取决于货重、目的港费用和货物能承受多少操作。这个法则是起点，不是运价分界线。
最先打破法则的是货重。12 立方米、9 吨的机械，和 12 立方米、2 吨的纸箱，不是同一种货。重货可能碰到 20GP 的载重上限；轻货则重量远没到、柜里大半是空的。托盘货又会改写一次：托盘浪费高度和地面，实际可用容积比纸箱数量算出来的少。20GP 能装的托盘数，可能比算术结果少。
第二个打破法则的是目的港。拼箱要有集拼服务和目的港拆箱站。吉达、苏赫纳、亚喀巴和吉布提有常规拼箱；苏丹港选择更少，航线也可能更长。目的港拆箱费还摊在你的小体积上，3 立方米的货可能承担了不成比例的操作成本。一定要让对方把目的港拆箱、单证和派送分开列。
10 立方米以下、不急：先问拼箱。
10–15 立方米：两边总价都比，含目的港拆箱。
超过 15 立方米或 15 吨：先问整柜。
托盘货或高价值货：算操作风险，不只算运费。
先写下体积、毛重、包装尺寸、货值、备货日期和收货地址。然后要两份报价：一份对应柜型的整柜，一份把目的港费用拆开的拼箱。比总到门成本和时效，不要只比海运费。
两个总价接近，就选交接少、免柜期更清楚的那个。拼箱明显便宜、货又不急，拼箱就是正确答案。目标不是选一个标签，而是选适合这批货的费用结构。
问：5 立方米走拼箱更便宜吗？
答：海运费通常更低，但总成本不一定。拼箱多出目的港拆箱、单证和集拼时间，这些费用相对 5 立方米可能不低。要比门到门总成本，不要只比海运费那一行。
问：不足 1 立方米能走吗？
答：可以，但拼箱按立方米与公吨中较大值计费，最低 1 W/M。货再小，也至少按 1 W/M 加目的港费用计。先问清最低收费再决定。
问：整柜一定更快吗？
答：通常交接更少，但还是要看船期和航线。直航整柜可能快过中转拼箱；延误的整柜也可能输给衔接顺的拼箱。比实际船期，不要只比标签。

documents.title: 20GP, 40GP or 40HQ: which container?
documents.description: 20GP, 40GP and 40HQ carry different volumes and weights. Choose by cargo density, pallets, inland limits and equipment, not by the lowest ocean rate.
documents.lead: 20GP, 40GP and 40HQ carry different volumes and weights. Choose by cargo density, pallets, inland limits and equipment, not by the lowest ocean rate.

body.text: The three boxes at a glance

richText.text: The three dry containers use the same width and length family but different heights and volumes. A 20GP is about 33 CBM. A 40GP is about 67 CBM. A 40HQ is about 76 CBM, with the extra height coming from the high-cube design. Payload is typically in the mid-to-high twenties of tonnes, but the carrier's limit and the road limit at destination decide what you can actually load.

Those numbers are planning figures, not a guarantee. Container weights and internal dimensions vary by manufacturer, and a carrier can impose a lower payload for a specific route or road. Use them to choose a direction, then confirm the exact limit with the carrier before you load.
20GP: about 33 CBM, for dense cargo.
40GP: about 67 CBM, for voluminous cargo that fits standard height.
40HQ: about 76 CBM, for light and voluminous cargo, pallets and taller cargo.

The 20GP is the smallest of the three and the usual choice for dense cargo: tiles, hardware, machinery parts, bagged material and other freight that reaches the weight limit before it fills the volume. Its ocean freight per container is often lower, and it is easier to move on roads with tight weight limits.

The trade-off is cost per CBM. If the cargo is light and bulky, a 20GP fills up long before it reaches its payload, and you pay for a container that is mostly air. In that case, a 40GP or 40HQ usually lowers the cost per cubic metre, even if the ocean freight line is higher.

The 40GP is the standard-height forty-foot box. It roughly doubles the volume of a 20GP without the extra height of a high cube. It suits cargo that is voluminous but not tall: cartons, furniture parts, appliances and mixed pallets that stay below the standard internal height.

Some carriers have fewer 40GP boxes than 40HQ boxes, especially on Red Sea services. If the cargo fits a 40GP, ask for both 40GP and 40HQ rates. The 40HQ may be easier to find and only slightly more expensive, while the 40GP may be cheaper when it is available.

The 40HQ is a high-cube forty-foot container. It has the same footprint as a 40GP but more internal height, which brings the volume to about 76 CBM. It is the usual choice for light, voluminous cargo, palletised goods and cartons that would otherwise leave a 40GP half empty by weight.

The extra height is not free everywhere. Inland bridges, tunnels, warehouse doors and some truck chassis can limit a high cube after it leaves the port. If the consignee's delivery point has a low door or a restrictive road, a 40GP may be the safer choice even if the 40HQ is cheaper on the ocean.

Start with the cargo volume and gross weight. If the cargo is dense, price a 20GP first. If it is light and bulky, price a 40HQ first. If it is in between, price both a 40GP and a 40HQ. Then add the pallet count and the internal height: a pallet that is too tall for a standard container can force a high cube, even when the volume is small.

Finally, check equipment and inland limits. A cheap rate for a container that is not available at your origin, or cannot be delivered at destination, is not a real option. Ask the carrier or forwarder about both before you book.
Dense cargo: 20GP first, then compare cost per CBM.
Light and bulky: 40HQ first, then 40GP.
Tall pallets or cargo: check internal height before choosing.
Inland delivery: check door height and road limits.

The container's volume is only half the choice. Each box also has a tare weight, and the tare is larger on a forty-foot container than on a 20GP. That matters for dense cargo: a 20GP can often carry more cargo tonnes than a 40HQ because the box itself weighs less and the axle load is spread differently. The carrier's payload limit and the road limit at destination decide the real number, not the container's nominal capacity.

Most destinations limit gross vehicle weight, and some also limit axle weight. A 40HQ loaded to its nominal payload can be legal on the ship and illegal on the road. The trucker may need a permit, a different chassis or a split delivery. Inland bridges and seasonal road restrictions can tighten the limit further. If the cargo is dense, price a 20GP first and confirm the payload with the carrier and the trucker in writing.

The shipper also has a legal obligation to provide a verified gross mass (VGM) before the container is loaded. Guessing the weight or using the booking weight is not enough. Weigh the packed container or use an approved method, and keep the figure consistent with the documents. A misdeclared weight can stop the box at the terminal or create a safety issue on the road.
Dense cargo: compare payload, not only CBM.
Check the road limit at the delivery address.
Confirm the carrier's payload limit for the route.
Provide a verified gross mass before loading.

The site's index uses 40HQ because it is the common container for light cargo on this trade. That does not mean 40HQ is always the right box for your cargo. The country pages show 20GP and 40HQ medians by origin where quotes exist, and the route pages show the equipment behind each lane.

At Jeddah, Sokhna, Aqaba, Djibouti and Port Sudan, the destination charges and free time can differ by container type. A 20GP may have a lower terminal handling charge, while a 40HQ may have a lower cost per CBM. Ask for the destination charges by container, not one blended number.
Q: Which container is cheapest?

A: A 20GP often has the lowest ocean freight per container, but not necessarily the lowest cost per CBM. A 40HQ usually carries more than twice the volume of a 20GP for a smaller premium. Compare cost per cubic metre and the total cargo, not the container price alone.
Q: Can I load 28 tonnes in a 40HQ?

A: The container may be rated for it, but the road limit and the carrier's payload limit decide. Many destinations restrict gross vehicle weight, and a 40HQ is heavier than a 20GP. Confirm the payload with the carrier and the trucker before you plan a dense load.
Q: Is a 40HQ always available?

A: No. Equipment varies by port and week. A 40HQ can be scarce when a lot of light cargo is moving, and a 20GP can be scarce when dense cargo is moving. Ask about equipment when you ask for the rate, especially if your cargo-ready date is tight.

documents.title: 20GP、40GP、40HQ：红海出货选哪种柜？
documents.description: 20GP、40GP、40HQ 的容积和载重不同。选柜要看货重、托盘、内陆限高和箱源，不能只看最低海运费。
documents.lead: 20GP、40GP、40HQ 的容积和载重不同。选柜要看货重、托盘、内陆限高和箱源，不能只看最低海运费。

richText.text: 三种干柜的宽度和长度体系相同，高度和容积不同。20GP 大约 33 立方米，40GP 大约 67 立方米，40HQ 大约 76 立方米，多出来的是高柜的高度。载重通常在二十多吨的中上段，但真正能装多少，要看船公司限制和目的港公路限重。
这些数字是计划用的，不是保证值。不同制造商的内尺寸和自重会有差异，船公司也可能对某条航线或公路给出更低载重。用它们判断方向，装柜前再和船公司确认具体限制。
20GP：约 33 立方米，适合重货。
40GP：约 67 立方米，适合体积货、且高度不超标准柜。
40HQ：约 76 立方米，适合轻货、体积货、托盘和较高的货。
20GP 是三者里最小的，通常给重货：瓷砖、五金、机械配件、袋装料，以及其他先到重量上限、后到容积上限的货。它的每柜海运费往往更低，在限重紧的公路上也更好安排。
代价是每立方米成本。货轻、体积大，20GP 很快就装满，但离载重上限还很远，等于为一个大部分是空气的柜子付钱。这种情况用 40GP 或 40HQ，通常能把每立方米成本拉低，哪怕海运费那一行更高。
40GP 是标准高度的四十尺柜。容积大约是 20GP 的两倍，但没有高柜多出来的高度。适合体积大、但不算高的货：纸箱、家具部件、家电，以及高度不超过标准柜内高的混合托盘。
有些船公司的 40GP 箱源比 40HQ 少，红海航线尤其如此。货能装 40GP，就同时问 40GP 和 40HQ 的价。40HQ 可能更好找、只贵一点；40GP 有箱时可能更便宜。
40HQ 是高柜四十尺。底面和 40GP 一样，内部更高，容积大约 76 立方米。轻货、体积货、托盘货，以及装 40GP 会“重量没满、体积先满”的纸箱货，通常选它。
多出来的高度不是在哪里都能用。内陆桥梁、隧道、仓库门，以及某些拖车底盘，都可能在离开港口后限制高柜。收货人的卸货点门矮、道路有限制，哪怕 40HQ 海运费更便宜，40GP 也可能更稳。
先看体积和毛重。货重，先问 20GP；货轻、体积大，先问 40HQ；介于两者之间，40GP 和 40HQ 都问。然后加托盘数量和货高：托盘太高、标准柜进不去，哪怕体积不大，也只能用高柜。
最后看箱源和内陆限制。起运港没箱、或者目的港送不到的柜型，再便宜也不是真选项。订舱前把这两件事一起问掉。
重货：先看 20GP，再比每立方米成本。
轻货、体积货：先看 40HQ，再看 40GP。
高托盘或高货：先核对内高再选柜。
内陆派送：核对门高和道路限制。
容积只是选择的一半。每个柜子还有自重，四十尺的自重比 20GP 大。这对重货很关键：20GP 往往能比 40HQ 多装货吨，因为柜子本身更轻、轴荷分布也不同。真正能装多少，由船公司载重限制和目的港公路限重决定，不是柜子的名义容量。
多数目的港限制车货总重，有些还限制轴重。40HQ 装到名义载重，可能在船上合法、在公路上超限。拖车可能要办许可、换底盘，或者分车送。内陆桥梁和季节性道路限制还会把上限压得更低。货重的话，先问 20GP，并让船公司和拖车书面确认可载重量。
发货人还有一项法定义务：集装箱装船前要提供核实总重（VGM）。估重量、拿订舱重量顶替都不行。要称重，或者用经批准的方法计算，并保证和单证一致。重量申报不实，可能在码头被拦，也会带来公路安全风险。
重货：比载重，不只比容积。
核对送货地址的公路限重。
确认船公司对该航线的载重限制。
装船前提供核实总重。
本站指数用 40HQ，是因为它是这条航线上轻货的常用柜型。这不代表你的货一定该用 40HQ。目的港页面按起运港列出 20GP 和 40HQ 的中位数（有报价时），路线页面则显示每条航线对应的柜型数据。
在吉达、苏赫纳、亚喀巴、吉布提和苏丹港，目的港费用和免柜期可能按柜型不同。20GP 的码头操作费可能更低，40HQ 的每立方米成本可能更低。要让对方按柜型列目的港费用，不要给一个混在一起的总数。
问：哪种柜最便宜？
答：20GP 的每柜海运费通常最低，但每立方米成本不一定最低。40HQ 的容积通常是 20GP 的两倍多，溢价却没有两倍。要比每立方米成本和整票货，不要只比每柜价格。
问：40HQ 能装 28 吨吗？
答：柜子本身可能允许，但公路限重和船公司载重限制才算数。很多目的港限制车货总重，40HQ 自重也比 20GP 大。装重货前先和船公司、拖车确认可载重量。
问：40HQ 一定有箱吗？
