答：不一定。箱源随港口和星期变化。轻货多的时候 40HQ 会紧，重货多的时候 20GP 会紧。询价时一起问箱源，货期紧尤其要问。

documents.title: DDP vs DAP to the Red Sea: what is included?
documents.description: DAP leaves import clearance and duty with the buyer. DDP puts them on the seller. The difference is who owns the import file, not just who pays the tax.
documents.lead: DAP leaves import clearance and duty with the buyer. DDP puts them on the seller. The difference is who owns the import file, not just who pays the tax.

richText.text: DAP and DDP are both delivery terms. Under DAP, the seller delivers the goods to the named place and the buyer handles import clearance and pays duty and VAT. Under DDP, the seller delivers to the named place and also handles import clearance and pays duty and VAT. The delivery point can be the same; the difference is who owns the import file and the tax liability.

That difference is bigger than it sounds. Import clearance needs an importer of record, a tax registration, a broker and a document set that matches the destination rules. A seller who can move cargo to the port may not be able to clear it. A DDP price that ignores this is not a complete DDP price.

A real door price starts with the cargo and ends at a named address. In between: origin pickup or factory loading, export declaration, origin charges, ocean freight, destination terminal handling, documentation, customs broker, duty, VAT, any inspection, inland trucking, insurance and the free time before demurrage or detention starts. Each line can be in or out of the quote.

Ask for the quote by line, not as one number. The same door price can hide very different assumptions: a terminal inside the port versus a warehouse three hours inland, a 20GP versus a 40HQ, a direct sailing versus a transhipment, or a free time of 7 days versus 14. The lines tell you what you are actually buying.
Ocean freight and origin charges.
Destination terminal handling and documentation.
Customs broker, duty, VAT and inspection.
Inland trucking to the named place.
Insurance, demurrage, detention and storage.

body.text: Why DDP is not just free delivery

richText.text: DDP means the seller takes on the import side. That requires an importer of record, a tax registration, a broker and a compliance file. In Saudi Arabia, the file may need SABER; in Egypt, ACID; in Djibouti, ECTN; in Sudan, ACD and SSMO. The seller also has to fund the duty and VAT before the buyer pays.

Those obligations are why a DDP quote can be higher than a DAP quote even when the duty is the same. The seller is pricing a service, a compliance risk and a cash-flow cost. If the seller cannot legally be the importer, the DDP quote may rely on a local broker, and the broker's name and responsibility should be written into the quote.

body.text: What DAP leaves with the buyer

richText.text: Under DAP, the seller delivers to the named place, but the buyer is the importer. The buyer needs the import registration, the broker, the duty and VAT, and the destination documents. The seller's job ends at delivery; unloading and import clearance are on the buyer's side.

DAP is often the cleaner choice when the consignee already imports regularly and has a broker. It keeps the import file with the party who knows the product and the local rules. It also avoids a foreign seller pretending to be a local importer. The trade-off is that the buyer carries the duty and the clearance risk.

Saudi Arabia: SABER shipment certificate, a commercial invoice and bill of lading that match, and duty plus VAT at import. Egypt: ACID before sailing, and the number must appear on the documents. Jordan: a customs declaration through the Jordanian portal and the right product documents. Djibouti: ECTN for containers unloaded there, with an exemption for direct transit to Ethiopia when the bill of lading says so. Sudan: ACD before loading, plus SSMO and an import licence for most goods.

The country page for each destination lists the documents and the taxes we have checked. Read it before you ask for a DDP price, because the answer changes by destination. A DDP quote for Jeddah is not a template for Sokhna, and a DAP quote for Djibouti is not a template for Port Sudan.

Build the comparison as a worksheet, not a single number. List the goods value, international freight, insurance, origin charges, destination port charges, duty, VAT, broker, inland delivery and a contingency for storage or demurrage. Next to each line, write who pays under DAP and who pays under DDP. The totals are only comparable when every line has an owner.

The VAT line is where many comparisons go wrong. A seller who is not registered in the destination may not be able to recover the VAT it pays on import, so the tax becomes a real cost inside the DDP price. A local buyer with a tax registration may recover it. The same duty and VAT can therefore produce different economics for the two parties. Ask whether the quote assumes recovery, and who holds the registration.

The HS code and the declared value drive both duty and VAT. A DDP quote based on a different code, a lower value or a different product description is not comparable, even if the delivery address is the same. Keep one commercial invoice and one classification for both quotes, and put the assumed code in writing.
Goods, freight and insurance.
Origin and destination charges.
Duty, VAT and the recovery assumption.
Broker, inland delivery and contingency.

body.text: How to compare DDP and DAP quotes

richText.text: Put the same cargo, the same named place and the same Incoterms version in front of both quotes. Check the HS code, the declared value, the importer of record, the duty and VAT treatment, the broker, the free time and the validity. A DDP quote with a different HS code or a different delivery address is not comparable.

If you are the buyer and you already have a broker, ask for DAP and compare it with your own duty estimate. If you are the seller and you do not have a local importer, do not promise DDP until the broker and the importer of record are confirmed in writing. The cheapest quote is the one that does not surprise you at destination.
Q: Is DDP always cheaper than DAP?

A: No. DDP moves the import clearance, duty and VAT into the seller's price, and the seller may add a margin for the risk and the cash flow. DAP can be cheaper on the invoice while the buyer pays the same duty and VAT locally. Compare the total landed cost, not the quoted number alone.
Q: Can a foreign seller be the importer of record?

A: Not automatically. Many Red Sea markets require a local importer, a tax registration or a licensed broker to clear the goods. A DDP quote only works if the seller has that entity or a broker who can act for it. Confirm the importer of record before you agree to DDP.
Q: Does DAP include duty?

A: No. Under DAP, the seller delivers to the named place, but the buyer handles import clearance and pays duty, VAT and any destination charges. The seller's price should include the transport to that place, not the import taxes.

documents.title: DDP 与 DAP：红海到门成本怎么算？
documents.description: DAP 由买方负责进口清关和税费，DDP 由卖方负责。差别不只是谁付税，而是谁承担进口申报责任。
documents.lead: DAP 由买方负责进口清关和税费，DDP 由卖方负责。差别不只是谁付税，而是谁承担进口申报责任。

richText.text: DAP 和 DDP 都是交货条款。DAP 下，卖方把货送到指定地点，买方负责进口清关并支付关税和增值税。DDP 下，卖方送到指定地点，同时负责进口清关并支付关税和增值税。交货点可以一样，差别在于谁承担进口申报和税负。
这个差别比听起来大。进口清关需要进口申报主体、税号、报关行，以及一套符合目的国规则的单证。能把货运到港口的卖方，不一定能清关。忽略这一点的 DDP 报价，不是完整的 DDP 报价。
真正的到门价格从货开始，到指定地址结束。中间包括：起运地提货或工厂装柜、出口申报、起运港费用、海运费、目的港码头操作、单证、报关行、关税、增值税、可能的查验、内陆拖车、保险，以及免柜期结束前的仓储。每一行都可能含或不合。
要分项报价，不要一个总数。同样的到门价可能藏着完全不同的假设：港区堆场还是三小时外的仓库、20GP 还是 40HQ、直航还是中转、7 天还是 14 天免柜期。分项才看得出你买的是什么。
海运费和起运港费用。
目的港码头操作和单证。
报关行、关税、增值税和查验。
到指定地点的内陆拖车。
保险、滞箱、滞港和仓储。
DDP 意味着卖方接下进口端。要有进口申报主体、税号、报关行和一套合规文件。沙特可能要做 SABER，埃及要 ACID，吉布提要 ECTN，苏丹要 ACD 和 SSMO。卖方还要在买方付款前先垫关税和增值税。
这些义务就是为什么关税一样，DDP 报价也可能高于 DAP。卖方报的是服务、合规风险和资金占用。卖方不能合法做进口商时，DDP 可能依赖当地报关行；报关行是谁、承担什么责任，应该写进报价。
DAP 下，卖方送到指定地点，但买方是进口商。买方要有进口登记、报关行、关税和增值税，以及目的港单证。卖方的工作到交货为止；卸货和进口清关在买方这边。
收货人本来就经常进口、也有报关行，DAP 往往更干净。进口文件留在熟悉产品和当地规则的一方，也避免外国卖方硬做当地进口商。代价是买方承担税费和清关风险。
沙特：SABER 货物证书，商业发票和提单要一致，进口时缴关税和增值税。埃及：开船前办 ACID，编号要出现在单证上。约旦：通过约旦门户报关，并备好产品文件。吉布提：在当地卸货的集装箱要 ECTN；直接转运埃塞俄比亚且提单写明的可免。苏丹：装船前办 ACD，多数商品还要 SSMO 和进口许可证。
每个目的港页面都列了我们核对过的单证和税费。问 DDP 价之前先看，因为答案随目的港变。吉达的 DDP 报价不能套到苏赫纳，吉布提的 DAP 报价也不能套到苏丹港。

items.text: 吉布提：ECTN 与埃塞转运

richText.text: 比较要做成工作表，不要只放一个数字。列出货值、国际运费、保险、起运港费用、目的港费用、关税、增值税、报关行、内陆派送，以及一笔仓储或滞箱的预备金。每一行旁边写清 DAP 下谁付、DDP 下谁付。每一行都有归属，总数才可比。
增值税这一行最容易比错。卖方在目的国没有税号，进口时交的增值税可能退不回来，这笔税就成了 DDP 价格里的真实成本。当地买方有税号，可能可以抵扣。同样的关税和增值税，对两方的经济效果不同。要问报价是否假设可抵扣，以及税号在谁名下。
HS 编码和申报货值同时决定关税和增值税。DDP 报价如果用了不同编码、更低货值或不同品名，哪怕送货地址一样，也不能直接比。两份报价用同一份商业发票、同一个归类，并把假设的编码写下来。
货值、运费和保险。
起运港和目的港费用。
关税、增值税及抵扣假设。
报关行、内陆派送和预备金。

body.text: DDP 和 DAP 怎么比

richText.text: 两份报价要用同一票货、同一个指定地点、同一版 Incoterms。核对 HS 编码、申报货值、进口申报主体、关税和增值税处理、报关行、免柜期和有效期。HS 编码或送货地址不同的 DDP 报价，不能直接比。
你是买方、已经有报关行，就要 DAP，再和你自己的税费估算比。你是卖方、没有当地进口主体，就不要在报关行和进口申报主体书面确认前承诺 DDP。最好的报价，是到了目的港不给你惊喜的那份。
问：DDP 一定比 DAP 便宜吗？
答：不一定。DDP 把进口清关、关税和增值税放进卖方价格，卖方可能为风险和垫资加一层利润。DAP 的发票价可能更低，但买方要在当地付同样的关税和增值税。要比总到岸成本，不能只比报价数字。
问：外国卖方能做进口申报主体吗？
答：不一定。红海很多市场要求当地进口商、税号或持牌报关行才能清关。DDP 报价只有在卖方有当地主体、或者有能代其申报的报关行时才成立。同意 DDP 前先确认进口申报主体是谁。
问：DAP 含关税吗？
答：不含。DAP 下卖方送到指定地点，但进口清关、关税、增值税和目的港费用由买方负责。卖方价格应包含送到该地点的运输，不包含进口税费。

documents.title: Dangerous goods and batteries to the Red Sea
documents.description: Batteries and dangerous goods need a carrier approval, the right UN number and documents before booking. Red Sea transhipment adds another check.
documents.lead: Batteries and dangerous goods need a carrier approval, the right UN number and documents before booking. Red Sea transhipment adds another check.

body.text: Why it is a separate booking

richText.text: Dangerous goods are not a normal container booking with an extra fee. They are a separate acceptance process under the IMDG Code. The carrier has to approve the UN number, the packing, the quantity and the route. The vessel has to be allowed to carry the class, and the transhipment port has to accept it. Any one of those can say no.

That is why a dangerous goods quote can take longer than a general cargo quote. The forwarder cannot confirm space until the carrier has the DG file. If you book first and declare later, the carrier can reject the container at the gate, and the cargo may sit while you look for another vessel.

Lithium-ion and lithium-metal batteries have different UN numbers depending on how they are packed. A battery shipped alone is not the same as a battery packed with equipment or contained in equipment. The UN number on the declaration has to match the actual packing, not the product's marketing name.

Other dangerous goods have their own classes and UN numbers: flammables, corrosives, oxidisers, aerosols, chemicals, vehicles and machinery with fuel or batteries. The class decides the packing, the label, the segregation and the carrier's acceptance. Do not guess the class from the product name.
UN3480: lithium-ion batteries shipped alone.
UN3481: lithium-ion batteries packed with or contained in equipment.
UN3090: lithium-metal batteries shipped alone.
UN3091: lithium-metal batteries packed with or contained in equipment.

body.text: The documents the carrier will ask for

richText.text: A typical lithium battery file includes the MSDS, the UN38.3 test summary, a dangerous goods declaration, a packing certificate, the commercial invoice and packing list, and the carrier's DG booking approval. The declaration has to be signed by a trained person, and the packing has to match the declared specification.

The carrier may also ask for the state of charge, the watt-hour rating, the net quantity per package, the package marks and the emergency contact. If the cargo is packed with equipment, the declaration has to say so. If the battery is damaged or defective, it is a different, harder acceptance and may be refused.
MSDS and UN38.3 test summary.
Dangerous goods declaration and packing certificate.
Commercial invoice, packing list and package marks.
Carrier DG approval and, where required, port approval.

Not every carrier accepts every DG class on every route. A carrier may accept a class on a direct sailing but refuse it on a service that tranships through a hub. The transhipment port can also have its own storage and segregation rules. A booking that is accepted at origin can still fail at the connection.

Expect a DG surcharge, a separate allocation and a longer cut-off. The surcharge is not the same as the ocean freight, and it can change by class, quantity and route. Ask for the DG surcharge as a line item, and ask whether the transhipment port has confirmed acceptance in writing.

Red Sea routings can involve a transhipment at Jeddah, Jebel Ali, Djibouti, Colombo or Singapore. Each hub has its own DG rules. War-risk insurance and the carrier's war-risk surcharge are separate from the DG acceptance, but both can affect whether the booking is commercially viable.

At destination, the import rules also apply. Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Jordan, Djibouti and Sudan each have their own restricted goods, labelling and inspection requirements. A DG that is accepted by the carrier can still be stopped by the import authority if the product documents do not match.

State of charge is a transport condition, not a performance specification. Many carriers apply a limit to lithium-ion cells and batteries shipped alone, often 30% or less, and ask the shipper to measure and document it. A low state of charge reduces the energy available if a cell fails, but it does not make the shipment non-dangerous. The battery still needs the correct UN number, packaging and marks.

Packing has to prevent short circuits and protect the terminals. That means inner packaging that holds each battery or pack in place, insulation against contact, cushioning for shock and a strong outer packaging that meets the applicable UN specification. Cells and batteries shipped alone, packed with equipment or contained in equipment each have their own packaging rules, and the marks on the box have to match the way it is packed.

The package also carries the class 9 label and the lithium battery mark where required, plus the shipper's name and the emergency contact. An overpack needs its own mark and must not hide the labels underneath. If the cargo is mixed with equipment, the declaration has to say so, and the packing must stop the battery from moving inside the box. A photo of the actual packing is often the fastest way to settle a carrier's question.
Measure and declare the state of charge.
Protect terminals and prevent movement.
Use the packaging and marks that match the packing method.
Photograph the packed carton before it is closed.

Do not book a battery or a chemical as general cargo and declare it later. Do not use the UN number from an old shipment without checking the packing and the current carrier requirements. Do not ship damaged, recalled or prototype cells without a separate acceptance. Do not assume a forwarder's verbal yes is a carrier approval.

If you are unsure, send the product specification, the battery type, the UN number, the MSDS, the packing photos and the route before you ask for a price. A complete file gets a real answer. A partial file gets a maybe, and a maybe is not a booking.
No undeclared batteries in general cargo.
No damaged or recalled cells without separate acceptance.
No booking without the carrier's DG approval.
No assumption that the transhipment port will accept it.
Q: Can I ship a lithium battery in a container?

A: Sometimes, but it is not a default yes. It depends on the UN number, the battery type, the state of charge, the packaging, the carrier's acceptance and the transhipment port. A lithium battery booked as general cargo is an undeclared dangerous good, and that can stop the container at the first inspection.
Q: Is a power bank dangerous goods?

A: Often yes, because it contains a lithium battery. The UN number depends on whether it is shipped alone, packed with equipment or contained in equipment. The carrier will also ask for the MSDS, the UN38.3 summary and the state of charge.
Q: Do I need UN38.3 for every battery shipment?

A: For lithium batteries, the UN38.3 test summary is a standard part of the file. The carrier may also ask for the test report, the packaging specification and a DG declaration. Requirements vary by carrier and route, so send the documents before you book, not after.

documents.title: 危险品与电池货出红海：先查什么？
documents.description: 电池和危险品订舱前要拿到船公司批复、正确的 UN 编号和单证。红海航线还要多一道中转审核。
documents.lead: 电池和危险品订舱前要拿到船公司批复、正确的 UN 编号和单证。红海航线还要多一道中转审核。

richText.text: 危险品不是普通订舱加一笔费用，而是 IMDG 规则下的一套独立接收流程。船公司要批复 UN 编号、包装、数量和航线；船舶要允许装这一类别；中转港要接受。任何一环都可以说不。
所以危险品报价比普货慢。船公司拿到危险品资料之前，货代确认不了舱位。先订舱、后申报，船公司可能在闸口拒收，货就卡在那里等下一班船。

body.text: 电池类型与 UN 编号

richText.text: 锂离子和锂金属电池按包装方式分不同的 UN 编号。单独运输的电池，和与设备同箱、装在设备里的电池，不是同一个编号。申报单上的 UN 编号要和实际包装一致，不能按产品的市场名称填。
其他危险品有自己的类别和 UN 编号：易燃、腐蚀、氧化、气雾剂、化学品、带燃料或电池的车辆和机械。类别决定包装、标签、隔离和船公司是否接收。不要凭产品名称猜类别。
UN3480：单独运输的锂离子电池。
UN3481：与设备同箱或装在设备里的锂离子电池。
UN3090：单独运输的锂金属电池。
UN3091：与设备同箱或装在设备里的锂金属电池。
典型的锂电池资料包括 MSDS、UN38.3 测试摘要、危险品申报单、包装证明、商业发票和装箱单，以及船公司的危险品订舱批复。申报单要由受过培训的人签署，包装要和申报规格一致。
船公司还可能问电量、瓦时数、每件净重、包装标记和应急联系人。与设备同箱，申报要写明。电池损坏或有缺陷，属于另一种更难接收的情形，可能直接被拒。
MSDS 和 UN38.3 测试摘要。
危险品申报单和包装证明。
商业发票、装箱单和包装标记。
船公司危险品批复；需要时还有港口批复。
不是每家船公司、每条航线都接所有危险品类别。某家船公司可能接受直航，但不接受经枢纽中转的同一票货。中转港还有自己的仓储和隔离规则。起运港接受的订舱，到了衔接点仍可能出问题。
预期会有危险品附加费、单独舱位分配和更早的截点。附加费不等于海运费，会按类别、数量和航线变。让货代把危险品附加费单列，并确认中转港是否书面接受。
红海航线可能经吉达、杰贝阿里、吉布提、科伦坡或新加坡中转，每个枢纽有自己的危险品规则。战争风险保险和船公司的战争风险附加费与危险品接收是两件事，但都会影响这票货是否划算。
到了目的港，还有进口规则。沙特、埃及、约旦、吉布提和苏丹各有自己的限制商品、标签和检验要求。船公司接受的危险品，如果产品文件和进口要求不一致，仍可能被主管部门拦下。
电量是运输条件，不是产品性能指标。很多船公司对单独运输的锂离子电芯和电池设电量上限，常见是 30% 或更低，并要求发货人测量、记录。低电量会降低电芯失效时释放的能量，但不会把货变成非危险品。电池仍然需要正确的 UN 编号、包装和标记。
包装要防短路、保护端子。内包装要把每个电池或电池组固定住，做好绝缘，避免相互接触，加缓冲防震，外包装要符合适用的 UN 规格。单独运输、与设备同箱、装在设备里，三种方式的包装规则不同，箱上的标记要和实际包装方式一致。
包装上还要有第 9 类标签、需要时的锂电池标记，以及发货人名称和应急联系人。外套箱有自己的标记要求，不能把里面的标签遮住。货和设备混装，申报要写明，包装要防止电池在箱内移动。实际包装的照片，往往是回答船公司疑问最快的方式。
测量并申报电量。
保护端子，防止移动。
包装和标记要与包装方式匹配。
封箱前拍下实际包装。
不要把电池或化学品按普货订舱、之后再申报。不要拿上一票的 UN 编号直接套，先核对包装和船公司当前要求。损坏、召回或原型电芯，不要在没有单独接收的情况下走。货代口头说可以，不等于船公司批复。
拿不准，就在问价前把产品规格、电池类型、UN 编号、MSDS、包装照片和航线发过来。资料完整，才有真答案；资料不全，只能得到“也许”，而“也许”不是订舱。
普货里不要夹带未申报电池。
损坏或召回电芯，没有单独接收不要走。
没有船公司危险品批复，不要订舱。
不要假设中转港一定接收。
问：锂电池能装柜走海运吗？
答：有时可以，但不是默认可以。要看 UN 编号、电池类型、电量、包装、船公司是否接受，以及中转港是否接受。把锂电池当普货订舱，就是未申报危险品，第一次查验就可能把柜子扣下。
问：充电宝算危险品吗？
答：通常算，因为里面有锂电池。UN 编号取决于它是单独运输、与设备同箱，还是装在设备里。船公司还会要 MSDS、UN38.3 摘要和电量信息。
问：每票电池货都要 UN38.3 吗？
答：锂电池通常都要 UN38.3 测试摘要。船公司还可能要求测试报告、包装说明和危险品申报单。不同船公司、不同航线要求不同，单证要在订舱前发，不要等订舱后再补。

documents.title: Port Sudan: clearance, transit and charges
documents.description: Port Sudan has limited direct sailings, an ACD filing before loading and local charges that sit outside the ocean freight. Here is the checklist.
documents.lead: Port Sudan has limited direct sailings, an ACD filing before loading and local charges that sit outside the ocean freight. Here is the checklist.

richText.text: Port Sudan is Sudan's working sea gateway. The country has been in armed conflict since April 2023, and the port's operating conditions can change. Direct sailings from China are limited, so much cargo is transhipped through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti. The routing, the connection and the consignee's ability to clear and pay are part of the quote, not background information.

Before booking, confirm the port, the terminal, the banking channel and the inland leg with the consignee. A rate that works on paper can fail if the consignee cannot get the foreign exchange or the cargo cannot move inland. Ask for a written confirmation of the current situation, not an old quote from last month.

body.text: Transit: why there is no single number

richText.text: A direct sailing is the short version, but direct capacity to Port Sudan is limited. A transhipment adds a hub and a connection window. If the first vessel is late, or the connection is full, the box waits. That is why a quote can say 30 days one week and 45 the next without either number being wrong.

Ask which hub, which carrier, how long the connection is and what happens if the connection is missed. Ask whether the free time at destination starts on discharge or on availability, and who pays the storage if the consignee cannot take the box. Those answers decide the real transit cost.

The Advance Cargo Declaration (ACD, also called ECTN) is mandatory for Sudan-bound cargo on vessels sailing from 1 January 2026. Obtain the 15-digit number before loading in China and print it on the bill of lading. The application needs the draft bill of lading, commercial invoice, freight invoice, certificate of origin and packing list.

Most commercial goods also need an SSMO certificate of inspection from an authorised agency before leaving China, plus an import licence and an IM form. The consignee and the bank have their own requirements. A missing ACD or a mismatched invoice can stop the cargo before it reaches the vessel.
ACD 15-digit number, printed on the bill of lading.
Draft bill of lading, commercial invoice, freight invoice.
Certificate of origin and packing list.
SSMO inspection certificate, import licence and IM form where required.

Clearance is handled by a local broker with the consignee. The broker files the customs declaration, presents the documents, arranges inspection if required and obtains the delivery order. The consignee needs the import registration, the licence and the bank documents. The port and the terminal have their own release process.

Duty is 5–25% for most goods, plus 17% VAT, according to the country page. The HS code and the declared value decide the amount. A broker can give you an estimate, but the customs authority decides. Do not treat a broker's verbal estimate as a fixed landed cost.

body.text: Local charges: what to ask for

richText.text: Local charges at Port Sudan sit outside the ocean freight. They can include port dues, terminal handling, documentation, delivery order, customs broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit and inland transport. The amounts vary by terminal, container type and how long the box stays.

Ask for a line-item destination quote, not one lump sum. Ask what is included in the terminal handling, what the free time is, when demurrage starts, and whether the consignee can pay in local currency. A cheap ocean rate with a large, undisclosed destination charge is not a cheap route.
Port dues and terminal handling.
Documentation, delivery order and broker fees.
Inspection, storage and demurrage/detention.
Container deposit and inland transport.

body.text: Conflict, banking and the inland leg

richText.text: Sudan has been in armed conflict since April 2023, and the operating picture can change faster than a shipping schedule. Port operations, inland roads, border crossings and banking services may be affected in different ways at the same time. Check the current status with the carrier, the local broker and the consignee before each shipment. A route that worked two months ago is not evidence that it works this month.

Banking is part of the routing. The consignee needs the foreign exchange and the payment channel to release the documents and pay the destination charges. If the bank cannot transfer or the importer cannot obtain FX, the cargo can arrive and still not move. Ask the consignee to confirm the bank, the account and the payment steps in writing, and ask whether the bank requires a specific document set before it releases the bill of lading.

The inland leg from Port Sudan to Khartoum and other cities is a separate operation with its own risk and cost. Roads, checkpoints and fuel availability can change. Insurance may exclude war and related risks, so confirm the cover with the insurer, not only the freight forwarder. If the consignee cannot arrange the inland leg, the container may sit at the port and storage will start.
Confirm the port and terminal status before booking.
Confirm the consignee's bank, FX and document release steps.
Name the inland carrier and the delivery point.
Check war-risk cover with the insurer.

Before you confirm, put these in writing: the port and terminal, the routing and connection, the transit range, the ACD number and who files it, the SSMO and import licence status, the consignee's bank and import registration, the destination charges by line, the free time, and the plan if the connection is missed. Send the completed checklist to the broker and the carrier well before the cargo-ready date so any gap can be fixed.

If any line is missing, ask before the cargo leaves the factory. Port Sudan is not a route where a verbal promise is enough. The country page lists the documents we have checked, and the route pages show the current market reading by origin.
Q: How long does shipping from China to Port Sudan take?

A: There is no single reliable range. Direct sailings from China are limited, and much cargo tranships through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti. The connection decides the transit, and a missed connection can add a week or more. Ask for the routing and the connection port on every quote.
Q: What is the ACD for Sudan?

A: The Advance Cargo Declaration is a 15-digit number required for Sudan-bound cargo on vessels sailing from 1 January 2026. It must be obtained before loading in China and printed on the bill of lading. The application uses the draft bill of lading, commercial invoice, freight invoice, certificate of origin and packing list.
Q: Are Port Sudan local charges included in the ocean rate?

A: No. The ocean rate is port-to-port freight. Port dues, terminal handling, documentation, customs broker, duty, VAT, storage, demurrage and inland transport are separate. Ask for a line-item destination quote before you compare two ocean rates.

documents.title: 苏丹港：清关、时效与当地杂费
documents.description: 苏丹港直航有限，装船前要办 ACD，当地杂费也不在海运费里。这篇给出清关、时效和费用的核对清单。
documents.lead: 苏丹港直航有限，装船前要办 ACD，当地杂费也不在海运费里。这篇给出清关、时效和费用的核对清单。

richText.text: 苏丹港是目前苏丹可用的海上门户。苏丹自 2023 年 4 月起处于武装冲突中，港口运营条件可能变化。中国直航有限，很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提中转。航线、衔接，以及收货人能否清关和付款，都是报价的一部分，不是背景信息。
订舱前，和收货人确认港口、码头、银行渠道和内陆段。纸面上成立的运价，如果收货人拿不到外汇、或者货走不了内陆，也会失败。要书面的当前情况确认，不要拿上个月的旧报价。

body.text: 时效：为什么没有统一数字

richText.text: 直航是短的走法，但去苏丹港的直航舱位有限。中转多一个枢纽和一个衔接窗口。第一程晚了，或者衔接舱位满了，柜子就等。所以同一票货，这周报 30 天、下周报 45 天，两个数字都可能没错。
问清哪个枢纽、哪家船公司、衔接要等多久、错过衔接怎么办。问目的港免柜期是从卸船算还是从可提货算，收货人提不了柜时仓储谁付。这些答案才决定真实的时效成本。
预先货物申报（ACD，也称 ECTN）对 2026 年 1 月 1 日起开航的去苏丹货物是强制要求。须在中国装船前取得 15 位编号，并打印在提单上。申请需要提单草稿、商业发票、运费发票、原产地证和装箱单。
多数商品出运前还要由授权机构出具苏丹标准计量局（SSMO）检验证书，另需进口许可证和 IM 表。收货人和银行还有各自的要求。少一个 ACD，或者发票信息不一致，货可能在装船前就被拦下。
ACD 15 位编号，打印在提单上。
提单草稿、商业发票、运费发票。
原产地证和装箱单。
需要时的 SSMO 检验证书、进口许可证和 IM 表。
清关由当地报关行和收货人办理。报关行提交报关单、递交单证、安排查验（如需要），并取得提货单。收货人要有进口登记、许可证和银行单证。港口和码头还有自己的放货流程。
根据目的港页面，多数货物关税为 5–25%，另加 17% 增值税。HS 编码和申报货值决定金额。报关行可以给估算，但最终由海关决定。不要把报关行口头估算当成固定的到岸成本。
苏丹港的当地杂费不在海运费里。可能包括港务费、码头操作、单证、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金和内陆运输。金额随码头、柜型和停留时间变化。
要分项目的目的港报价，不要一个总数。问码头操作含什么、免柜期多久、滞箱从哪天算、收货人能否用当地货币支付。海运费便宜、目的港却有一大笔没说清的费用，不是便宜的航线。
港务费和码头操作。
单证、提货单和报关行费用。
查验、仓储和滞港/滞箱。
柜押金和内陆运输。
苏丹自 2023 年 4 月起处于武装冲突中，运营情况可能比船期变得更快。港口作业、内陆道路、边境口岸和银行服务可能同时受到不同影响。每票货出运前，向船公司、当地报关行和收货人确认当前状态。两个月前能走的路线，不代表这个月还能走。
银行是航线的一部分。收货人要有外汇和付款渠道，才能赎单、支付目的港费用。银行转不出钱，或者进口商拿不到外汇，货到了也动不了。让收货人书面确认银行、账户和付款步骤，并问清银行放提单前是否需要特定单证。
从苏丹港到喀土穆和其他城市的内陆段，是另一套操作，有自己的风险和成本。道路、检查站和燃油供应都可能变化。保险可能排除战争及相关风险，要向保险方确认承保范围，不要只问货代。收货人安排不了内陆段，柜子就可能压在港口，仓储开始计费。
订舱前确认港口和码头状态。
确认收货人的银行、外汇和放单步骤。
明确内陆承运人和交货地点。
向保险方核对战争风险承保范围。
确认之前，把这些写下来：港口和码头、航线和衔接、时效区间、ACD 编号及由谁办理、SSMO 和进口许可证状态、收货人的银行和进口登记、分项目的目的港费用、免柜期，以及错过衔接的预案。把填好的清单在备货日前发给报关行和船公司，留出补漏时间。
少任何一行，就在货离开工厂前问。苏丹港不是靠口头承诺就能走的航线。目的港页面列了我们核对过的单证，路线页面显示各起运港的当前市场读数。
问：中国到苏丹港海运要多久？
答：没有一个可靠统一的数字。中国直航有限，很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提中转。衔接决定时效，错过衔接可能多等一周以上。每份报价都要问航线和衔接港。
问：苏丹的 ACD 是什么？
答：预先货物申报（ACD）是 2026 年 1 月 1 日起开航的去苏丹货物必须办理的 15 位编号。须在中国装船前取得，并打印在提单上。申请要用提单草稿、商业发票、运费发票、原产地证和装箱单。
问：苏丹港当地费用含在海运费里吗？
答：不含。海运费是港到港运费。港务费、码头操作、单证、报关行、关税、增值税、仓储、滞箱和内陆运输都另计。比较两份海运费之前，先要一份分项目的目的港报价。

documents.title: Djibouti: clearance, transit and charges
documents.description: Djibouti is the gateway for Ethiopia and a transhipment hub for the region. The ECTN, the Ethiopia transit route and the local charges decide the real cost.
documents.lead: Djibouti is the gateway for Ethiopia and a transhipment hub for the region. The ECTN, the Ethiopia transit route and the local charges decide the real cost.

richText.text: Djibouti serves its own market and, more importantly, the Ethiopian hinterland. Most cargo moving to Addis Ababa enters through Djibouti and continues by rail or road, often via the Modjo dry port. The port is also a transhipment hub for Red Sea and East African destinations, so the same terminal handles local, transit and transhipment cargo.

The ocean rate is only the first line. The ECTN, the Ethiopia import licence and foreign exchange, the transit corridor and the local charges decide whether the cargo arrives on budget. Ask for the destination quote in two parts: Djibouti port and the onward leg.

From China, allow about 19–24 days to Djibouti on a direct sailing and 25–30 days with one transhipment, plus clearance. From Djibouti to Addis Ababa, the rail takes about 12–15 hours and the road about 2–5 days, depending on the border and the corridor. These are sailing and transport times, not a door-to-door promise.

The Ethiopia import licence and foreign exchange are often the real constraint. The consignee needs the licence, the bank permit and the FX before the cargo can be cleared for transit. If those are not ready, the box waits at Djibouti and storage starts. Confirm the documents before booking, not after arrival.

The ECTN is required for Djibouti-bound cargo since 15 June 2023. Obtain it before loading and show the number on the bill of lading. The application typically needs the bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin and freight invoice. A mismatch between the ECTN and the bill of lading can stop the cargo.

For cargo in direct transit to Ethiopia, the ECTN is exempt when the bill of lading states “In transit to Ethiopia” and the consignee is in Ethiopia. The exemption is checked on the documents, so the exact wording and the consignee's details matter. Do not assume a verbal instruction is enough.
ECTN number, or the exact Ethiopia transit wording on the bill of lading.
Bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin.
Ethiopia import licence and bank permit/FX where the cargo moves to Ethiopia.
Freight invoice and any certificate required for the commodity.

A local broker files the declaration with the consignee and obtains the delivery order. Local cargo is cleared into Djibouti. Transit cargo to Ethiopia is cleared under the transit regime and moves by rail or road, often through Modjo. The broker needs the ECTN, the bill of lading, the invoice, the packing list and the transit documents.

Ask the broker to confirm the corridor, the border post and the rail or road schedule before the cargo arrives. Ask who handles the Ethiopia side and who pays the storage if the transit documents are incomplete. The port and the corridor are two different operations, and both need an owner.

body.text: Local charges: what to ask for

richText.text: Djibouti local charges sit outside the ocean freight. They can include port dues, terminal handling, documentation, ECTN fee, delivery order, broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit and the onward rail or road leg. The amounts vary by terminal, container type and dwell time.

Ask for the Djibouti port charges and the Ethiopia transit charges as separate lines. Ask what the ECTN fee covers, what the free time is, when storage starts, and whether the rail or road rate includes the border and the dry port. A single lump sum hides the part that will grow.
Port dues and terminal handling.
Documentation, ECTN and broker fees.
Storage, demurrage and detention.
Container deposit, rail or road to the dry port.

body.text: The last mile: rail, road and Modjo

richText.text: From Djibouti, the container can continue by rail or road. The rail leg to Addis Ababa takes about 12–15 hours, but the total door-to-door time includes the terminal handling at both ends, the train schedule and the clearance at Modjo. The road leg takes about 2–5 days and is more flexible on timing, but it depends on the border, the corridor and the truck available. Neither option is automatically cheaper; the cargo, the volume and the delivery point decide.

Modjo is a dry port, not a final destination. Cargo can be cleared there and then delivered locally, or moved onward. The consignee needs a broker who can handle the dry-port release, and the trucker needs the right documents to collect the container. If the container is not returned within the free time, detention continues even after the cargo is unloaded. Ask who is responsible for the empty return and where it goes.

The Ethiopia-side broker and the Djibouti-side broker are often different companies. Make one of them the owner of the full chain, or define the handover point in writing. The most common failure is not the ocean leg; it is a document that arrives after the container, or a truck that cannot cross because the transit paper is wrong. Put the handover point, the contact and the document list in the booking confirmation.
Rail: faster line-haul, fixed schedule, terminal handling at both ends.
Road: flexible, but border and corridor time vary.
Modjo: clearance and release, not the final address.
Empty return: confirm who returns the box and by when.

Before you confirm, put these in writing: the ECTN status or the Ethiopia transit wording, the bill of lading details, the import licence and FX status, the corridor and border post, the rail or road schedule, the destination charges by line, the free time, and who handles the Ethiopia side.

If the cargo is for Ethiopia, treat the Djibouti port and the corridor as one plan with two owners. If the cargo is for Djibouti itself, confirm the local clearance and delivery address. The country page and the route pages give the current reading and the documents we have checked.
Q: How long does shipping from China to Djibouti take?

A: Allow about 19–24 days for a direct sailing and 25–30 days with one transhipment, plus clearance and the inland leg. From Djibouti to Addis Ababa, the rail takes about 12–15 hours and the road about 2–5 days. The Ethiopia import licence and foreign exchange can add time before the cargo moves.
Q: Do I need an ECTN for Djibouti?

A: Yes, since 15 June 2023. The ECTN must be obtained before loading and the number shown on the bill of lading. Cargo in direct transit to Ethiopia is exempt when the bill of lading states “In transit to Ethiopia” and the consignee is in Ethiopia. The exemption is documentary, so the wording must be exact.
Q: Are Djibouti local charges included in the ocean rate?

A: No. Port dues, terminal handling, documentation, ECTN fee, broker, storage, demurrage, container deposit and the inland or rail leg are separate. Ask for a line-item quote that separates Djibouti port charges from the Ethiopia transit cost.

documents.title: 吉布提：清关、时效与当地杂费
documents.description: 吉布提是埃塞俄比亚的门户，也是区域中转枢纽。ECTN、埃塞过境路线和当地杂费决定真实成本。
documents.lead: 吉布提是埃塞俄比亚的门户，也是区域中转枢纽。ECTN、埃塞过境路线和当地杂费决定真实成本。

richText.text: 吉布提服务本国市场，更重要的是服务埃塞俄比亚腹地。去亚的斯亚贝巴的货大多经吉布提入境，再走铁路或公路，常经 Modjo 陆港。吉布提港也是红海和东非目的地的中转枢纽，同一个码头要处理本地、过境和中转货。
海运费只是第一行。ECTN、埃塞进口许可证和外汇、过境走廊和当地杂费，才决定货是否在预算内到。目的港报价要分两部分要：吉布提港和后续段。
从中国到吉布提，直航约 19–24 天，一次中转约 25–30 天，另加清关。吉布提至亚的斯亚贝巴，铁路约 12–15 小时，公路约 2–5 天，取决于口岸和走廊。这些是航程和运输时间，不是门到门承诺。
埃塞进口许可证和外汇往往才是真正的瓶颈。收货人要有许可证、银行许可和外汇，货才能办过境。这些没准备好，柜子就在吉布提等，仓储开始计费。订舱前确认单证，不要等到港后。
去吉布提的货物自 2023 年 6 月 15 日起需要 ECTN。装船前取得，并在提单上显示编号。申请通常需要提单、商业发票、装箱单、原产地证和运费发票。ECTN 与提单信息不一致，货可能被拦。
直接过境到埃塞俄比亚的货物，提单注明“In transit to Ethiopia”且收货人在埃塞俄比亚时，可免 ECTN。豁免按单证审核，措辞和收货人信息都要准确。不要以为口头说明就够了。
ECTN 编号，或提单上准确的埃塞过境措辞。
提单、商业发票、装箱单、原产地证。
货去埃塞俄比亚时的进口许可证和银行许可/外汇。
运费发票和商品所需的证书。
当地报关行和收货人提交报关，取得提货单。本地货清关进入吉布提。去埃塞俄比亚的过境货按过境制度清关，走铁路或公路，常经 Modjo。报关行需要 ECTN、提单、发票、装箱单和过境单证。
货到前，让报关行确认走廊、口岸和铁路或公路班期。问埃塞一侧由谁处理、过境单证不齐时仓储谁付。港口和走廊是两套操作，都要有负责人。
吉布提当地杂费不在海运费里。可能包括港务费、码头操作、单证、ECTN 费、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金和后续铁路或公路段。金额随码头、柜型和停留时间变化。
吉布提港杂费和埃塞过境费要分开列。问 ECTN 费含什么、免柜期多久、仓储从哪天算、铁路或公路价是否含口岸和陆港。一个总数会把以后会涨的那部分藏起来。
港务费和码头操作。
单证、ECTN 和报关行费用。
仓储、滞港和滞箱。
柜押金、铁路或公路到陆港。

body.text: 最后一程：铁路、公路与 Modjo

richText.text: 从吉布提出来，柜子可以走铁路或公路。铁路到亚的斯亚贝巴约 12–15 小时，但门到门总时长还要加两端的码头操作、班列计划和 Modjo 的清关。公路约 2–5 天，时间上更灵活，但取决于口岸、走廊和可用车辆。两种方式没有绝对的便宜，货种、货量和送货点决定选择。
Modjo 是陆港，不是最终目的地。货可以在那里清关后再本地派送，也可以继续转运。收货人要有能处理陆港放货的报关行，拖车要有正确单证才能提柜。柜子没有在免柜期内还回，哪怕货已经卸了，滞箱费还会继续。要问清空柜由谁负责还、还到哪里。
埃塞一侧的报关行和吉布提一侧的报关行，往往是两家公司。让其中一家负责全链条，或者把交接点写清楚。最常见的失败不在海上，而是单证比柜子晚到，或者过境纸错了、车过不了口岸。把交接点、联系人和单证清单写进订舱确认。
铁路：干线快、班期固定，两端有码头操作。
公路：灵活，但口岸和走廊时间会变。
Modjo：清关和放货点，不是最终地址。
空柜：确认谁还、什么时候还。
确认之前，把这些写下来：ECTN 状态或埃塞过境措辞、提单信息、进口许可证和外汇状态、走廊和口岸、铁路或公路班期、分项目的目的港费用、免柜期，以及埃塞一侧由谁负责。
货去埃塞俄比亚，就把吉布提港和走廊当成一个计划、两个负责人。货去吉布提本地，就确认本地清关和送货地址。目的港页面和路线页面给出当前市场读数和我们核对过的单证。

items.text: 中国到吉布提目的港页

richText.text: 问：中国到吉布提海运要多久？
答：直航约 19–24 天，一次中转约 25–30 天，另加清关和内陆段。吉布提至亚的斯亚贝巴，铁路约 12–15 小时，公路约 2–5 天。埃塞进口许可证和外汇可能让货在转运前多等。
问：去吉布提需要 ECTN 吗？
答：需要，自 2023 年 6 月 15 日起。ECTN 须在装船前取得，编号显示在提单上。直接过境到埃塞俄比亚的货物，在提单注明“In transit to Ethiopia”且收货人在埃塞俄比亚时可豁免。豁免是单证层面的，措辞必须准确。
问：吉布提当地费用含在海运费里吗？
答：不含。港务费、码头操作、单证、ECTN 费、报关行、仓储、滞箱、柜押金和内陆或铁路段都另计。要一份把吉布提港杂费和埃塞过境成本分开列出的分项报价。

documents.title: Shanghai to Red Sea Shipping: Routes & Transit
documents.description: Shanghai offers the widest carrier choice on this trade, but the cheapest ocean line is not always the cheapest door cost.
documents.lead: Shanghai offers the widest carrier choice on this trade, but the cheapest ocean line is not always the cheapest door cost.

body.text: Why Shanghai, and who it suits

richText.text: Shanghai is China's largest container gateway and the main outlet for the Yangtze Delta. Its advantage is choice: more carriers, more sailings and more routing combinations than any other Chinese port on this trade. For a shipper in Shanghai, southern Jiangsu or northern Zhejiang, that choice can mean a direct sailing to Jeddah, Sokhna, Aqaba or Djibouti, and a workable connection to Port Sudan.

Choice is not the same as the lowest total cost. Shanghai's local charges and trucking can be higher than Ningbo's, and a factory in Zhejiang may be closer to Ningbo. Shanghai suits time-sensitive cargo, high-value goods, mixed SKUs and shippers who need several sailing options in the same week. It is less compelling when the cargo is heavy, the factory is far away and the only goal is the lowest ocean line.

Direct and transhipment sailings both exist. The country pages give port-to-port ranges: Jeddah 17–31 days, Sokhna 20–35 days, Aqaba 20–35 days, Djibouti 19–30 days. Jeddah has direct sailings from Shanghai and Shenzhen at about 17–18 days; Sokhna has direct sailings from South China at about 20–23 days, while North China cargo often tranships and can take 32–35 days. Port Sudan has limited direct capacity and much cargo connects via Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti.

Those ranges are not a schedule. A carrier may publish 18 days and still miss the connection, and a transhipment quote can arrive earlier than a direct one if the direct sailing is full or delayed. Ask for the next two ETDs, the connection port, the cut-off at each end and the free time at destination. If the cargo has a fixed delivery date, compare the arrival window, not the fastest published number.

The ocean freight is only one line. Origin charges at Shanghai can include terminal handling, documentation, export declaration, trucking from the factory and, for LCL, warehouse handling and consolidation. War-risk and peak-season surcharges may sit on top. The same destination can quote differently from Shanghai and Ningbo because the sailing, the equipment and the local charges are different.

Compare a line-item quote, not a single number. Ask what is included in the terminal handling, whether the trucking is to the port or only to a depot, how many free days the destination gives, and how long the rate is valid. A low ocean line with a long truck leg or a short free time can cost more than a slightly higher all-in quote.

Rates on this trade are usually valid for a short window, not the whole month. The ocean line, the war-risk surcharge and the space can change together. Ask for the validity date and the date by which the container must be gated in. If the rate expires before your cargo is ready, the next quote may be different. A booking that holds a rate but misses the vessel is not a saving.

Shanghai handles high-value electronics, machinery, mixed consumer goods, e-commerce cargo and time-sensitive shipments well because there are more sailings to choose from. LCL consolidation is also broad, which helps smaller shippers. Dangerous goods and batteries can move, but only with carrier approval, the right UN number and a transhipment port that accepts the class.

For dense cargo, price a 20GP first and confirm the payload; for light, voluminous cargo, a 40HQ usually lowers the cost per cubic metre. Project cargo and out-of-gauge units need a separate review of equipment, lifting and road permits. Do not assume a container rate applies to a flat rack or an open-top.

Booking early matters in peak weeks. Shanghai's sailings fill from both local and feeder cargo, and equipment can tighten before the rate does. If the cargo is ready, book before the cut-off, not after. If it is not ready, ask for a later sailing rather than holding space you cannot use. A confirmed booking with the wrong cargo-ready date is worse than a later sailing with the right one.
Time-sensitive or high-value cargo: Shanghai's sailing choice helps.
Factory in Zhejiang: compare Ningbo before booking.
Heavy cargo: 20GP first, then check payload and road limits.
DG or batteries: carrier approval before the booking.

Jeddah is the most straightforward: direct sailings from Shanghai are listed at about 17–18 days, with transhipment options up to 31 days. Sokhna depends on the sailing; South China direct services are faster, while East and North China cargo often connects through a hub. Aqaba has direct services at about 20–28 days, and a transhipment adds roughly 3–7 days. Djibouti has direct services at about 19–24 days and one-stop options at 25–30 days.

Port Sudan is the exception. Direct sailings from China are limited, and much cargo tranships through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti. A missed connection can add a week or more. Confirm the port, terminal, banking channel and inland leg with the consignee before booking; the country page lists the ACD and SSMO documents we have checked.
Jeddah: direct 17–18 days; transhipment up to 31 days.
Sokhna: South China direct 20–23 days; North China transhipment 32–35 days.
Aqaba: direct 20–28 days; transhipment adds 3–7 days.
Djibouti: direct 19–24 days; one-stop 25–30 days.
Port Sudan: limited direct; confirm the hub and connection.

Before you ask for a rate, write down the cargo-ready date, the factory address, the nearest origin port, the destination port, the container type and quantity, the HS code and the Incoterms. Add the consignee's document requirements and the delivery address. A complete enquiry gets a quote you can compare; a partial one gets a maybe.

If the cargo is ready now, ask for the next two sailings. If it is flexible, ask what changes next week. Do not book on the ocean line alone: check the routing, the connection, the free time and the total cost. The links below go to the Shanghai route pages, the destination pages and the current market reading.

items.text: China to Saudi Arabia rates and documents

richText.text: Q: Is Shanghai the best origin for every Red Sea shipment?

A: No. Shanghai has the widest carrier choice, but a factory in Zhejiang may save more by loading at Ningbo, and a factory in Shandong may save more at Qingdao. Compare the total cost including trucking, not only the ocean freight.
Q: How long does Shanghai to Jeddah take?

A: The country page lists 17–31 days port to port: about 17–18 days on a direct sailing, up to 31 days with a transhipment. The exact figure depends on the carrier and the connection, so ask for the routing on your quote.
Q: Can I ship dangerous goods from Shanghai?

A: Sometimes. The carrier must approve the UN number, packing and route, and the transhipment port must accept the class. Send the MSDS, UN38.3 summary and packing details before booking; a general cargo booking cannot be converted later.

documents.title: 上海到红海海运：船期、时效与货型
documents.description: 上海的优势是船公司和船期选择多，但海运费最低不一定到门最便宜。这篇讲上海出红海怎么选。
documents.lead: 上海的优势是船公司和船期选择多，但海运费最低不一定到门最便宜。这篇讲上海出红海怎么选。

richText.text: 上海是中国最大的集装箱门户，也是长三角的主要出海口。它的优势是选择多：这条航线上，船公司、船期和航线组合都比其他中国港口多。对上海、苏南、浙北的货主来说，这种选择可能意味着到吉达、苏赫纳、亚喀巴或吉布提有直航，到苏丹港也能接上中转。
选择多不等于总成本最低。上海的本地费用和拖车可能高于宁波，浙江工厂离宁波也更近。上海适合时效紧的货、高价值货、多品种拼票，以及同一周需要几个船期备选的货主。货重、工厂远、只追求海运费最低时，上海的优势就没那么明显。
直航和中转都有。目的港页面给出港到港区间：吉达 17–31 天，苏赫纳 20–35 天，亚喀巴 20–35 天，吉布提 19–30 天。吉达有上海和深圳直航，约 17–18 天；苏赫纳有华南直航，约 20–23 天，华北货常需中转，可能 32–35 天。苏丹港直航舱位有限，很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接。
这些区间不是船期表。船公司可能写 18 天，实际仍会错过衔接；直航满舱或延误时，中转报价也可能更早到。问最近两个 ETD、中转港、两端截点和目的港免柜期。货有固定交期，就比到货窗口，不要只比最快的那一天。
海运费只是一行。上海的起运港费用可能包括码头操作、单证、出口申报、工厂拖车；拼箱还有仓库操作和集拼。战争风险和旺季附加费可能另加。同一个目的港，上海和宁波的报价不同，因为船期、箱源和本地费用不同。
要比分项报价，不要只比一个总数。问码头操作含什么、拖车是到港区还是只到堆场、目的港免柜几天、价格有效期多久。海运费低、拖车远或免柜期短，最后可能比贵一点的全包价更贵。
这条航线的价格通常只在一段短窗口内有效，不是整月不变。海运费、战争风险附加费和舱位可能一起变。问有效期和进闸截止日。运价在货好之前到期，下一份报价可能就不同了。拿着旧价却赶不上船，不算省钱。
上海适合高价值电子、机械、混合消费品、电商货和时效紧的货，因为船期选择多。拼箱集拼也广，小货主更容易找到舱位。危险品和电池可以走，但要有船公司批复、正确 UN 编号，以及接受该类别的中转港。
重货先问 20GP 并确认载重；轻货、体积货用 40HQ 通常能把每立方米成本拉低。项目货和超尺寸货要单独看设备、吊装和公路许可。不要以为普通柜的运价能套到框架柜或开顶柜。
旺季要早订。上海的舱位同时被本地货和驳船货占用，箱源可能比运价更早紧张。货好了就在截点前订，不要拖到截点后。货没好，就问下一班船，不要占着舱位却用不上。备货日期填错的确认订舱，比晚一班船更麻烦。
时效紧或高价值货：上海的船期选择有帮助。
工厂在浙江：订舱前先比宁波。
重货：先看 20GP，再核对载重和公路限重。
危险品或电池：先拿船公司批复再订舱。
吉达最直接：上海直航约 17–18 天，中转最长约 31 天。苏赫纳看船期：华南直航更快，华东和华北货常经枢纽衔接。亚喀巴有直航，约 20–28 天，中转多约 3–7 天。吉布提直航约 19–24 天，一次中转约 25–30 天。
苏丹港是例外。中国直航有限，很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提中转。错过衔接可能多等一周以上。订舱前和收货人确认港口、码头、银行渠道和内陆段；目的港页面列了我们核对过的 ACD 和 SSMO 单证。
吉达：直航 17–18 天；中转最长 31 天。
苏赫纳：华南直航 20–23 天；华北中转 32–35 天。
亚喀巴：直航 20–28 天；中转多 3–7 天。
吉布提：直航 19–24 天；一次中转 25–30 天。
苏丹港：直航有限；确认枢纽和衔接。
询价前先写下备货日期、工厂地址、最近起运港、目的港、柜型和数量、HS 编码和贸易条款。再加上收货人的单证要求和送货地址。资料完整，拿到的是能比较的报价；资料不全，只能得到“也许”。
货已经好了，就问最近两班船；货期灵活，就问下周有什么变化。不要只看海运费订舱：航线、衔接、免柜期和总成本都要看。下面的链接通向上海航线页、目的港页面和当前市场读数。

richText.text: 问：上海是发红海的最佳起运港吗？
答：不一定。上海船公司选择最多，但浙江工厂走宁波可能更省，山东工厂走青岛可能更省。要把拖车费算进去比总成本，不能只看海运费。
问：上海到吉达要多久？
答：目的港页面给出 17–31 天港到港：直航约 17–18 天，中转最长约 31 天。具体看船公司和衔接，询价时问清航线。
问：上海能出危险品吗？
答：有时可以。船公司要批复 UN 编号、包装和航线，中转港也要接受该类别。订舱前先发 MSDS、UN38.3 摘要和包装资料；普货订舱不能事后改成危险品。

documents.title: Ningbo to Red Sea Shipping: Routes & Transit
documents.description: Ningbo is Zhejiang's deep-water outlet. It can beat Shanghai on total cost for heavy cargo, but has fewer direct Red Sea calls.
documents.lead: Ningbo is Zhejiang's deep-water outlet. It can beat Shanghai on total cost for heavy cargo, but has fewer direct Red Sea calls.

body.text: Why Ningbo, and who it suits

richText.text: Ningbo is the main seaport for Zhejiang and one of the busiest container ports in the world. Its deep-water berths and strong feeder network make it a natural outlet for machinery, furniture, tiles, auto parts, building materials and project cargo from Ningbo, Hangzhou, Wenzhou, Taizhou and the surrounding manufacturing belt. For a factory in Zhejiang, the truck leg is often shorter and cheaper than trucking to Shanghai.

The trade-off is choice. Ningbo has fewer direct Red Sea calls than Shanghai, and some sailings feed into Shanghai or connect through an Asian hub. That can add a day or a week, depending on the connection. Ningbo suits cost-sensitive cargo, heavy loads and shippers who value a short inland leg; it is less ideal when the delivery date is tight and only a direct sailing will do.

Ningbo's Red Sea services mix direct calls and transhipment. Jeddah is listed at 17–31 days port to port, Sokhna at 20–35 days, Aqaba at 20–35 days and Djibouti at 19–30 days. Direct sailings are faster; a connection through Shanghai, Singapore or Colombo can add several days. Port Sudan has limited direct capacity and often connects via Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti.

Ask whether the first vessel actually loads at Ningbo or feeds to Shanghai. A feeder leg adds a handover and a cut-off, and it changes who is responsible if the connection is missed. Ask for the connection port and the next sailing after a missed connection. A quote that says only “Ningbo to Jeddah” does not answer those questions.

The ocean freight, origin charges and trucking decide the total. Ningbo's local charges can be lower than Shanghai's for some cargo, and the truck leg from a Zhejiang factory is often shorter. But a feeder to Shanghai adds a leg, and a transhipment adds destination handling. The cheapest ocean line may not be the cheapest door cost.

Ask for a line-item quote: terminal handling, documentation, export declaration, trucking, feeder if any, ocean freight, war risk, destination charges and free time. If the cargo is heavy, confirm the payload and the road limit before you compare per-container rates. A 20GP may carry more cargo tonnes than a 40HQ, even if the ocean line looks higher.

Equipment is part of the cost. A 40HQ may be easier to find than a 40GP, and a 20GP may be scarce when dense cargo is moving. Ask about the container type and the pick-up location, not only the ocean rate. If the box has to be trucked empty from another depot, that leg belongs in the comparison.

Ningbo is a good fit for dense and voluminous cargo: machinery, furniture, tiles, sanitary ware, auto parts, steel products, building materials and project units. The port has the equipment and the feeder network to handle heavy loads, and the shorter truck leg from Zhejiang reduces road risk. For light consumer goods, the choice between Ningbo and Shanghai often comes down to the sailing, not the port.

Dangerous goods and batteries need the same carrier approval as any other origin. Do not assume a Ningbo sailing accepts a class because Shanghai does. Ask the carrier and the transhipment port separately. For high-value or fragile cargo, the extra handover of a feeder or transhipment is a risk to price into the decision.

Consolidation is another reason to compare. Ningbo has LCL services, but departure frequency may be lower than Shanghai's. If the cargo is small, waiting for the next consolidation can cost more than the truck to Shanghai. If it fills a 20GP or 40HQ, the sailing choice matters more than the LCL schedule. For inland factories in Hangzhou, Shaoxing or Taizhou, rail and barge options can move boxes to Ningbo without a long truck leg; ask whether the quote includes that leg and who owns the cut-off.
Heavy machinery and project cargo: check equipment and lifting.
Furniture, tiles and building materials: 40HQ for volume, 20GP for weight.
Zhejiang factory: compare the truck leg to Ningbo and Shanghai.
DG or batteries: confirm the class on the actual sailing.

Jeddah, Sokhna, Aqaba and Djibouti are all reachable from Ningbo, but the mix of direct and transhipment changes by carrier and week. Jeddah is the most mature route, with direct and connecting options. Sokhna can be direct from South China and transhipped from East/North China. Aqaba and Djibouti often connect through a hub, so the connection window matters as much as the ocean leg.

Port Sudan is the least direct. Much cargo connects through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti, and a missed connection can add a week or more. If the consignee needs a specific arrival window, ask for the connection port and the contingency plan before booking. The country page lists the ACD and SSMO requirements.
Jeddah: direct and transhipment options; 17–31 days.
Sokhna: 20–35 days; North China cargo often tranships.
Aqaba: 20–35 days; confirm the connection.
Djibouti: 19–30 days; direct or one-stop.
Port Sudan: limited direct; plan for a hub connection.

Write down the factory address, cargo-ready date, destination, container type, gross weight, HS code and Incoterms. Add the consignee's document requirements and the delivery address. If the factory is in Zhejiang, get trucking quotes to both Ningbo and Shanghai; the difference can decide the origin.

Ask for the next two sailings, the routing, the connection port and the free time. Do not compare a Ningbo transhipment quote with a Shanghai direct quote as if they were the same product. If the cargo is time-sensitive, the direct option may be worth the higher ocean line. If it is not, the cheaper connection may be the better total. If the two totals are close, choose the shorter inland leg and the clearer free time.

items.text: China to Egypt rates and ACID

richText.text: Q: Is Ningbo cheaper than Shanghai for Red Sea cargo?

A: Not always. Ningbo can be cheaper for cargo originating in Zhejiang because the truck leg is shorter, and its ocean rates are often competitive. Shanghai has more sailings and sometimes more direct options. Compare the total cost, including trucking and local charges, for the same sailing window.
Q: Does Ningbo have direct sailings to the Red Sea?

A: Some services call directly, but the choice is narrower than Shanghai's. Many Red Sea sailings from Ningbo connect through Shanghai, Singapore, Colombo or another hub. Ask whether the quote is direct, which hub it uses and how long the connection is.
Q: What cargo suits Ningbo?

A: Heavy and voluminous cargo from Zhejiang: machinery, furniture, tiles, auto parts, building materials and project cargo. The port's deep water and equipment make it a practical choice for dense loads. Small, urgent shipments may still find more sailings at Shanghai.

documents.title: 宁波到红海海运：船期、时效与货型
documents.description: 宁波是浙江制造业的深水出海口。重货走宁波的总成本可能低于上海，但红海直航较少。订舱前两个港都值得比。
documents.lead: 宁波是浙江制造业的深水出海口。重货走宁波的总成本可能低于上海，但红海直航较少。订舱前两个港都值得比。

richText.text: 宁波是浙江的主要出海口，也是全球最繁忙的集装箱港之一。深水泊位和密集的支线网络，使它适合宁波、杭州、温州、台州及周边制造业的机械、家具、瓷砖、汽车配件、建材和项目货。浙江工厂走宁波，拖车通常比到上海更短、更便宜。
代价是选择少。宁波的红海直航比上海少，有些船要先驳到上海，或者经亚洲枢纽衔接。衔接可能多一天，也可能多一周。宁波适合对成本敏感、货重、看重短拖车的货主；交期很紧、只要直航时，就没那么合适。
宁波的红海航线直航和中转都有。吉达港到港 17–31 天，苏赫纳 20–35 天，亚喀巴 20–35 天，吉布提 19–30 天。直航更快；经上海、新加坡或科伦坡衔接可能多几天。苏丹港直航有限，常经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接。
问清第一程是在宁波装船，还是先驳到上海。支线多一次交接和截点，也会改变错过衔接时的责任。问中转港，以及错过后的下一班船。只写“宁波到吉达”的报价，回答不了这些问题。
总成本由海运费、起运港费用和拖车决定。某些货走宁波，本地费用比上海低，浙江工厂的拖车也更短。但驳到上海会多一段，中转会在目的港多一次操作。海运费最低，不一定到门最便宜。
要分项报价：码头操作、单证、出口申报、拖车、可能的驳船、海运费、战争风险、目的港费用和免柜期。货重的话，比每柜运价前先确认载重和公路限重。20GP 可能比 40HQ 多装货吨，哪怕海运费看起来更高。
箱源也是成本的一部分。40HQ 可能比 40GP 好找；重货多的时候 20GP 也会紧。问柜型和提柜地点，不要只问海运费。空柜要从另一个堆场拖过来，这段也要算进比较。
宁波适合重货和体积货：机械、家具、瓷砖、洁具、汽车配件、钢材、建材和项目设备。港口设备和支线网络能处理重柜，浙江短拖车也降低公路风险。轻泡消费品走宁波还是上海，往往取决于船期，不取决于港口本身。
危险品和电池同样要船公司批复。不要以为上海接受的类别，宁波也一定接受。船公司和中转港要分别确认。高价值或易碎货，要把支线或中转多一次交接的风险算进决策。
集拼也是比较的理由。宁波有拼箱服务，但班次可能比上海少。货少，等下一班集拼的成本可能高于拖到上海。货能装满 20GP 或 40HQ，船期就比拼箱班次更重要。杭州、绍兴、台州等内陆工厂，可以用铁路或驳船把柜子运到宁波，减少长拖车；问报价是否含这一段、截点由谁负责。
重型机械和项目货：确认设备和吊装。
家具、瓷砖、建材：体积货看 40HQ，重货看 20GP。
浙江工厂：比较到宁波和上海的拖车。
危险品或电池：按实际船期确认类别。
宁波到吉达、苏赫纳、亚喀巴和吉布提都能走，但直航和中转的比例随船公司、星期变化。吉达最成熟，直航和中转都有。苏赫纳华南有直航，华东/华北常中转。亚喀巴和吉布提常经枢纽衔接，衔接窗口和海上段一样重要。
苏丹港最不直接。很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接，错过衔接可能多等一周以上。收货人有明确到货窗口，就订舱前问清中转港和预案。目的港页面列了 ACD 和 SSMO 要求。
吉达：直航和中转都有；17–31 天。
苏赫纳：20–35 天；华北货常中转。
亚喀巴：20–35 天；确认衔接。
吉布提：19–30 天；直航或一次中转。
苏丹港：直航有限；按枢纽衔接做计划。
写下工厂地址、备货日期、目的港、柜型、毛重、HS 编码和贸易条款。再加上收货人的单证要求和送货地址。工厂在浙江，就同时问宁波和上海的拖车价；差额可能直接决定起运港。
问最近两班船、航线、中转港和免柜期。不要拿宁波中转报价和上海直航报价当同一个产品比。货急，直航可能值更高的海运费；货不急，便宜的中转可能总成本更低。如果两个总价接近，选内陆段更短、免柜期更清楚的那个。

richText.text: 问：宁波比上海便宜吗？
答：不一定。浙江起运的货走宁波，拖车更短，海运费也常有竞争力。上海船期更多，直航选择有时更多。要在同一个出运窗口里比总成本，含拖车和本地费用。
问：宁波有红海直航吗？
答：有船直挂，但选择比上海少。宁波很多红海货经上海、新加坡、科伦坡或其他枢纽衔接。问清是直航还是中转、走哪个枢纽、衔接多久。
问：什么货适合走宁波？
答：浙江起运的重货和体积货：机械、家具、瓷砖、汽车配件、建材和项目货。宁波水深、设备条件好，适合重柜。小批量、时效紧的货，上海船期可能更多。

documents.title: Shenzhen to Red Sea Shipping: Routes & Transit
documents.description: Shenzhen is South China's gateway for electronics, batteries and consumer goods. It has direct Red Sea options, but DG needs carrier approval.
documents.lead: Shenzhen is South China's gateway for electronics, batteries and consumer goods. It has direct Red Sea options, but DG needs carrier approval.

body.text: Why Shenzhen, and who it suits

richText.text: Shenzhen is the container gateway for the Pearl River Delta and the manufacturing belt around Shenzhen, Dongguan, Huizhou and Guangzhou. Yantian and Shekou handle a large share of South China's electronics, batteries, appliances, furniture and consumer goods. For a factory in Guangdong, the truck leg is short, and the port has deep experience with high-value and dangerous goods cargo.

Shenzhen's advantage is not just cost. It is the combination of direct South China sailings, a dense feeder network and a supply chain that understands export documentation. That suits electronics, e-commerce, high-value consumer goods and time-sensitive shipments. For heavy, low-value cargo from outside Guangdong, the truck leg may erase the advantage; compare Ningbo or Shanghai.

South China has direct services to several Red Sea ports. Jeddah is listed at 17–31 days port to port, with direct sailings from Shenzhen at about 17–18 days. Sokhna has direct South China services at about 20–23 days; North China cargo often tranships and can take 32–35 days. Aqaba is 20–35 days, Djibouti 19–30 days, and Port Sudan has limited direct capacity.

The direct sailing is usually the simpler product: one vessel, one bill of lading, fewer handovers. A transhipment through Singapore, Colombo or a Middle East hub can be cheaper or the only option in a given week. Ask which port the box connects at, how long the connection is, and what happens if the first vessel is late. For batteries and DG, the connection port's acceptance is part of the routing.

Shenzhen's ocean freight can be competitive on South China direct services, but the total depends on origin charges, trucking and the destination. Yantian and Shekou are different terminals with different cut-offs and truck routes; the quote should name the terminal. For high-value cargo, security and insurance may add cost, and a direct sailing may be worth a premium over a longer connection.

Ask for a line-item quote and compare the same sailing window. A cheap ocean line with a feeder to another South China port, or a transhipment with a short free time, can cost more at destination. If the cargo is batteries or DG, the DG surcharge and the separate allocation are additional lines, not part of the normal ocean freight.

Destination free time is another line. A cheaper sailing with five free days can cost more than a slightly higher sailing with fourteen, especially if the consignee needs time to clear. Ask when free time starts, whether it is calendar or working days, and who pays storage and detention. Those answers matter more than a small difference in the ocean rate.

Shenzhen is a natural fit for electronics, appliances, batteries, e-commerce parcels, high-value consumer goods and time-sensitive shipments. The port handles a lot of DG, but the carrier still decides per UN number and per sailing. Lithium batteries need the right UN number, MSDS, UN38.3 summary, DG declaration and packing; damaged or recalled cells need a separate acceptance.

For furniture, appliances and mixed consumer goods, a 40HQ is usually the volume choice; for dense machinery or hardware, a 20GP may carry more payload. If the cargo is high-value, ask about security, sealing and insurance, and avoid unnecessary handovers. If the cargo is low-value and heavy, the South China truck leg may make another origin cheaper.

Terminal choice matters in Shenzhen. Yantian and Shekou have different sailing lists, cut-offs and truck routes, and a quote that says only “Shenzhen” can hide which one. Ask for the terminal and the latest gate-in time. For e-commerce cargo, ask how the forwarder handles multiple suppliers and whether the cargo can be consolidated before the cut-off. For batteries, ask whether the carrier accepts the watt-hour rating and the state of charge on that specific sailing. A direct sailing from Yantian is not the same product as a feeder from Shekou.
Electronics and high-value goods: direct sailing reduces handovers.
Batteries and DG: carrier approval before booking.
Light consumer goods: 40HQ for volume.
Dense hardware: 20GP first, then check payload.

Jeddah and Sokhna have the strongest direct South China options. Jeddah is about 17–18 days direct; Sokhna about 20–23 days direct. Aqaba and Djibouti can be direct or connect through Singapore, Colombo or a Middle East hub; the connection decides whether the transit is closer to 20 days or 30. Port Sudan usually needs a connection through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti.

If the cargo is for Ethiopia, Djibouti is the gateway and the Ethiopia transit file matters as much as the ocean leg. If the cargo is for Saudi Arabia, Jeddah is the Red Sea gateway; Jebel Ali is in Dubai and is a different customs destination. Do not compare a Jeddah quote with a Jebel Ali quote without adding the inland leg and the import regime.
Jeddah: direct 17–18 days; transhipment up to 31 days.
Sokhna: direct South China 20–23 days.
Aqaba: direct or connection; 20–35 days.
Djibouti: direct 19–24 days; one-stop 25–30 days.
Port Sudan: connect via Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti.

Write down the factory address, cargo-ready date, terminal preference, destination, container type, gross weight, HS code and Incoterms. For batteries or DG, add the UN number, MSDS, UN38.3 summary, packing photos and the carrier approval status. For high-value cargo, add the insurance and security requirements.

Ask for the next two sailings and the routing. If the quote is direct, confirm the vessel and the terminal. If it tranships, confirm the hub and the connection. Do not book a DG cargo as general cargo and declare it later; that can stop the container at the gate and cost more than the freight difference. A complete DG file is part of the booking, not a postscript.
Q: Does Shenzhen have direct sailings to the Red Sea?

A: Yes, for some destinations. Jeddah has direct sailings from Shenzhen at about 17–18 days, and Sokhna has direct South China services at about 20–23 days. Aqaba and Djibouti may be direct or connect through a hub, depending on the carrier. Ask for the routing on the specific sailing.
Q: Can I ship lithium batteries from Shenzhen?

A: Only with carrier approval and the correct UN number, MSDS, UN38.3 summary, DG declaration and packing. The transhipment port must also accept the class. Shenzhen has a lot of battery experience, but that does not make every sailing available; send the file before booking.
Q: Is Shenzhen cheaper than Shanghai for Red Sea cargo?

A: It depends on the destination and the sailing. South China direct services can be competitive to Sokhna and Djibouti, while Shanghai may have more options to Jeddah and Aqaba. Compare the total cost from the factory, including trucking and local charges.

documents.title: 深圳到红海海运：船期、时效与货型
documents.description: 深圳是华南电子、电池和消费品的出海口。红海有直航选择，但危险品要单独拿船公司批复。
documents.lead: 深圳是华南电子、电池和消费品的出海口。红海有直航选择，但危险品要单独拿船公司批复。

richText.text: 深圳是珠三角和深圳、东莞、惠州、广州制造业带的集装箱门户。盐田和蛇口承接华南大量电子、电池、家电、家具和消费品。广东工厂走深圳，拖车短，港口在高价值和危险品货方面经验多。
深圳的优势不只是价格，而是华南直航、密集支线和熟悉出口单证的供应链。适合电子、电商、高价值消费品和时效紧的货。广东以外的重货、低值货，拖车可能把优势吃掉；可以比宁波或上海。
华南到几个红海港口有直航。吉达港到港 17–31 天，深圳直航约 17–18 天。苏赫纳华南直航约 20–23 天；华北货常中转，可能 32–35 天。亚喀巴 20–35 天，吉布提 19–30 天，苏丹港直航有限。
直航通常更简单：一条船、一份提单、交接少。经新加坡、科伦坡或中东枢纽中转，可能更便宜，也可能是当周唯一选择。问清在哪个港衔接、等多久、第一程晚了怎么办。电池和危险品，还要把中转港是否接受算进航线。
深圳海运费在华南直航上可能有竞争力，但总成本还看起运港费用、拖车和目的港。盐田和蛇口是不同的码头，截点和拖车路线不同；报价要写清码头。高价值货还有安保和保险成本，直航比长中转贵一点也可能值得。
要分项报价，并在同一个出运窗口比较。海运费便宜、但要驳到另一个华南港口，或者中转免柜期短，目的港可能更贵。电池或危险品，危险品附加费和单独舱位分配是另外的费用，不是普通海运费的一部分。
目的港免柜期也是费用。便宜 100 美元、只给 5 天免柜的船，可能比贵一点、给 14 天的船更贵，尤其收货人清关需要时间。问免柜从哪天算、按自然日还是工作日、仓储和滞箱谁付。这些答案比海运费差几十美元更重要。
深圳适合电子、家电、电池、电商包裹、高价值消费品和时效紧的货。港口危险品经验多，但船公司仍按 UN 编号和具体船期决定。锂电池要正确 UN 编号、MSDS、UN38.3 摘要、危险品申报和包装；损坏或召回电芯要单独接收。
家具、家电和混合消费品通常用 40HQ 装体积；重机械、五金可能 20GP 装得更多。高价值货要问安保、封条和保险，尽量减少交接。低值重货，华南拖车可能让另一个起运港更便宜。
深圳的码头选择很重要。盐田和蛇口的船期、截点和拖车路线不同，只写“深圳”的报价可能藏着具体码头。问清码头和最晚进闸时间。电商货要问货代怎么处理多个供应商、截点前能否集拼。电池货要问船公司是否接受该票的瓦时数和电量。盐田直航和蛇口驳船不是同一个产品。
电子和高价值货：直航减少交接。
电池和危险品：订舱前拿船公司批复。
轻泡消费品：40HQ 装体积。
重五金：先看 20GP，再核对载重。
吉达和苏赫纳的华南直航最强。吉达直航约 17–18 天，苏赫纳直航约 20–23 天。亚喀巴和吉布提可能直航，也可能经新加坡、科伦坡或中东枢纽衔接；衔接决定是 20 天还是 30 天。苏丹港通常经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接。
货去埃塞俄比亚，吉布提是门户，埃塞过境文件和海上段一样重要。货去沙特，吉达是红海门户；杰贝阿里在迪拜，是另一个海关目的地。吉达报价和杰贝阿里报价，不加上内陆段和进口制度，不能直接比。
吉达：直航 17–18 天；中转最长 31 天。
苏赫纳：华南直航 20–23 天。
亚喀巴：直航或中转；20–35 天。
吉布提：直航 19–24 天；一次中转 25–30 天。
苏丹港：经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接。
写下工厂地址、备货日期、码头偏好、目的港、柜型、毛重、HS 编码和贸易条款。电池或危险品，再加 UN 编号、MSDS、UN38.3 摘要、包装照片和船公司批复状态。高价值货，再加保险和安保要求。
问最近两班船和航线。直航就确认船名和码头；中转就确认枢纽和衔接。危险品不要按普货订舱后再申报；可能在闸口被拒，损失比运费差更大。完整的危险品资料是订舱的一部分，不是事后补的附件。

items.text: 中国到吉布提与埃塞俄比亚

richText.text: 问：深圳有红海直航吗？
答：部分目的港有。深圳到吉达直航约 17–18 天，华南到苏赫纳直航约 20–23 天。亚喀巴和吉布提可能直航，也可能经枢纽衔接，看船公司。按具体船期问航线。
问：深圳能出锂电池吗？
答：要有船公司批复、正确 UN 编号、MSDS、UN38.3 摘要、危险品申报和包装。中转港也要接受该类别。深圳电池货经验多，但不代表每条船都能走；订舱前先发资料。
问：深圳比上海便宜吗？
答：看目的港和船期。华南直航到苏赫纳、吉布提可能有竞争力；上海到吉达、亚喀巴的选择可能更多。要从工厂算总成本，含拖车和本地费用。

documents.title: Qingdao to Red Sea Shipping: Routes & Transit
documents.description: Qingdao is North China's gateway for machinery, tyres and building materials. Most Red Sea sailings connect through a hub.
documents.lead: Qingdao is North China's gateway for machinery, tyres and building materials. Most Red Sea sailings connect through a hub.

body.text: Why Qingdao, and who it suits

richText.text: Qingdao is the main container gateway for Shandong and a practical outlet for Hebei, Henan and other North China manufacturing regions. Its cargo mix is heavier and more industrial than Shenzhen's: machinery, tyres, chemicals, steel, building materials, agricultural equipment and project cargo. For a factory in Shandong, the truck or rail leg to Qingdao is usually the shortest.

The trade-off is connectivity. Qingdao has fewer direct Red Sea calls than Shanghai or Shenzhen, and many shipments connect through Shanghai, Ningbo, Singapore or Colombo. That can add days and a handover. Qingdao suits cost-sensitive, dense or project cargo where the inland leg matters; it is less ideal for a tight delivery date that requires a direct sailing.

The country ranges are port to port: Jeddah 17–31 days, Sokhna 20–35 days, Aqaba 20–35 days, Djibouti 19–30 days. From Qingdao, the longer end of each range is more likely when the sailing connects through a hub. Port Sudan has limited direct capacity and often connects via Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti; a missed connection can add a week or more.

Ask whether the first vessel loads at Qingdao or feeds to another Chinese port. A feeder adds a cut-off and a handover; a connection in Singapore or Colombo adds a hub. Ask for the next two ETDs and the connection window. If the cargo is time-sensitive, compare a Qingdao connection with a Shanghai or Ningbo direct sailing before you decide.

Qingdao's ocean freight can be competitive for dense cargo, but the total includes origin charges, trucking or rail to the port, a possible feeder and the destination charges. The longer transit also has a cost: more working capital, more inventory and a later delivery. For heavy cargo, a 20GP may carry more payload than a 40HQ and reduce the cost per tonne.

Compare line items and the same sailing window. A low ocean line with a feeder to Shanghai and a transhipment in Singapore is a different product from a direct Shanghai sailing. Ask for the free time, the war-risk line and the validity. If the cargo is project cargo, ask about lifting, lashing and road permits separately.

Schedule reliability is part of the cost. A connection that is advertised as one week can become two if the feeder is late or the hub is congested. Ask for the buffer and the next sailing. If the cargo has a fixed delivery date, add a contingency to the budget, not only to the transit time. The cheapest quote is not necessarily the one with the shortest published transit; it is the one whose arrival window you can plan around.

Qingdao is a strong fit for machinery, tyres, chemicals, steel, building materials, agricultural equipment and project cargo. Dense cargo should start with a 20GP and a payload check; light building materials or bulky equipment may need a 40HQ or a flat rack. The port's industrial hinterland means many suppliers are used to export packing and heavy lifts.

Chemicals and batteries are dangerous goods and need a separate acceptance. Do not assume a Qingdao sailing accepts a class because another Chinese port does. For project cargo, check the road from the factory to the port, the lifting capacity and the vessel's gear. A cheap ocean rate cannot fix a cargo that cannot be loaded.

North China cargo often reaches Qingdao by truck or rail. For a factory in Jinan, Zibo or Weifang, the truck leg is manageable; for Hebei or Henan, rail may be cheaper but adds a handover. Ask whether the quote starts at the factory or at the port, and who pays for the rail or truck. For project cargo, a road survey can change the route and the cost before the ocean rate matters. Winter weather can also affect trucking in Shandong, so leave a buffer before the cut-off.
Machinery and project cargo: check lifting, lashing and road permits.
Tyres and dense cargo: 20GP first, then payload.
Building materials: 40HQ for volume, 20GP for weight.
Chemicals and batteries: carrier approval before booking.

Jeddah and Sokhna are the main Red Sea gateways from North China, but the routing often includes a connection. Jeddah is 17–31 days; Sokhna 20–35 days. Aqaba and Djibouti are reachable, with 20–35 and 19–30 days respectively. Port Sudan is the least direct and may require a hub connection through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti.

For Saudi Arabia, Jeddah is the Red Sea destination; Jebel Ali is in Dubai and is not a substitute without the inland leg and the UAE customs regime. For Egypt, Sokhna is the Red Sea port. For Jordan, Aqaba is the only seaport. For Ethiopia, Djibouti is the gateway and the transit file matters. Match the port to the final address before comparing rates.
Jeddah: 17–31 days; often a connection from Qingdao.
Sokhna: 20–35 days; North China transhipment.
Aqaba: 20–35 days; confirm the routing.
Djibouti: 19–30 days; direct or one-stop.
Port Sudan: limited direct; plan the hub.

Write down the factory address, cargo-ready date, destination, container type, gross weight, dimensions, HS code and Incoterms. For project cargo, add the lifting plan and the road survey. For chemicals or batteries, add the UN number, MSDS and packing details. A complete file gets a real routing answer.

Ask for the next two sailings, the connection port and the free time. Compare the Qingdao quote with a Shanghai or Ningbo option on the same cargo and date. The cheapest ocean line may not be the cheapest total once the feeder, the connection and the longer transit are counted. If the two totals are close, choose the shorter inland leg, the clearer free time and the more reliable connection.

items.text: China to Jordan rates and customs

richText.text: Q: Does Qingdao have direct sailings to the Red Sea?

A: Some carriers call directly, but many Qingdao Red Sea shipments connect through Shanghai, Ningbo, Singapore or Colombo. The direct/transhipment mix changes by week. Ask for the connection port and the total transit, not only the ocean leg.
Q: Why is Qingdao transit longer?

A: Qingdao is further north, so the vessel may need a feeder or a connection to join a Red Sea service. The extra handover adds time. The country ranges already include this: Sokhna can be 20–35 days, and Port Sudan has limited direct capacity.
Q: What cargo suits Qingdao?

A: Machinery, tyres, chemicals, steel, building materials and project cargo from Shandong and North China. Dense cargo can use a 20GP; light building materials may need a 40HQ. Dangerous goods need carrier approval and a connection port that accepts the class.

documents.title: 青岛到红海海运：船期、时效与货型
documents.description: 青岛是华北机械、轮胎和建材的出海口。红海航线常经枢纽衔接，所以衔接本身就是时效的一部分。
documents.lead: 青岛是华北机械、轮胎和建材的出海口。红海航线常经枢纽衔接，所以衔接本身就是时效的一部分。

richText.text: 青岛是山东的主要集装箱门户，也是河北、河南等华北制造业的实用出海口。货种比深圳更重、更工业：机械、轮胎、化工品、钢材、建材、农业设备和项目货。山东工厂到青岛的拖车或铁路通常最短。
代价是衔接。青岛的红海直航比上海、深圳少，很多货经上海、宁波、新加坡或科伦坡衔接。这会多几天、多一次交接。青岛适合对成本敏感、货重或项目货、看重内陆段的货主；交期紧、必须直航时，就没那么合适。
目的港区间是港到港：吉达 17–31 天，苏赫纳 20–35 天，亚喀巴 20–35 天，吉布提 19–30 天。从青岛走，经枢纽衔接时更容易落在区间上端。苏丹港直航有限，常经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接；错过衔接可能多等一周以上。
问第一程是在青岛装船，还是驳到另一个中国港口。支线多一个截点和交接；在新加坡或科伦坡衔接多一个枢纽。问最近两个 ETD 和衔接窗口。货急，就把青岛中转和上海/宁波直航放在一起比。
青岛海运费对重货可能有竞争力，但总成本还包括起运港费用、拖车或铁路、可能的支线和目的港费用。更长的时效也有成本：资金占用、库存和更晚交付。重货用 20GP 可能比 40HQ 装得更多，降低每吨成本。
比同一出运窗口的分项报价。海运费低、但要驳到上海再经新加坡中转，和上海直航不是同一个产品。问免柜期、战争风险和有效期。项目货还要单独问吊装、绑扎和公路许可。
船期可靠性也是成本。写着等一周的衔接，支线晚了或枢纽堵了，可能变成两周。问缓冲和下一班船。货有固定交期，预算里要留预备金，不只是时效上留余量。最便宜的报价不一定写着最短航程，而是到货窗口你能安排的那一份。
青岛适合机械、轮胎、化工品、钢材、建材、农业设备和项目货。重货先看 20GP 和载重；轻泡建材或大件设备可能需要 40HQ 或框架柜。港口腹地工业多，供应商通常熟悉出口包装和重吊。
化工品和电池属于危险品，要单独接收。不要以为别的中国港口接受，青岛也一定接受。项目货要核对工厂到港口的道路、吊装能力和船舶设备。海运费再便宜，装不上船也没用。
华北货到青岛，常走拖车或铁路。济南、淄博、潍坊的工厂，拖车可控；河北、河南走铁路可能更省，但多一次交接。问报价从工厂算还是从港口算，铁路或拖车谁付。项目货先做道路勘察，路线和成本可能在比海运费之前就变了。山东冬季天气也会影响拖车，截点前要留缓冲。
机械和项目货：核对吊装、绑扎和公路许可。
轮胎和重货：先看 20GP，再核对载重。
建材：体积货看 40HQ，重货看 20GP。
化工品和电池：订舱前拿船公司批复。
吉达和苏赫纳是华北到红海的主要门户，但航线常含衔接。吉达 17–31 天，苏赫纳 20–35 天。亚喀巴和吉布提也能走，分别 20–35 天和 19–30 天。苏丹港最不直接，可能经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接。
去沙特，吉达是红海目的港；杰贝阿里在迪拜，不加上内陆段和阿联酋海关制度，不能替代。去埃及，苏赫纳是红海港口。去约旦，亚喀巴是唯一海港。去埃塞俄比亚，吉布提是门户，过境文件很重要。先按最终地址选港口，再比运价。
吉达：17–31 天；青岛常需衔接。
苏赫纳：20–35 天；华北常中转。
亚喀巴：20–35 天；确认航线。
吉布提：19–30 天；直航或一次中转。
苏丹港：直航有限；规划枢纽。
写下工厂地址、备货日期、目的港、柜型、毛重、尺寸、HS 编码和贸易条款。项目货加吊装方案和道路勘察。化工品或电池加 UN 编号、MSDS 和包装资料。资料完整，才有真正的航线答案。
问最近两班船、中转港和免柜期。把青岛报价和同一票货、同一日期的上海/宁波方案放在一起比。把支线、衔接和更长时效算进去，海运费最低不一定总成本最低。两个总价接近，就选内陆段更短、免柜期更清楚、衔接更可靠的那个。
