richText.text: 问：青岛有红海直航吗？
答：有船直挂，但很多青岛红海货经上海、宁波、新加坡或科伦坡衔接。直航和中转的比例每周变化。问中转港和总时效，不要只看海上段。
问：青岛的时效为什么更长？
答：青岛位置更北，船可能需要支线或衔接才能接上红海航线。多一次交接就多一段时间。目的港区间已经包含这一点：苏赫纳可能 20–35 天，苏丹港直航有限。
问：什么货适合走青岛？
答：山东和华北的机械、轮胎、化工品、钢材、建材和项目货。重货用 20GP，轻泡建材可能用 40HQ。危险品要船公司批复，且中转港接受该类别。

documents.title: Jordan Import Clearance: Aqaba Guide
documents.description: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport. Most cargo clears on the consignee's tax number, but regulated products need JSMO or JFDA approval before arrival.
documents.lead: Aqaba is Jordan's only seaport. Most cargo clears on the consignee's tax number, but regulated products need JSMO or JFDA approval before arrival.

richText.text: Jordan's import file belongs to a Jordanian importer with an active tax number and an importer card or commercial registration. The importer can be the consignee or a local company acting for it, but the name on the invoice, the bill of lading and the customs declaration has to match. A foreign seller cannot clear the cargo without a local importer or a broker acting for one. Confirm the importer of record before the cargo leaves China.

Aqaba is the only seaport, and the port area sits inside the Aqaba Special Economic Zone (ASEZA). That matters for the tax treatment and for the delivery address. A warehouse inside ASEZA and a warehouse in Amman are not the same customs destination. Ask the consignee for the exact address and whether the goods are entering the zone or moving outside it.

Most goods enter Jordan without a general import licence, but the importer still needs an importer card or commercial registration. Telecommunications and security equipment need a specific licence, and some food and agricultural products need a pre-approval. Regulated goods also need approval from the Jordan Standards and Metrology Organization (JSMO/JISM), and medicines, medical devices and some food products need JFDA registration. The HS code decides which approval applies.

Product approvals take time, and some need samples or a factory audit. If the approval is not ready when the vessel arrives, the container waits and storage starts. Ask the supplier for the test reports, the certificate of conformity and the Arabic label before booking. A certificate issued for another country is not automatically accepted in Jordan.
JSMO/JISM approval for regulated products.
JFDA registration for medicines and medical items.
Arabic labelling and product test reports where required.
HS code checked before the proforma invoice is final.

The core set is a commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading and certificate of origin. The invoice should show the importer's name and tax number, the HS code, the Incoterms, the currency and a clear description of the goods. The bill of lading, invoice and packing list must agree on the quantity, the package count and the consignee. A small mismatch can stop the declaration.

Regulated products add the JSMO/JISM approval, the certificate of conformity and the product label. Food, cosmetics and chemicals may need additional health or safety certificates. Send the draft set to the broker before the vessel sails; the broker can catch a missing field while there is still time to correct it. Do not wait for the arrival notice.

Jordan uses ASYCUDA World for the customs declaration. The broker files the declaration, presents the documents, arranges inspection if required and obtains the release. Clean cargo usually clears in 2–5 working days. The importer pays the duty and the general sales tax before release. Outside ASEZA, the country page lists duty commonly at 5% (0–30%) plus 16% general sales tax; inside ASEZA a flat 5% applies.

The customs value is based on the transaction, and the broker may ask for the freight and insurance breakdown. Keep the commercial invoice and the freight invoice consistent. If the declaration is amended after submission, the release can slip. Ask the broker for the expected release date and the free time before the vessel arrives, not after storage starts.

Aqaba to Amman is a long inland leg, and the route to Irbid or Zarqa can be longer. The trucker needs the release, the delivery order and the consignee's instructions. If the cargo moves from ASEZA to a warehouse outside the zone, the customs status changes; confirm whether a transit document or a new declaration is needed. Do not assume the port release is also the delivery release.

Delivery addresses in Jordan can be informal, so ask for a map pin, a contact and a receiving window. Check whether the truck can enter the site, whether there is a forklift and who unloads. If the consignee cannot take the container, detention continues. For high-value cargo, arrange insurance and a sealed truck; the ocean cover may not extend to the inland leg.

Delivery is not automatic after customs release. The consignee needs a delivery order, a truck booking and a receiving slot. For a warehouse outside Aqaba, the broker may need a transit declaration; for a delivery inside ASEZA, the zone rules apply. Ask who books the truck, who pays the waiting time and who signs the proof of delivery. If the container is not unloaded at the appointment, detention can start before the cargo is stored. A clear delivery plan is part of the clearance, not a separate task.

For high-value cargo, keep the original documents and the release in one handover. Send scanned copies in advance, but do not release the original bill of lading until the payment terms are met. If the consignee uses a broker, confirm the broker's authority in writing. A cargo that is cleared but cannot be delivered is still a cost. Keep the delivery appointment, the truck plate and the receiving contact in writing before the container is released. Written details prevent a gate dispute.

body.text: Local charges: what to ask for

richText.text: Aqaba local charges sit outside the ocean freight. They can include port dues, terminal handling, documentation, delivery order, customs broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit and inland trucking. The amounts vary by terminal, container type and dwell time. Ask for a line-item quote in Jordanian dinars or US dollars, with the exchange rate stated.

Ask what the terminal handling includes, when free time starts, whether it is calendar or working days, and who pays if the consignee cannot collect. For ASEZA cargo, ask whether the zone has a separate charge. A cheap ocean rate with a short free time and an unclear zone charge is not a cheap door price.

items.text: China to Jordan rates and customs

richText.text: Q: How long does clearance at Aqaba take?

A: The country page lists 2–5 working days for clean cargo with complete documents. An inspection, a missing product approval or a mismatch between the invoice and the bill of lading can add time. Free time at Aqaba is often short, so start the clearance file before the vessel arrives.
Q: Do I need an import licence for Jordan?

A: Most goods do not need a general import licence, but the importer needs an importer card or commercial registration, and specific categories such as telecommunications, security equipment, some food and agricultural products need a licence or pre-approval. Regulated products also need JSMO, JFDA or another ministry approval. Confirm the product rules before you ship, not after arrival.
Q: Are Aqaba local charges included in the ocean rate?

A: No. The ocean rate is port-to-port freight. Port dues, terminal handling, documentation, delivery order, broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit and inland trucking are separate. Ask for a line-item destination quote.

documents.title: 约旦进口清关：亚喀巴单证与到门
documents.description: 亚喀巴是约旦唯一的海港。多数货物用收货人的税号清关，但受管制产品要在到港前拿到 JSMO 或 JFDA 的批准。
documents.lead: 亚喀巴是约旦唯一的海港。多数货物用收货人的税号清关，但受管制产品要在到港前拿到 JSMO 或 JFDA 的批准。

richText.text: 约旦的进口文件属于一个有有效税号、并有进口商卡或商业登记的约旦进口商。进口商可以是收货人，也可以是代其操作的当地公司，但发票、提单和报关单上的名称必须一致。外国卖方没有当地进口商或代其申报的报关行，就清不了关。货离开中国前，先确认进口申报主体。
亚喀巴是唯一海港，港区位于亚喀巴经济特区（ASEZA）内。这会影响税务处理和送货地址。特区内仓库和安曼仓库不是同一个海关目的地。让收货人给出准确地址，并说明货是进特区还是转到特区外。
多数货物进入约旦不需要通用进口许可证，但进口商仍要有进口商卡或商业登记。电信和安防设备需要专项许可证，部分食品和农产品需要预批准。受管制商品还要约旦标准计量局（JSMO/JISM）批准；药品、医疗器械和部分食品要 JFDA 注册。HS 编码决定适用哪种批准。
产品批准需要时间，有些还要样品或工厂审核。船到港时批准没下来，柜子就等，仓储开始计费。订舱前向供应商要测试报告、符合性证书和阿拉伯语标签。在其他国家出的证书，约旦不一定直接接受。
受管制产品需 JSMO/JISM 批准。
药品和医疗用品需 JFDA 注册。
需要时的阿拉伯语标签和产品测试报告。
形式发票定稿前核对 HS 编码。
核心单证是商业发票、装箱单、提单和原产地证。发票要写进口商名称和税号、HS 编码、贸易条款、币种和清楚的品名。提单、发票和装箱单在数量、件数和收货人上必须一致。一个小差异就可能让申报卡住。
受管制产品还要 JSMO/JISM 批准、符合性证书和产品标签。食品、化妆品和化工品可能需要额外的卫生或安全证书。开船前把草稿发给报关行；还有时间改的时候，报关行能发现缺项。不要等到到货通知才处理。
约旦使用 ASYCUDA World 报关。报关行提交申报、递交单证、安排查验（如需要）并取得放行。单证齐全的货通常 2–5 个工作日清关。进口商在放行前缴关税和一般销售税。目的港页面写的是：ASEZA 以外关税通常 5%（0–30%）加 16% 一般销售税；ASEZA 内统一 5%。
海关估价按交易价格，报关行可能要运费和保险的明细。商业发票和运费发票要保持一致。申报提交后再改，放行可能往后拖。船到前就问报关行预计放行日和免柜期，不要等仓储开始计费才问。
亚喀巴到安曼是一段长内陆运输，到伊尔比德或扎尔卡可能更远。拖车要放行单、提货单和收货人的指示。货从 ASEZA 转到特区外仓库，海关状态会变；确认是否需要过境单或新的申报。不要以为港口放行就等于可以送货。
约旦的送货地址有时不够正式，要地图定位、联系人和收货时间窗。确认拖车能否进厂、有没有叉车、谁卸货。收货人提不了柜，滞箱继续。高价值货要安排保险和封条车；海运保险不一定覆盖内陆段。
海关放行不等于自动送货。收货人要有提货单、拖车订舱和收货时间窗。送到亚喀巴以外的仓库，报关行可能需要过境申报；送到 ASEZA 内，适用特区规则。问谁订车、谁付等待费、谁签收货单。约了时间没卸成，货还没入库，滞箱就可能开始。清楚的派送计划是清关的一部分，不是另一件事。
高价值货，正本单证和放行文件要在一次交接里点清。可以提前发扫描件，但付款条件没满足前不要放正本提单。收货人用报关行，要书面确认报关行的授权。清关完成却送不到，仍然是成本。放行前把送货预约、车牌和收货联系人写下来。写清楚能减少闸口争议。
亚喀巴当地杂费不在海运费里。可能包括港务费、码头操作、单证、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金和内陆拖车。金额随码头、柜型和停留时间变化。要一份以约旦第纳尔或美元计价的分项报价，并写明汇率。
问码头操作含什么、免柜期从哪天算、按自然日还是工作日、收货人提不了柜时谁付。货进 ASEZA，还要问特区是否有单独收费。海运费便宜、免柜期短、特区费用又没说清，不是便宜的到门价。
港务费和码头操作。
单证、提货单和报关行费用。
查验、仓储和滞港/滞箱。

DDP 与 DAP 到门成本

richText.text: 问：亚喀巴清关要多久？
答：目的港页面写的是单证齐全、无需查验的货通常 2–5 个工作日。遇到查验、缺产品批准，或者发票和提单不一致，就会更久。亚喀巴免柜期常较短，船到前就要开始准备清关文件。
问：去约旦需要进口许可证吗？
答：多数货物不需要通用进口许可证，但进口商要有进口商卡或商业登记；电信、安防设备、部分食品和农产品等特定类别需要许可证或预批准。受管制产品还要 JSMO、JFDA 或其他部门批准。产品规则要在出运前确认，不要等货到。
问：亚喀巴当地费用含在海运费里吗？
答：不含。海运费是港到港运费。港务费、码头操作、单证、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金和内陆拖车都另计。要一份分项目的目的港报价。

documents.title: Sudan Import Clearance: Port Sudan Guide
documents.description: Port Sudan requires an ACD before loading, an SSMO certificate for most goods, and a consignee who can clear and pay.
documents.lead: Port Sudan requires an ACD before loading, an SSMO certificate for most goods, and a consignee who can clear and pay.

richText.text: The import file belongs to a Sudanese importer with an import licence and the bank channel to pay for the goods. The importer, the bank and the broker are three different roles, and each can stop the shipment. Before booking, confirm who holds the licence, who releases the documents and who pays the destination charges. A foreign seller cannot assume the consignee can do all three.

Sudan has been in armed conflict since April 2023, and the operating picture can change. Port Sudan is the working gateway, but port operations, inland roads and banking services may be affected. Confirm the current status with the carrier, the local broker and the consignee before each shipment. A route that worked two months ago is not evidence that it works this month.

Most commercial goods need a Sudanese import licence and an IM form. The licence is product- and importer-specific; it is not a generic permit for any cargo. The consignee should confirm the licence covers the HS code and the quantity before the proforma invoice is final. If the licence does not match, the cargo can be stopped before loading or at destination.

Most goods also need an SSMO certificate of inspection from an authorised agency before leaving China. The ACD is separate: it is the advance cargo declaration, and it must be obtained before loading for vessels sailing from 1 January 2026. Do not confuse the three. The ACD is not an import licence, and the SSMO certificate is not a customs declaration.
Import licence covering the HS code and quantity.
IM form for the import file.
SSMO inspection certificate before leaving China.
ACD 15-digit number before loading.

The ACD application needs the draft bill of lading, commercial invoice, freight invoice, certificate of origin and packing list. Once issued, the 15-digit number must appear on the bill of lading. The invoice should show the importer, the HS code, the Incoterms and a clear description. The packing list should match the invoice and the container load.

The SSMO certificate, import licence and IM form sit alongside the core set. Some products need additional health, agricultural or standards approvals. Send the draft set to the broker before the cargo leaves the factory. The broker can check the Arabic description, the HS code and the licence match while there is still time to correct them.

A local broker files the customs declaration with the consignee, presents the documents, arranges inspection if required and obtains the delivery order. The consignee needs the import registration, the licence and the bank documents. The port and the terminal have their own release process. Clearance is not finished when the vessel arrives; it is finished when the delivery order is issued and the container can move.

Duty is 5–25% for most goods, plus 17% VAT, according to the country page. The HS code and the declared value decide the amount. A broker can give an estimate, but the customs authority decides. Do not treat a broker's verbal estimate as a fixed landed cost. Ask for the duty and VAT assumptions in writing, separately from the local charges.

Port Sudan to Khartoum and other cities is a separate operation with its own risk and cost. Roads, checkpoints and fuel availability can change. Insurance may exclude war and related risks, so confirm the cover with the insurer, not only the freight forwarder. If the consignee cannot arrange the inland leg, the container may sit at the port and storage will start.

Ask for the inland carrier's name, the truck plate and the delivery contact before the container is released. Confirm whether the cargo needs an escort, a permit or a specific route. For high-value or sensitive cargo, consider splitting the shipment and keeping one part at the port until the inland leg is confirmed. A single large shipment is harder to recover if the route changes.

Port storage is the clock that matters after discharge. The consignee should have the broker, the bank and the truck ready before the vessel arrives, because a missing document can turn into a storage bill. For inland delivery, ask for a written route plan and a contact at each checkpoint. Keep a copy of the ACD, the bill of lading and the customs declaration in the truck. If the route changes, stop and confirm before the container moves; a truck stuck between checkpoints is harder to recover than a container waiting at the port.

Cash and fuel can be practical constraints. Confirm who pays the truck, the fuel and any local handling, and whether the driver can use the agreed route. For high-value cargo, split the shipment or keep part at the port until the first truck completes the route. A plan that assumes the road is unchanged is not a plan. Confirm the truck's fuel, cash and communication plan before the container is released, and keep a written copy at the port. A written plan is better than a phone promise.

body.text: Local charges: what to ask for

richText.text: Port Sudan local charges sit outside the ocean freight. They can include port dues, terminal handling, documentation, delivery order, customs broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit, inland transport and bank charges. The amounts vary by terminal, container type and dwell time. Ask for a line-item quote and the currency.

Ask what the terminal handling includes, when free time starts, who pays storage if the consignee cannot take the box, and whether the broker's fee includes the inspection attendance. A cheap ocean rate with a large, undisclosed destination charge is not a cheap route. The country page and the Port Sudan guide list the document checks in more detail.

items.text: China to Sudan rates and ACD
Port Sudan clearance and local charges

richText.text: Q: What is the ACD for Sudan?

A: The Advance Cargo Declaration is a 15-digit number required for Sudan-bound cargo on vessels sailing from 1 January 2026. It must be obtained before loading in China and printed on the bill of lading. The application uses the draft bill of lading, commercial invoice, freight invoice, certificate of origin and packing list.
Q: How long does shipping to Port Sudan take?

A: There is no single reliable range. Direct sailings from China are limited, and much cargo tranships through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti. The connection decides the transit, and a missed connection can add a week or more. Ask for the routing and the connection port on every quote.
Q: Are Port Sudan local charges included in the ocean rate?

A: No. Port dues, terminal handling, documentation, delivery order, broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit and inland transport are separate. Ask for a line-item destination quote before you compare two ocean rates.

documents.lead: 苏丹港要求装船前办 ACD、多数商品有 SSMO 证书，收货人还要能清关和付款。订舱前先确认港口和银行情况。

richText.text: 进口文件属于一个有进口许可证、且有银行付款渠道的苏丹进口商。进口商、银行和报关行是三个角色，任何一个都可能让货走不动。订舱前确认许可证在谁名下、谁赎单、谁付目的港费用。外国卖方不能假设收货人三件事都能办。
苏丹自 2023 年 4 月起处于武装冲突中，运营情况可能变化。苏丹港是目前可用的门户，但港口作业、内陆道路和银行服务都可能受影响。每票货出运前，向船公司、当地报关行和收货人确认当前状态。两个月前能走的路线，不代表这个月还能走。
多数商品需要苏丹进口许可证和 IM 表。许可证按产品和进口商签发，不是任何货都能用的通用许可。形式发票定稿前，收货人要确认许可证覆盖该 HS 编码和数量。许可证不匹配，货可能在装船前或目的港被拦。
多数商品出运前还要由授权机构出具苏丹标准计量局（SSMO）检验证书。ACD 是另一件事：它是预先货物申报，2026 年 1 月 1 日起开航的船必须在装船前取得。三者不要混。ACD 不是进口许可证，SSMO 证书也不是报关单。
覆盖 HS 编码和数量的进口许可证。
进口文件中的 IM 表。
出运前的 SSMO 检验证书。
装船前的 ACD 15 位编号。
ACD 申请需要提单草稿、商业发票、运费发票、原产地证和装箱单。编号出来后，15 位数字必须出现在提单上。发票要写进口商、HS 编码、贸易条款和清楚品名。装箱单要和发票、柜内装载一致。
SSMO 证书、进口许可证和 IM 表和核心单证放在一起。部分产品还要卫生、农业或标准方面的额外批准。货离开工厂前，把草稿发给报关行。报关行还有时间改的时候，可以核对阿拉伯语品名、HS 编码和许可证是否匹配。
当地报关行和收货人提交报关、递交单证、安排查验（如需要）并取得提货单。收货人要有进口登记、许可证和银行单证。港口和码头还有自己的放货流程。清关不是船到就结束，而是提货单出来、柜子能走才算结束。
根据目的港页面，多数货物关税 5–25%，另加 17% 增值税。HS 编码和申报货值决定金额。报关行可以给估算，但最终由海关决定。不要把报关行口头估算当成固定的到岸成本。让报关行把关税和增值税假设书面列出，和当地杂费分开。
从苏丹港到喀土穆和其他城市，是另一套操作，有自己的风险和成本。道路、检查站和燃油供应都可能变化。保险可能排除战争及相关风险，要向保险方确认承保范围，不要只问货代。收货人安排不了内陆段，柜子就可能压在港口，仓储开始计费。
柜子放行前，问清内陆承运人名称、车牌和收货联系人。确认货是否需要押运、许可或特定路线。高价值或敏感货，可以考虑分票，先留一部分在港口，等内陆段确认再走。路线一变，一票大货更难调整。
卸船后，港口仓储就是计时器。船到前，收货人要把报关行、银行和拖车都准备好；少一份单证，就可能变成一笔仓储费。内陆派送要书面路线计划和每个检查站的联系人。车上带 ACD、提单和报关单副本。路线变了，先停下来确认再走；车卡在检查站之间，比柜子留在港口更难处理。
现金和燃油是实际约束。确认拖车、燃油和当地操作由谁付，司机能否走约定路线。高价值货可以分票，或者先留一部分在港口，等第一车走通再发。假设道路不会变的计划，不算计划。放行前确认拖车的燃油、现金和通信方案，并在港口留一份书面记录。书面计划比电话承诺可靠。
苏丹港当地杂费不在海运费里。可能包括港务费、码头操作、单证、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金、内陆运输和银行费用。金额随码头、柜型和停留时间变化。要分项报价，并写清币种。
问码头操作含什么、免柜期从哪天算、收货人提不了柜时仓储谁付、报关行费用是否含查验陪同。海运费便宜、目的港却有一大笔没说清的费用，不是便宜的航线。目的港页面和苏丹港指南有更详细的单证核对。

items.text: 中国到苏丹运价与 ACD
苏丹港清关与当地杂费

richText.text: 问：苏丹的 ACD 是什么？
答：预先货物申报（ACD）是 2026 年 1 月 1 日起开航的去苏丹货物必须办理的 15 位编号。须在中国装船前取得，并打印在提单上。申请要用提单草稿、商业发票、运费发票、原产地证和装箱单。
问：到苏丹港要多久？
答：没有一个可靠统一的数字。中国直航有限，很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提中转。衔接决定时效，错过衔接可能多等一周以上。每份报价都要问航线和衔接港。
问：苏丹港当地费用含在海运费里吗？
答：不含。港务费、码头操作、单证、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金和内陆运输都另计。比较两份海运费之前，先要一份分项目的目的港报价。

documents.title: Djibouti Clearance & Ethiopia Transit
documents.description: Djibouti is two flows in one port: local Djibouti cargo and Ethiopia-bound transit. The ECTN and the Ethiopia import file decide which one you are in.
documents.lead: Djibouti is two flows in one port: local Djibouti cargo and Ethiopia-bound transit. The ECTN and the Ethiopia import file decide which one you are in.

richText.text: Djibouti handles local imports for its own market and transit cargo for landlocked Ethiopia. The two flows use different documents, different customs treatments and often different brokers. Local cargo is cleared into Djibouti; Ethiopia-bound cargo moves under customs bond to the border and then to Modjo dry port. Before you book, decide which flow your cargo belongs to.

The ECTN is the first filter. Since 15 June 2023, containers unloaded in Djibouti need an ECTN, unless the cargo is in direct transit to Ethiopia and the bill of lading says “In transit to Ethiopia” with an Ethiopian consignee. The exemption is checked on the documents, not on a verbal instruction. If the wording is wrong, the cargo can be treated as local import.

For local Djibouti imports, the consignee needs a registered importer and a broker. For Ethiopia-bound cargo, the Ethiopian importer needs an import licence and foreign-exchange approval through an Ethiopian bank before shipping. The licence and the bank permit are Ethiopian documents, not Djibouti documents, but the Djibouti transit file has to match them.

The Ethiopia import licence is product-specific, and the bank permit is tied to the invoice and the supplier. If the licence does not cover the HS code, or the bank permit does not match the invoice, the cargo can reach Djibouti and still not move. Confirm both before the vessel sails. A late correction can take longer than the ocean leg.
Djibouti local importer registration and broker.
Ethiopia import licence covering the HS code.
Ethiopian bank permit and FX approval.
ECTN or the exact Ethiopia transit wording on the bill of lading.

The ECTN application typically needs the bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin and freight invoice. For Ethiopia transit, add the Ethiopian import declaration, the bank permit and the transit documents required by the corridor. The bill of lading, invoice and packing list must agree on the consignee, the quantity and the description.

The Ethiopia-side broker and the Djibouti-side broker are often different companies. Make one of them the owner of the full chain, or define the handover point in writing. The most common failure is not the ocean leg; it is a document that arrives after the container, or a transit paper that does not match the Ethiopian declaration. Put the document list and the handover point in the booking confirmation.

A local broker files the Djibouti declaration and obtains the delivery order. Local cargo is cleared into Djibouti. Transit cargo moves under customs bond to the border and then to Modjo dry port, where the Ethiopian declaration is completed. The rail takes about 12–15 hours; the road takes about 2–5 days. The total door-to-door time includes terminal handling at both ends and the train or truck schedule.

Modjo is a dry port, not the final address. Cargo can be cleared there and delivered locally, or moved onward. The consignee needs a broker who can handle the dry-port release, and the trucker needs the right documents to collect the container. If the container is not returned within the free time, detention continues even after the cargo is unloaded.

For Djibouti local delivery, confirm the address, the truck access and the unloading arrangement. For Ethiopia, confirm the final warehouse, the Modjo release and the truck or rail booking. The delivery address may be in Addis Ababa or another city; Modjo is only the customs point. Do not quote a door price to Addis if the quote stops at Modjo.

Ask who returns the empty container, where it goes and by when. The free time may start at discharge or at availability, and the rail or road leg can eat most of it. If the consignee cannot return the box, detention can exceed the value of the cargo. Put the empty-return responsibility in the booking confirmation, not in a phone call.

Rail and road are not interchangeable. The rail has a fixed schedule and terminal handling at both ends; the road is more flexible but depends on the border and the truck. Ask for the train cut-off, the Modjo release and the empty-return point before you choose. If the consignee needs the cargo in Addis on a specific date, compare the total door-to-door time, not only the line-haul time. A rail booking that misses the train can be slower than a road trip that leaves on time.

For local Djibouti delivery, confirm the address and the truck access. For Ethiopia, confirm the final warehouse and who clears at Modjo. Do not let the Djibouti broker and the Ethiopia broker each assume the other has booked the next leg. The handover point should be written, with a name and a phone number. Write the handover point, the named contact and the document list into the booking confirmation before the vessel arrives, not into a chat message that disappears, and keep a copy with the driver. The written handover is the one both brokers can follow.

body.text: Local charges: what to ask for

richText.text: Djibouti local charges sit outside the ocean freight. They can include port dues, terminal handling, documentation, ECTN fee, delivery order, customs broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit and the onward rail or road leg. The amounts vary by terminal, container type and dwell time. Ask for the Djibouti port charges and the Ethiopia transit charges as separate lines.

Ask what the ECTN fee covers, when free time starts, whether storage is charged by calendar or working day, and who pays the dry-port handling at Modjo. A single lump sum hides the part that will grow. The Djibouti port guide and the country page list the document checks in more detail.
Port dues and terminal handling.
Documentation, ECTN and broker fees.
Storage, demurrage and detention.
Container deposit, rail or road and dry-port handling.
Q: Do I need an ECTN for Djibouti?

A: Yes, since 15 June 2023. The ECTN must be obtained before loading and the number shown on the bill of lading. Cargo in direct transit to Ethiopia is exempt when the bill of lading states “In transit to Ethiopia” and the consignee is in Ethiopia. The exemption is documentary, so the wording must be exact.
Q: How long does Djibouti to Addis Ababa take?

A: The rail takes about 12–15 hours and the road about 2–5 days, plus clearance at Djibouti and Modjo. The ocean leg is 19–24 days direct or 25–30 days with one transhipment. The Ethiopia import licence and foreign exchange can add time before the cargo moves.
Q: Are Djibouti local charges included in the ocean rate?

A: No. Port dues, terminal handling, documentation, ECTN fee, delivery order, broker, inspection, storage, demurrage, detention, container deposit, rail or road and dry-port charges are separate. Ask for the Djibouti port charges and the Ethiopia transit charges as separate lines.

documents.title: 吉布提清关与埃塞俄比亚过境
documents.description: 吉布提港同时处理两类货：吉布提本地货和去埃塞俄比亚的过境货。ECTN 和埃塞进口文件决定你走哪一类。
documents.lead: 吉布提港同时处理两类货：吉布提本地货和去埃塞俄比亚的过境货。ECTN 和埃塞进口文件决定你走哪一类。

richText.text: 吉布提既处理本国进口，也处理内陆国埃塞俄比亚的过境货。两类货的单证、海关处理和报关行往往不同。本地货清关进入吉布提；去埃塞的货在海关监管下运到边境，再到 Modjo 陆港。订舱前先确定你的货属于哪一类。
ECTN 是第一道筛选。自 2023 年 6 月 15 日起，在吉布提卸货的集装箱需要 ECTN；直接过境埃塞俄比亚、提单注明“In transit to Ethiopia”且收货人在埃塞的货物可免。豁免按单证审核，不认口头说明。措辞不对，货可能被按本地进口处理。
吉布提本地进口，收货人要有注册进口商和报关行。去埃塞俄比亚的货，埃塞进口商要在出运前持有进口许可证，并通过埃塞银行取得外汇批准。许可证和银行许可是埃塞文件，不是吉布提文件，但吉布提过境文件必须和它们一致。
埃塞进口许可证按产品签发，银行许可和发票、供应商绑定。许可证不覆盖 HS 编码，或者银行许可和发票不一致，货到了吉布提也走不了。开船前把两者确认好。事后改，可能比海上段还久。
吉布提本地进口商注册和报关行。
覆盖 HS 编码的埃塞进口许可证。
埃塞银行许可和外汇批准。
ECTN 或提单上准确的埃塞过境措辞。
ECTN 申请通常需要提单、商业发票、装箱单、原产地证和运费发票。去埃塞过境，还要埃塞进口申报、银行许可和走廊要求的过境单证。提单、发票和装箱单在收货人、数量和品名上必须一致。
埃塞一侧和吉布提一侧的报关行往往是两家公司。让其中一家负责全链条，或者把交接点写清楚。最常见的失败不在海上，而是单证比柜子晚到，或者过境纸和埃塞申报不一致。把单证清单和交接点写进订舱确认。
当地报关行提交吉布提申报并取得提货单。本地货清关进入吉布提。过境货在海关监管下运到边境，再到 Modjo 陆港完成埃塞申报。铁路约 12–15 小时，公路约 2–5 天。门到门总时长还要加两端的码头操作和铁路或卡车班期。
Modjo 是陆港，不是最终地址。货可以在那里清关后再本地派送，也可以继续转运。收货人要有能处理陆港放货的报关行，拖车要有正确单证才能提柜。柜子没有在免柜期内还回，哪怕货已经卸了，滞箱费还会继续。
吉布提本地派送，确认地址、拖车进出和卸货安排。去埃塞，确认最终仓库、Modjo 放货和铁路或卡车订舱。送货地址可能在亚的斯亚贝巴或其他城市；Modjo 只是海关点。报价到 Modjo 为止，就不要说成到亚的斯门到门。
问清空柜由谁还、还到哪里、什么时候还。免柜期可能从卸船算，也可能从可提货算，铁路或公路段会吃掉大部分时间。收货人还不了柜，滞箱费可能超过货值。把空柜返还责任写进订舱确认，不要只打电话说。
铁路和公路不能互换。铁路班期固定，两端有码头操作；公路更灵活，但取决于口岸和车辆。选择前问清铁路截点、Modjo 放货和空柜返还点。收货人要在某天到亚的斯，就比门到门总时长，不要只比干线时间。铁路订舱错过班列，可能比按时出发的公路更慢。
吉布提本地派送，确认地址和拖车进出。去埃塞，确认最终仓库和 Modjo 由谁清关。不要让吉布提报关行和埃塞报关行都以为对方订了下一段。交接点要写下来，有名字和电话。把交接点、联系人和单证清单写进订舱确认，不要只发一条会消失的聊天消息，并让司机带一份。书面交接是两边都能执行的版本。
吉布提当地杂费不在海运费里。可能包括港务费、码头操作、单证、ECTN 费、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金和后续铁路或公路段。金额随码头、柜型和停留时间变化。吉布提港杂费和埃塞过境费要分开列。
问 ECTN 费含什么、免柜期从哪天算、仓储按自然日还是工作日、Modjo 陆港操作谁付。一个总数会把以后会涨的那部分藏起来。吉布提港口指南和目的港页面有更详细的单证核对。

吉布提清关与当地杂费

richText.text: 问：去吉布提需要 ECTN 吗？
答：需要，自 2023 年 6 月 15 日起。ECTN 须在装船前取得，编号显示在提单上。直接过境到埃塞俄比亚的货物，在提单注明“In transit to Ethiopia”且收货人在埃塞俄比亚时可豁免。豁免是单证层面的，措辞必须准确。
问：吉布提到亚的斯亚贝巴要多久？
答：铁路约 12–15 小时，公路约 2–5 天，另加吉布提和 Modjo 的清关。海上段直航约 19–24 天，一次中转约 25–30 天。埃塞进口许可证和外汇可能让货在转运前多等。
问：吉布提当地费用含在海运费里吗？
答：不含。港务费、码头操作、单证、ECTN 费、提货单、报关行、查验、仓储、滞港、滞箱、柜押金、铁路或公路和陆港费用都另计。要一份把吉布提港杂费和埃塞过境费分开列出的报价。

documents.title: Red Sea vs Jebel Ali: Which Gateway?
documents.description: Jebel Ali is in Dubai, not on the Red Sea. The right gateway depends on the final address, the import regime and the inland leg.
documents.lead: Jebel Ali is in Dubai, not on the Red Sea. The right gateway depends on the final address, the import regime and the inland leg.

body.text: They are not the same product

richText.text: Jebel Ali is a UAE port in Dubai. Jeddah, Sokhna, Aqaba, Djibouti and Port Sudan are Red Sea ports in five different countries. The ocean leg may start from the same Chinese origin, but the destination country, the import regime, the duty, the documents and the inland leg are different. A quote to Jebel Ali and a quote to Jeddah answer different questions, even if both say “Middle East”.

The first question is the final address, not the port. If the warehouse is in Dubai, Jebel Ali is the natural gateway. If it is in Riyadh, Jeddah is the Red Sea gateway; Jebel Ali plus a truck is a different routing with a different customs file. If it is in Cairo, Sokhna is the Red Sea port. If it is in Amman, Aqaba. If it is in Addis Ababa, Djibouti. If it is in Khartoum, Port Sudan.

Jebel Ali is the right choice when the final destination is in the UAE, or when the cargo is genuinely transhipping through the UAE to another market. It has frequent sailings, a large hub network and a mature Dubai trading ecosystem. The site's Jebel Ali page lists a 26-day direct sailing from China and a separate market reference; it is deliberately outside the Red Sea index because it is a different destination.

Jebel Ali can also be a transhipment hub for Red Sea cargo, but that is a routing decision, not a final destination. If the box is transhipped at Jebel Ali and then moves to a Red Sea port, the quote should name the connection and the final port. Do not compare the Jebel Ali ocean leg with a Red Sea door price as if they were the same.
Final address in the UAE: Jebel Ali is the natural port.
Transhipment through the UAE: name the final port and connection.
Dubai trading or free-zone cargo: confirm the customs regime.
Do not treat Jebel Ali as a Saudi or Egyptian destination.

body.text: When a Red Sea port wins

richText.text: A Red Sea port wins when the final address is in its hinterland and the cargo can clear there. Jeddah serves Saudi Arabia; Sokhna serves Egypt; Aqaba serves Jordan; Djibouti serves Djibouti and Ethiopia; Port Sudan serves Sudan. A direct call to that port avoids a second customs regime and an extra inland leg. For time-sensitive cargo, that can matter more than a lower ocean line through a hub.

The Red Sea port is not automatically cheaper. War-risk surcharges, congestion and a shorter free time can make it more expensive than a Jebel Ali routing on paper. The point is to compare the delivered cost and the risk, not the ocean line. A port with a direct call but no empty equipment or no truck is not a working option.
Saudi Arabia: Jeddah is the Red Sea gateway.
Egypt: Sokhna serves Cairo and the Suez zone.
Jordan: Aqaba is the only seaport.
Djibouti/Ethiopia: Djibouti is the gateway; Modjo is the dry port.
Sudan: Port Sudan is the working gateway.

Build the comparison from the factory to the final address. Include origin charges, ocean freight, war risk, destination port charges, customs broker, duty, VAT, inland trucking, insurance and the cost of one extra week of transit. For Jebel Ali plus a road into Saudi Arabia, add the UAE entry or transit cost, the border clearance and the Saudi inland leg. For a Red Sea port, add the local delivery and any storage.

Do not compare a port-to-port ocean rate with a door price. Do not compare a Jebel Ali quote that stops at the UAE border with a Jeddah quote that includes Saudi clearance. Put the same Incoterms, the same HS code, the same delivery address and the same free time in front of both. If one quote has a different scope, the difference is not a saving; it is a missing line.

Jebel Ali and the Red Sea ports have different import rules. Saudi Arabia needs SABER; Egypt needs ACID; Jordan needs its own customs declaration and product approvals; Djibouti needs ECTN, with an exemption for Ethiopia transit; Sudan needs ACD and SSMO. A Jebel Ali routing may need a UAE entry or a transit bond, plus the destination country's import file. Two customs regimes mean two sets of documents.

For dangerous goods, batteries and high-value cargo, the extra handover is a risk. A Jebel Ali transhipment may accept a class that a Red Sea feeder does not, or the other way around. Ask each carrier and each port. For high-value cargo, the security and insurance of the inland leg matter as much as the ocean leg.

Write down the final address, the importer, the HS code, the Incoterms, the delivery date and the free time. Then ask for two quotes: one to the Red Sea port and one to Jebel Ali, each with the full scope to the final address. If the Jebel Ali quote stops at the UAE, ask for the border and inland lines. If the Red Sea quote stops at the port, ask for the delivery line.

Choose the route with the lower delivered cost and the risk you can manage. If the cargo is time-sensitive, a direct Red Sea call may win even at a higher ocean rate. If the final address is in Dubai, Jebel Ali wins. If the final address is in Saudi Arabia, compare Jeddah with Jebel Ali plus road only when you have the full customs and inland numbers. The port name is not the answer; the final address is the answer, not the port name. The final address decides the route, not the port name.
Q: Is Jebel Ali a Red Sea port?

A: No. Jebel Ali is in Dubai, in the United Arab Emirates. It is a major hub for the UAE and for transhipment, but it is not one of the five Red Sea destinations on this site. A Jebel Ali quote is not a substitute for a Jeddah, Sokhna, Aqaba, Djibouti or Port Sudan quote.
Q: Can I use Jebel Ali for Saudi cargo?

A: It can be part of a routing, but it is not the same product as Jeddah. Cargo would need a UAE customs entry or a transit regime, then a road leg into Saudi Arabia, with Saudi import clearance at the border. Compare the total cost and the customs risk with a direct Jeddah quote before choosing.
Q: Which gateway is cheaper?

A: There is no general answer. A Jebel Ali ocean rate may look lower, but the UAE charges, the inland leg and the second customs regime can add more. A Red Sea port may have a higher ocean line but a shorter inland leg and one import file. Compare the delivered cost to the final address.

documents.title: 红海还是杰贝阿里：怎么选门户？
documents.description: 杰贝阿里在迪拜，不在红海。选门户要看最终地址、进口制度和内陆段，不能只看海运费。
documents.lead: 杰贝阿里在迪拜，不在红海。选门户要看最终地址、进口制度和内陆段，不能只看海运费。

richText.text: 杰贝阿里是阿联酋迪拜的港口。吉达、苏赫纳、亚喀巴、吉布提和苏丹港是五个不同国家的红海港口。海上段可能从同一个中国起运港出发，但目的国、进口制度、关税、单证和内陆段都不同。杰贝阿里报价和吉达报价回答的是不同问题，哪怕都写着“中东”。
第一个问题是最终地址，不是港口。仓库在迪拜，杰贝阿里是自然门户。仓库在利雅得，吉达是红海门户；杰贝阿里加拖车是另一条航线、另一套海关文件。仓库在开罗，苏赫纳是红海港口。在安曼，亚喀巴。在亚的斯亚贝巴，吉布提。在喀土穆，苏丹港。
最终目的地在阿联酋，或者货确实要经阿联酋转口到其他市场，杰贝阿里才合适。它船期密、枢纽网络大、迪拜贸易生态成熟。本站杰贝阿里页面列了 26 天直航和单独的市场参考；它不属于红海指数，因为目的地不同。
杰贝阿里也可以做红海货的中转枢纽，但那是航线选择，不是最终目的地。柜子在杰贝阿里中转、再运到红海港口，报价要写清衔接和最终目的港。不要把杰贝阿里海上段和红海到门价比成同一个产品。
最终地址在阿联酋：杰贝阿里是自然门户。
经阿联酋转口：写清最终目的港和衔接。
迪拜贸易或自由区货：确认海关制度。
不要把杰贝阿里当成沙特或埃及目的港。
最终地址在港口腹地、且能在那里清关，红海港口就赢。吉达服务沙特，苏赫纳服务埃及，亚喀巴服务约旦，吉布提服务吉布提和埃塞俄比亚，苏丹港服务苏丹。直挂该港可以少一套海关制度、少一段内陆运输。时效紧的货，这可能比经枢纽的低海运费更重要。
红海港口不一定更便宜。战争风险附加费、拥堵和较短的免柜期，可能让它在纸面上比杰贝阿里路线更贵。要比到门成本和风险，不是比海运费。有直航、但没箱源或没拖车的港口，不是可执行的选项。
沙特：吉达是红海门户。
埃及：苏赫纳服务开罗和苏伊士区。
约旦：亚喀巴是唯一海港。
吉布提/埃塞：吉布提是门户，Modjo 是陆港。
苏丹：苏丹港是可用门户。
从工厂算到最终地址。包括起运港费用、海运费、战争风险、目的港费用、报关行、关税、增值税、内陆拖车、保险和多一周时效的成本。杰贝阿里加陆运进沙特，还要加阿联酋进口或过境费用、边境清关和沙特内陆段。红海港口则加本地派送和可能的仓储。
不要拿港到港海运费和到门价比。不要拿只到阿联酋边境的杰贝阿里报价，和含沙特清关的吉达报价比。两份报价用同一贸易条款、同一 HS 编码、同一送货地址和同一免柜期。口径不同，差额不是省钱，是少了一行。
杰贝阿里和红海港口的进口规则不同。沙特要 SABER，埃及要 ACID，约旦有自己的报关和产品批准，吉布提要 ECTN（埃塞过境可免），苏丹要 ACD 和 SSMO。杰贝阿里路线可能要阿联酋进口或过境保函，再加目的国的进口文件。两套海关制度就是两套单证。
危险品、电池和高价值货，多一次交接就是多一个风险。杰贝阿里中转接受的类别，红海支线可能不接受，反过来也一样。船公司和港口要分别问。高价值货，内陆段的安保和保险和海上段一样重要。
写下最终地址、进口商、HS 编码、贸易条款、交期和免柜期。然后要两份报价：一份到红海港口，一份到杰贝阿里，都要含到最终地址的完整范围。杰贝阿里报价只到阿联酋，就补边境和内陆段；红海报价只到港口，就补派送段。
选到门成本更低、风险你能管的那条。货急，红海直航哪怕海运费高也可能赢。最终地址在迪拜，杰贝阿里赢。最终地址在沙特，只有在拿到完整海关和内陆数字后，才把吉达和杰贝阿里加陆运放在一起比。港口名字不是答案，最终地址才是。最终地址决定路线，不是港口名字。
问：杰贝阿里是红海港口吗？
答：不是。杰贝阿里在阿联酋迪拜，是阿联酋和转口的重要枢纽，但不是本站五个红海目的港之一。杰贝阿里报价不能替代吉达、苏赫纳、亚喀巴、吉布提或苏丹港报价。
问：去沙特的货能走杰贝阿里吗？
答：可以作为航线的一部分，但和吉达不是同一个产品。货要先在阿联酋清关或走过境，再陆运进沙特，在边境完成沙特进口清关。选择前把总成本和海关风险与吉达直航报价一起比。
问：哪个门户更便宜？
答：没有统一答案。杰贝阿里海运费可能看起来低，但阿联酋费用、内陆段和第二套海关制度可能加得更多。红海港口海运费可能高，但内陆段短、只有一套进口文件。比到最终地址的总成本。

documents.title: Direct vs Transhipment to the Red Sea
documents.description: Direct and transhipment are different products. Direct is not always faster, and transhipment is not always cheaper. Compare the connection and total cost.
documents.lead: Direct and transhipment are different products. Direct is not always faster, and transhipment is not always cheaper. Compare the connection and total cost.

richText.text: A direct sailing carries the container from the Chinese origin to the Red Sea destination on one vessel. A transhipment carries it on a first vessel to a hub, then on a second vessel to the destination. The hub can be Jeddah, Jebel Ali, Djibouti, Colombo, Singapore or another port. The connection is the time the box waits at the hub, and it is part of the transit.

A feeder is not the same as a transhipment, but it has the same effect for the shipper: an extra handover. A feeder may move the box from Ningbo to Shanghai, or from Qingdao to a larger load port, before the ocean vessel. Ask whether the quote includes a feeder, a transhipment, or both. Each handover has a cut-off and a responsibility gap.

Direct wins when the cargo is time-sensitive, high-value, fragile or dangerous. Fewer handovers mean fewer chances for a delay, a document mismatch or damage. Direct also wins when the destination free time is short: a transhipment can eat several days at the hub before the box even arrives. For a project cargo or a production line, the simpler routing is often worth a higher ocean line.

Direct is not a guarantee. A direct vessel can be late, full or omit a port, and a direct quote can still have a feeder at the origin. Ask what “direct” means in the quote: one vessel from the named origin to the named destination, or a feeder plus one ocean vessel. If the quote cannot name the vessel and the routing, the label is doing too much work.
Time-sensitive or high-value cargo: fewer handovers.
Dangerous goods: confirm the direct vessel accepts the class.
Short free time: direct avoids hub waiting.
Project cargo: one vessel is easier to control.

Transhipment wins when there is no direct space, the direct sailing is too expensive, or the destination has limited direct calls. Port Sudan is the clearest example: direct capacity from China is limited, so much cargo connects through Jeddah, Jebel Ali or Djibouti. A transhipment can also be the only way to reach a port with a small direct service.

Transhipment can be cheaper on the ocean line, but the saving is not automatic. The extra handover can add destination charges, a second set of documents and a longer free-time risk. If the cargo is flexible and the connection is clean, the total can be lower. If the connection is tight or the hub is congested, the saving can disappear in storage and detention.
No direct space in the sailing window.
Destination with limited direct calls, such as Port Sudan.
Flexible cargo and a clean connection.
Lower ocean line that survives the total-cost check.

The first missing line is the connection wait. A quote may show 30 days, but the box can sit at the hub for a week before the second vessel. The second is the destination charge: a transhipment can add handling, documentation and a delivery order at the hub or at destination. The third is the free time: it may start at discharge, and the connection can use it up before the consignee clears.

The fourth is the missed-connection cost. If the first vessel is late, who pays the storage, the rebooking and the new freight? The fifth is insurance: the cover may not respond the same way at a hub. The sixth is the document risk: a transhipment has more parties, and a mismatch can stop the box at the connection. Ask for the contingency plan in writing.

Free time is not the same at every port. A transhipment can add a week at the hub, and the destination free time may start only when the box arrives. If the consignee needs two weeks to clear, a sailing with seven free days is a false economy. Ask for the free time in writing and add the storage cost to the comparison.

Put the same cargo, the same origin, the same destination and the same sailing window in front of both quotes. Ask for the vessel, the routing, the connection port, the connection time and the free time. If the quote is direct, ask whether a feeder is included. If it is transhipped, ask which hub and what happens if the connection is missed.

Then compare the total delivered cost, not the ocean line. Add origin charges, destination charges, duty, VAT, inland trucking, insurance and the cost of one extra week. If the direct quote is higher but arrives a week earlier and avoids a hub, it may be the better product. If the transhipment is cheaper and the cargo can wait, it may be the better total.

Write down the cargo-ready date, the delivery date, the cargo value, the free time and whether the cargo is DG. Then ask for the next two sailings, one direct and one transhipment if both exist. Compare the arrival window, the connection port and the total cost. Do not choose on the label or the ocean line alone.

If the cargo is time-sensitive or high-value, start with direct and only move to transhipment if the direct option is unavailable or clearly worse. If the cargo is flexible, compare the total and the connection risk. If the destination is Port Sudan, assume a connection and plan for the extra week.

Ask for the routing in writing: vessel, connection port, connection time and the next sailing if the connection is missed. A verbal “direct” or “fast” is not a routing. If the forwarder cannot name the connection, the quote is not complete. That is the minimum for a comparison. A written routing is part of the quote, not an optional extra.
Written routing: vessel, hub and missed-connection plan.
Ask for it before you pay.
Q: Is a direct sailing always faster?

A: No. A direct sailing can be delayed, full or omit a port, while a clean transhipment can arrive earlier. Compare the actual arrival window, not the label. Ask for the vessel, the ETD and the connection if the quote is not direct.
Q: Is transhipment always cheaper?

A: No. The ocean line may be lower, but the extra handover can add destination charges, storage and a longer free-time risk. A cheap transhipment with a missed connection can cost more than a direct sailing. Compare the total delivered cost.
Q: Which is better for dangerous goods?

A: It depends on the carrier and the hub. A direct sailing has fewer handovers, which is usually simpler for DG, but the direct vessel may not accept the class. A transhipment needs the hub to accept it too. Ask both carriers and confirm the routing in writing.

documents.title: 直航还是中转：红海出货怎么选？
documents.description: 直航和中转是两种产品。直航不一定更快，中转也不一定更便宜。要比衔接、免柜期和总成本。
documents.lead: 直航和中转是两种产品。直航不一定更快，中转也不一定更便宜。要比衔接、免柜期和总成本。

richText.text: 直航是同一艘船把柜子从中国起运港运到红海目的港。中转是第一艘船先运到枢纽，再换第二艘船到目的港。枢纽可能是吉达、杰贝阿里、吉布提、科伦坡、新加坡或其他港口。衔接是柜子在枢纽等待的时间，也是航程的一部分。
支线不等同于中转，但对货主的影响一样：多一次交接。支线可能把柜子从宁波驳到上海，或从青岛驳到更大的装货港，再上海洋船。问报价含的是支线、中转，还是两者都有。每次交接都有截点和责任空档。
货急、价值高、易碎或属于危险品，直航赢。交接少，延误、单证不一致或货损的机会就少。目的港免柜期短，直航也赢：中转可能在枢纽先吃掉几天，柜子还没到。项目货或生产线用料，简单的航线往往值更高的海运费。
直航不是保证。直航船也可能晚、满舱或跳港，直航报价也可能含起运港支线。问清报价里的“直航”是什么意思：从指定起运港到指定目的港一条船，还是支线加一条海洋船。报价说不出船名和航线，这个标签就不可靠。
时效紧或高价值货：交接少。
危险品：确认直航船接受该类别。
免柜期短：直航避免枢纽等待。
项目货：一条船更好控制。
没有直航舱位、直航太贵，或者目的港直航挂靠少，中转就赢。苏丹港最典型：中国直航舱位有限，很多货经吉达、杰贝阿里或吉布提衔接。目的港直航服务很小，中转也可能是唯一走法。
中转的海运费可能更低，但省下的钱不是自动的。多一次交接会增加目的港费用、第二套单证和更长的免柜期风险。货期灵活、衔接顺，总成本可能更低。衔接紧或枢纽堵，省下的钱会在仓储和滞箱里消失。
出运窗口没有直航舱位。
目的港直航少，例如苏丹港。
货期灵活，衔接顺。
海运费更低，且经得起总成本核算。
第一项容易漏的是衔接等待。报价写 30 天，柜子可能在枢纽等一周才上第二艘船。第二项是目的港费用：中转可能在枢纽或目的港多出操作、单证和提货单。第三项是免柜期：可能从卸船算，衔接在收货人清关前就用掉了。
第四项是错过衔接的成本。第一程晚了，仓储、改配和新运费谁付？第五项是保险：枢纽段的承保可能不同。第六项是单证风险：中转参与方更多，一个不一致就可能在衔接点卡住。让货代把预案写下来。
每个港口的免柜期不一样。中转可能在枢纽多一周，目的港免柜期又要等柜子到了才算。收货人清关要两周，只给 7 天免柜的船就是假便宜。让货代书面写清免柜期，并把仓储成本加进比较。
两份报价用同一票货、同一启运港、同一目的港、同一出运窗口。问船名、航线、中转港、衔接时间和免柜期。直航要问含不含支线；中转要问哪个枢纽、错过衔接怎么办。
然后比到门总成本，不是比海运费。加起运港费用、目的港费用、关税、增值税、内陆拖车、保险和多一周的成本。直航贵一点，但早到一周、少一个枢纽，可能是更好的产品。中转便宜、货又能等，可能是更好的总成本。
写下备货日期、交期、货值、免柜期，以及货是否危险品。然后问最近两班船，直航和中转各一份（如果都有）。比到货窗口、中转港和总成本。不要只看标签或海运费。
货急或价值高，先看直航；直航没有或明显更差，再看中转。货期灵活，就比总成本和衔接风险。目的港是苏丹港，就按有衔接来做计划，并留出多一周的余量。
让货代书面写航线：船名、中转港、衔接时间，以及错过衔接后的下一班船。口头说“直航”或“快”，不是航线。货代说不出中转港，报价就不完整。这是比较的最低要求。书面航线不是可选项，是报价的一部分，必须写清楚。
书面航线：船名、枢纽和错过衔接预案。
付款前就要这份书面航线。
问：直航一定更快吗？
答：不一定。直航可能延误、满舱或跳港，衔接顺的中转反而更早到。比实际到货窗口，不要只看标签。问船名、ETD，中转还要问衔接。
问：中转一定更便宜吗？
答：不一定。海运费可能低，但多一次交接会增加目的港费用、仓储和免柜期风险。中转便宜、却错过衔接，可能比直航更贵。要比到门总成本。
问：危险品选哪种？
答：看船公司和枢纽。直航交接少，通常对危险品更简单，但直航船不一定接受该类别。中转还要枢纽接受。两家船公司都要问，航线要书面确认。

documents.title: How RedSeaRate builds its rate index
documents.description: How RedSeaRate collects China–Red Sea 40HQ quotes, builds the 28-day median, removes outliers and what the index leaves out.
documents.lead: The index is a dated market reading, not a bookable price. This page explains what is measured, how the median is built, and what the number leaves out.

richText.text: RedSeaRate publishes 40HQ port-to-port ocean freight readings for five Red Sea destinations: Jeddah, Sokhna, Aqaba, Djibouti and Port Sudan. The reading is a median of market quotes collected from China origins, not a carrier's published tariff and not a quote we can book on the date shown.

Each destination has its own sample. A port with a large sample and a port with a thin sample are not equally reliable, even when both show a median. The sample count is part of the reading, not a footnote. When the sample is too thin, we show no median rather than a number that looks more precise than it is.

We use quotes collected in the last 28 days. The window is deliberately longer than a week so a quiet week does not erase the market level, and short enough that an old rate does not set the current reading. The median is the middle value of the sample after outliers are removed.
Container: 40HQ, the common equipment for light cargo on this trade.
Window: the last 28 days, counted in Shanghai time.
Outliers: quotes far outside the sample are removed before the median.
Sample: the number of quotes behind the median is shown with the figure.
Origins: quotes can come from Shanghai, Ningbo, Shenzhen, Qingdao, Nansha and other collected origins.

The median is not weighted by volume. A single large shipper and a single small shipper count as one quote each. That keeps the method simple and reproducible, but it means the reading describes the quote sample, not the whole market.

The reading is port-to-port ocean freight only. It does not include origin charges in China, destination port charges, customs clearance, duty, VAT, insurance, inland trucking or the cost of a missed connection. Those lines can change the delivered cost by more than the difference between two ocean quotes.
Origin: terminal handling, documentation, export declaration and trucking.
Destination: port dues, terminal handling, delivery order and broker.
Import: duty, VAT, inspection and any product approval.
Inland: trucking, rail, dry-port handling and empty return.
Risk: war-risk surcharge, storage, demurrage and detention.

body.text: Why some ports show no median

richText.text: A port may show “no recent quotes” or “sample too thin” instead of a median. That is a data statement, not a missing page. It usually means the quote window did not contain enough comparable 40HQ market quotes, or the quotes that arrived were too dispersed to summarise. Ask for a quote on the specific sailing instead of reading a thin sample as a price.
The same rule applies to the week-on-week figure. A change built on a small sample is a reading, not a trend. The market brief shows the sample count next to every move for that reason.

Use the index to see the level, the direction and the sample size. Then ask for a quote on your actual cargo, origin, destination and date. A bookable quote should name the sailing, the routing, the container, the free time, the surcharges and the validity. If a quote cannot name those lines, it is not comparable with the index or with another quote.

The index is not a forecast. A weekly move can reverse, and a route can change its direct/transhipment mix without changing the median. If the cargo is time-sensitive, compare the arrival window and the connection, not only the ocean line.

If a figure looks wrong, send the page URL, the date and the quote or source you are checking. We will review the sample and correct the page if needed. For a shipment, use the estimate form or contact the team on WeChat or WhatsApp; a message does not reserve space until we confirm the sailing and price.

documents.title: 红海运价指数的方法与边界
documents.description: 红海运价指数如何收集中国至红海 40HQ 报价、计算近 28 天中位数、剔除离群值，以及这些数字不包含什么。
documents.lead: 这个指数是有日期的市场读数，不是可订舱价格。本页说明我们衡量什么、中位数怎么算，以及这个数字不包含什么。

richText.text: RedSeaRate 发布五个红海目的港的 40HQ 港到港海运费读数：吉达、苏赫纳、亚喀巴、吉布提和苏丹港。这个读数是收集到的中国市场报价的中位数，不是船公司的公开运价表，也不是标注日期当天一定能订到的价格。
每个目的港有自己的样本。样本大的港口和样本小的港口，哪怕都显示中位数，可靠程度也不同。样本量是读数的一部分，不是脚注。样本太薄时，我们宁可不给中位数，也不给一个看起来比实际更精确的数字。
我们使用近 28 天收集的报价。窗口比一周长，是为了避免某一周成交少就把市场水平抹掉；又不会太长，避免旧价格决定当前读数。中位数是剔除离群值后样本的中间值。
柜型：40HQ，这条航线上轻货的常用柜型。
窗口：近 28 天，按上海时间计算。
离群值：明显偏离样本的报价在中位数计算前剔除。
样本：中位数旁边显示背后的报价条数。
起运港：报价可能来自上海、宁波、深圳、青岛、南沙及其他收集到的起运港。
中位数不按货量加权。一个大货主和一个小货主，各算一条报价。这样方法简单、可复现，但也意味着这个读数描述的是报价样本，不是整个市场。
这个读数只含港到港海运费。不含中国起运港费用、目的港费用、清关、关税、增值税、保险、内陆拖车，也不含错过衔接的成本。这些项目对到门成本的影响，可能比两份海运费之间的差额更大。
起运港：码头操作、单证、出口申报和拖车。
目的港：港务费、码头操作、提货单和报关行。
进口：关税、增值税、查验和产品批准。
内陆：拖车、铁路、陆港操作和空柜返还。
风险：战争风险附加费、仓储、滞港和滞箱。

body.text: 为什么有些港口没有中位数

richText.text: 有些港口会显示“近期无报价”或“样本不足”，而不是中位数。这是数据说明，不是页面缺失。通常意味着窗口内没有足够可比的 40HQ 市场报价，或者报价太分散、无法汇总。按具体船期询价，不要把薄样本当成价格。
周环比也用同一规则。小样本上的变动是读数，不是趋势。市场周报在每一个涨跌旁边都列出样本量，就是这个原因。
用指数看水平、方向和样本量，再按你的实际货物、起运港、目的港和日期询价。可订舱报价应写清船期、航线、柜型、免柜期、附加费和有效期。报价写不清这些，就无法和指数或另一份报价比较。
指数不是预测。周环比可能反转，航线也可能在中位数不变的情况下改变直航/中转比例。货急，要比到货窗口和衔接，不要只比海运费。
如果某个数字看起来不对，把页面 URL、日期和你在核对的报价或来源发给我们。我们会检查样本，必要时更正页面。要走出运，用估价表或通过微信、WhatsApp 联系团队；我们确认船期和价格前，消息不代表舱位已留。
